XREF-TARGET.name: XrefTarget
XREF-TARGET.description: note:This element specifies a reference target which can be scattered throughout the text. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="XrefTarget" stereotype:atpObject

0.name: AR-PACKAGE
0.description:
note:AUTOSAR package, allowing to create top level packages to structure the contained ARElements.

ARPackages are open sets. This means that in a file based description system multiple files can be used to partially describe the contents of a package.

This is an extended version of MSR's SW-SYSTEM. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ARPackage" stereotype:atpObject

1.name: AUTOSAR
1.description: note:Root element of an AUTOSAR description, also the root element in corresponding XML documents. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AUTOSAR";xml.globalElement="true" stereotype:atpObject

3.name: ACL-OBJECT-SET
3.description:
note:This meta class represents the ability to denote a set of objects for which roles and rights (access control lists) shall be defined. It basically can define the objects based on

* the nature of objects
* the involved blueprints
* the artifact in which the objects are serialized
* the definition of the object (in a definition - value pattern)
* individual reference objects tag:atp.recommendedPackage="AclObjectSets";mmt.qualifiedName="AclObjectSet" stereotype:atpObject

4.name: ACL-OPERATION
4.description: note:This meta class represents the ability to denote a particular operation which may be performed on objects in an AUTOSAR model. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="AclOperations";mmt.qualifiedName="AclOperation" stereotype:atpObject

5.name: ACL-PERMISSION
5.description: note:This meta class represents the ability to represent permissions granted on objects in an AUTOSAR model. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="AclPermissions";mmt.qualifiedName="AclPermission" stereotype:atpObject

6.name: ACL-ROLE
6.description: note:This meta class represents the ability to specify a particular role which is used to grant access rights to AUTOSAR model. The purpose of this meta-class is to support the mutual agreements between the involved parties. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="AclRoles";mmt.qualifiedName="AclRole" stereotype:atpObject

7.name: ADMIN-DATA
7.description:
note:AdminData represents the ability to express administrative information for an element. This administration information is to be treated as meta-data such as revision id or state of the file. There are basically four kinds of meta-data

* The language and/or used languages.

* Revision information covering e.g. revision number, state, release date, changes. Note that this information can be given in general as well as related to a particular company.

* Document meta-data specific for a company tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AdminData" stereotype:atpObject

8.name: AGE-CONSTRAINT
8.description:
note:The AgeConstraint is used to impose a constraint on an Timing Description Event referenced by the scope.

A minimum and a maximum age can be specified. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AgeConstraint" stereotype:atpObject

9.name: ALIAS-NAME-ASSIGNMENT
9.description:
note:This meta-class represents the ability to associate an alternative name to a flat representations or an Identifiable.

The usage of this name is defined outside of AUTOSAR. For example this name can be used by MCD tools or as a name for component instances in the ECU extract.

Note that flatInstance and identifiable are mutually exclusive. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AliasNameAssignment" stereotype:atpObject

10.name: ALIAS-NAME-SET
10.description:
note:This meta-class represents a set of AliasNames. The AliasNameSet can for example be an input to the A2L-Generator. It shall not be used by the RTE generator to generate the MC-Support.

In a given instance of AliasNameSet in the bound system there must be at most one aliasName per FlatInstanceDescriptor. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="AliasNameSets";mmt.qualifiedName="AliasNameSet" stereotype:atpObject

11.name: ANALYZED-EXECUTION-TIME
11.description: note:AnalyzedExecutionTime provides an analytic method for specifying the best and worst case execution time. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AnalyzedExecutionTime" stereotype:atpObject

12.name: ANNOTATION
12.description: note:This is a plain annotation which does not have further formal data. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Annotation" stereotype:atpObject

13.name: ANY-INSTANCE-REF
13.description: note:Describes a reference to any instance in an AUTOSAR model. This is the most generic form of an instance ref. Refer to the superclass notes for more details. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AnyInstanceRef" stereotype:atpObject,instanceRef

14.name: APPLICATION-ARRAY-DATA-TYPE
14.description: note:An application data type which is an array, each element is of the same application data type. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ApplicationDataTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationArrayDataType" stereotype:atpObject

15.name: APPLICATION-ARRAY-ELEMENT
15.description: note:Describes the properties of the elements of an application array data type. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationArrayElement" stereotype:atpObject

16.name: APPLICATION-COMPOSITE-DATA-TYPE-SUB-ELEMENT-REF
16.description: note:This meta-class represents the specialization of SubElementMapping with respect to ApplicationCompositeDataTypes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationCompositeDataTypeSubElementRef" stereotype:atpObject

18.name: APPLICATION-ENDPOINT
18.description: note:An application endpoint is the endpoint on an Ecu in terms of application addressing (e.g. socket). The application endpoint represents e.g. the listen socket in client-server-based communication. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationEndpoint" stereotype:atpObject

19.name: APPLICATION-ENTRY
19.description: note:Schedule table entry for application messages. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationEntry" stereotype:atpObject

20.name: APPLICATION-ERROR
20.description: note:This is a user-defined error that is associated with an element of an AUTOSAR interface. It is specific for the particular functionality or service provided by the AUTOSAR software component. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationError" stereotype:atpObject

21.name: APPLICATION-ERROR-MAPPING
21.description:
note:In client server communication, the server may return any value within the application error range.

The ApplicationError is mapped to the responseGroup. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationErrorMapping" stereotype:atpObject

22.name: APPLICATION-PRIMITIVE-DATA-TYPE
22.description: note:A primitive data type defines a set of allowed values. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ApplicationDataTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationPrimitiveDataType" stereotype:atpObject

23.name: APPLICATION-RECORD-DATA-TYPE
23.description: note:An application data type which can be decomposed into prototypes of other application data types. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ApplicationDataTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationRecordDataType" stereotype:atpObject

24.name: APPLICATION-RECORD-ELEMENT
24.description: note:Describes the properties of one particular element of an application record data type. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationRecordElement" stereotype:atpObject

25.name: APPLICATION-RULE-BASED-VALUE-SPECIFICATION
25.description: note:This meta-class represents rule based values for DataPrototypes typed by ApplicationDataTypes (ApplicationArrayDataType or a compound ApplicationPrimitiveDataType which also boils down to an array-nature). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationRuleBasedValueSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

26.name: APPLICATION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE
26.description: note:The ApplicationSwComponentType is used to represent the application software. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwComponentTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationSwComponentType" stereotype:atpObject

27.name: APPLICATION-VALUE-SPECIFICATION
27.description:
note:This meta-class represents values for DataPrototypes typed by ApplicationDataTypes (this includes in particular compound primitives). 

For further details refer to ASAM CDF 2.0. This meta-class corresponds to some extent with SW-INSTANCE in ASAM CDF 2.0. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ApplicationValueSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

28.name: AR-VARIABLE-IN-IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-INSTANCE-REF
28.description:
note:This class represents the ability to navigate into a data element inside of an VariableDataPrototype which is typed  by an ImplementationDatatype.

Note that it shall not be used if the target is the VariableDataPrototype itself (e.g. if its a primitive).

Note that this class follows the pattern of an InstanceRef but is not implemented based on the abstract classes because the ImplementationDataType isn't either, especially because ImplementationDataTypeElement isn't derived from AtpPrototype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ArVariableInImplementationDataInstanceRef" stereotype:atpObject

29.name: ARBITRARY-EVENT-TRIGGERING
29.description:
note:The ArbitraryEventTriggering describes that an event occurs occasionally, singly, irregularly or randomly.

The primary purpose of this event triggering is to abstract event occurrences captured by data acquisition tools (background debugger, trace analyzer, etc.) during system runtime. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ArbitraryEventTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

30.name: AREA
30.description:
note:This element specifies a region in an image map. Image maps enable authors to specify regions in an object (e.g. a graphic) and to assign a specific activity to each region (e.g. load a document, launch a program etc.).

For more details refer to the specification of HTML. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Area" stereotype:atpObject

31.name: ARGUMENT-DATA-PROTOTYPE
31.description: note:An argument of an operation, much like a data element, but also carries direction information and is owned by a particular ClientServerOperation. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ArgumentDataPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

32.name: ARRAY-VALUE-SPECIFICATION
32.description: note:Specifies the values for an array. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ArrayValueSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

33.name: ASSEMBLY-SW-CONNECTOR
33.description: note:AssemblySwConnectors are exclusively used to connect SwComponentPrototypes in the context of a CompositionSwComponentType. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AssemblySwConnector" stereotype:atpObject

34.name: ASSIGN-FRAME-ID
34.description: note:Schedule entry for an  Assign Frame Id master request. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AssignFrameId" stereotype:atpObject

35.name: ASSIGN-FRAME-ID-RANGE
35.description: note:AssignFrameIdRange generates an assign frame PID range request. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AssignFrameIdRange" stereotype:atpObject

36.name: ASSIGN-NAD
36.description: note:Schedule entry for an Assign NAD master request. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AssignNad" stereotype:atpObject

37.name: ASYNCHRONOUS-SERVER-CALL-POINT
37.description:
note:An AsynchronousServerCallPoint is used for asynchronous invocation of a ClientServerOperation.
IMPORTANT: a ServerCallPoint cannot be used concurrently. Once the client RunnableEntity has made the invocation, the ServerCallPoint cannot be used until the call returns (or an error occurs!) at which point the ServerCallPoint becomes available again. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AsynchronousServerCallPoint" stereotype:atpObject

38.name: ASYNCHRONOUS-SERVER-CALL-RESULT-POINT
38.description:
note:If a RunnableEntity owns a AsynchronousServerCallResultPoint it is entitled to get the result of the referenced AsynchronousServerCallPoint.
If it is associated with AsynchronousServerCallReturnsEvent, this RTEEvent notifies the completion of the required ClientServerOperation or a timeout. The occurrence of this event can either unblock a WaitPoint or can lead to the invocation of a RunnableEntity. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AsynchronousServerCallResultPoint" stereotype:atpObject

39.name: ASYNCHRONOUS-SERVER-CALL-RETURNS-EVENT
39.description: note:This event is raised when an asynchronous server call is finished. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AsynchronousServerCallReturnsEvent" stereotype:atpObject

40.name: AUTOSAR-DATA-TYPE-REF-CONDITIONAL
40.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AutosarDataType" stereotype:atpObject

41.name: AUTOSAR-ENGINEERING-OBJECT
41.description: note:This denotes an engineering object being part of the process. It is a specialization of the abstract class EngineeringObject for usage within AUTOSAR. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AutosarEngineeringObject" stereotype:atpObject

42.name: AUTOSAR-OPERATION-ARGUMENT-INSTANCE
42.description:
note:This class represents a reference to an argument instance. This way it is possible to reference an argument instance in the occurrence expression formula. The argument instance can target to one of the following arguments:

* a whole argument used in an operation of a PortPrototype with ClientServerInterface

* an element inside of a composite argument used in an operation of a PortPrototype with ClientServerInterface tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AutosarOperationArgumentInstance" stereotype:atpObject

43.name: AUTOSAR-PARAMETER-REF
43.description:
note:This class represents a reference to a parameter within AUTOSAR which can be one of the following use cases:

localParameter:

* localParameter which is used as whole (e.g.  sharedAxis for curve)

autosarVariable:

* a parameter provided via PortPrototype which is used as whole (e.g. parameterAccess)

* an element inside of a composite local parameter typed by ApplicationDatatype (e.g. sharedAxis for a curve)

* an element inside of a composite parameter provided via Port and typed by ApplicationDatatype (e.g. sharedAxis for a curve)

autosarParameterInImplDatatype:

* an element inside of a composite local parameter typed by ImplementationDatatype

* an element inside of a composite parameter provided via PortPrototype and typed by ImplementationDatatype tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AutosarParameterRef" stereotype:atpObject

44.name: AUTOSAR-VARIABLE-INSTANCE
44.description:
note:This class represents a reference to a variable instance within AUTOSAR. This way it is possible to reference a variable instance in the occurrence expression formula. The variable instance can target to one of the following variables:

* a variable provided via a PortPrototype as whole

* an element inside of a composite variable provided via a PortPrototype tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AutosarVariableInstance" stereotype:atpObject

45.name: AUTOSAR-VARIABLE-REF
45.description:
note:This class represents a reference to a variable within AUTOSAR which can be one of the following use cases:

localVariable:

* localVariable which is used as whole (e.g. InterRunnableVariable, inputValue for curve)

autosarVariable:

* a variable provided via Port which is used as whole (e.g. dataAccesspoints)

* an element inside of a composite local variable typed by ApplicationDatatype (e.g. inputValue for a curve)

* an element inside of a composite variable provided via Port and typed by ApplicationDatatype (e.g. inputValue for a curve)

autosarVariableInImplDatatype:

* an element inside of a composite local variable typed by ImplementationDatatype  (e.g. nvramData mapping)

* an element inside of a composite variable provided via Port and typed by ImplementationDatatype (e.g. inputValue for a curve) tag:mmt.qualifiedName="AutosarVariableRef" stereotype:atpObject

46.name: BACKGROUND-EVENT
46.description: note:This event is used to trigger RunnableEntities that are supposed to be executed in the background. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BackgroundEvent" stereotype:atpObject

47.name: BASE-TYPE-DIRECT-DEFINITION
47.description: note:This BaseType is defined directly (as opposite to a derived BaseType) tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BaseTypeDirectDefinition" stereotype:atpObject

48.name: BLUEPRINT-FORMULA
48.description: note:This class express the extension of the Formula Language to provide formalized blueprint-Value resp. blueprintCondition. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BlueprintFormula" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

49.name: BLUEPRINT-MAPPING
49.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to map two an object and its blueprint. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BlueprintMapping" stereotype:atpObject

50.name: BLUEPRINT-MAPPING-SET
50.description: note:This represents a container of mappings between "actual" model elements and the "blueprint" that has been taken for their creation. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="BlueprintMappingSets";mmt.qualifiedName="BlueprintMappingSet" stereotype:atpObject

51.name: BLUEPRINT-POLICY-LIST
51.description: note:The class represents that the related attribute is modifiable during the blueprinting. It applies only to attribute with upper multiplicity greater than 1. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BlueprintPolicyList" stereotype:atpObject

52.name: BLUEPRINT-POLICY-NOT-MODIFIABLE
52.description: note:The class represents that the related attribute is not modifiable during the blueprinting. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BlueprintPolicyNotModifiable" stereotype:atpObject

53.name: BLUEPRINT-POLICY-SINGLE
53.description: note:The class represents that the related attribute is modifiable during the blueprinting. It applies only to attribute with upper multiplicity equal 1. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BlueprintPolicySingle" stereotype:atpObject

54.name: BOOLEAN-VALUE-VARIATION-POINT
54.description:
note:This class represents an attribute value variation point for Boolean attributes.

Note that this class might be used in the extended meta-model on tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BooleanValueVariationPoint" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

55.name: BR
55.description: note:This element is the same as function here as in a HTML document i.e. it forces a line break. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Br" stereotype:atpObject

56.name: BSW-ASYNCHRONOUS-SERVER-CALL-POINT
56.description: note:Represents an asynchronous procedure call point via the BSW Scheduler. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswAsynchronousServerCallPoint" stereotype:atpObject

57.name: BSW-ASYNCHRONOUS-SERVER-CALL-RESULT-POINT
57.description: note:The callback point for an BswAsynchronousServerCallPoint i.e. the point at which the result can be retrieved from the BSW Scheduler. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswAsynchronousServerCallResultPoint" stereotype:atpObject

58.name: BSW-ASYNCHRONOUS-SERVER-CALL-RETURNS-EVENT
58.description:
note:This is the "callback" event for asynchronous Client-Server-Communication via the BSW Scheduler which is thrown after completion of the asynchronous Client-Server call.

Its eventSource specifies the call point to be used for retrieving the result. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswAsynchronousServerCallReturnsEvent" stereotype:atpObject

59.name: BSW-BACKGROUND-EVENT
59.description: note:A recurring BswEvent which is used to perform background activities. It is similar to a BswTimingEvent but has no fixed time period and is activated only with low priority. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswBackgroundEvent" stereotype:atpObject

60.name: BSW-CALLED-ENTITY
60.description: note:BSW module entity which is designed to be called from another BSW module or cluster. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswCalledEntity" stereotype:atpObject

61.name: BSW-CLIENT-POLICY
61.description: note:The requiredClientServerEntry for which the BSW Scheduler using this policy. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswClientPolicy" stereotype:atpObject

62.name: BSW-DATA-RECEIVED-EVENT
62.description: note:This event is thrown on reception of the referenced data via Sender-Receiver-Communication over the BSW Scheduler. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswDataReceivedEvent" stereotype:atpObject

63.name: BSW-DATA-SEND-POLICY
63.description: note:The data sent over the BSW Scheduler using this policy. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswDataSendPolicy" stereotype:atpObject

64.name: BSW-DEBUG-INFO
64.description: note:Collects the information on the data provided to the AUTOSAR debug module. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswDebugInfo" stereotype:atpObject

65.name: BSW-DIRECT-CALL-POINT
65.description:
note:Represents a concrete point in the code from where a BswModuleEntry is called directly, i.e. not via the BSW Scheduler. 

This information can be used to analyze call tree and resource locking scenarios. It is not needed to configure the BSW Scheduler. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswDirectCallPoint" stereotype:atpObject

66.name: BSW-DISTINGUISHED-PARTITION
66.description:
note:Each instance of this meta-class represents an abstract partition in which context the code of the enclosing  BswModuleBehavior can be executed.

The intended use case is to distinguish between several partitions in order to implement different behavior per partition, for example to behave either as a master or satellite in a multicore ECU with shared BSW code. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswDistinguishedPartition" stereotype:atpObject

67.name: BSW-EXCLUSIVE-AREA-POLICY
67.description: note:The ExclusiveArea for which the BSW Scheduler using this policy. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswExclusiveAreaPolicy" stereotype:atpObject

68.name: BSW-EXTERNAL-TRIGGER-OCCURRED-EVENT
68.description: note:A BswEvent resulting from a trigger released by another module or cluster. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswExternalTriggerOccurredEvent" stereotype:atpObject

69.name: BSW-IMPLEMENTATION
69.description:
note:Contains the implementation specific information in addition to the generic specification (BswModuleDescription and BswBehavior).
It is possible to have several different BswImplementations referring to the same BswBehavior. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="BswImplementations";mmt.qualifiedName="BswImplementation" stereotype:atpObject

70.name: BSW-INTERNAL-BEHAVIOR
70.description:
note:Specifies the behavior of a BSW module or a BSW cluster w.r.t. the code entities visible by the BSW Scheduler.
It is possible to have several different BswInternalBehaviors referring to the same BswModuleDescription. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswInternalBehavior" stereotype:atpObject

71.name: BSW-INTERNAL-TRIGGER-OCCURRED-EVENT
71.description: note:A BswEvent, which can happen sporadically. The event is activated by explicit calls from the module to the BSW Scheduler. The main purpose for such an event is to cause a context switch, e.g. from an ISR context into a task context. Activation and switching are handled within the same module or cluster only. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswInternalTriggerOccurredEvent" stereotype:atpObject

72.name: BSW-INTERNAL-TRIGGERING-POINT
72.description: note:Represents the activation point for one or more BswInternalTriggerOccurredEvents. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswInternalTriggeringPoint" stereotype:atpObject

74.name: BSW-INTERNAL-TRIGGERING-POINT-REF-CONDITIONAL
74.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswInternalTriggeringPoint" stereotype:atpObject

75.name: BSW-INTERRUPT-ENTITY
75.description: note:BSW module entity, which is designed to be triggered by an interrupt. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswInterruptEntity" stereotype:atpObject

76.name: BSW-MGR-NEEDS
76.description: note:Specifies the abstract needs on the configuration of the Basic Software Manager for one "user". tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswMgrNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

77.name: BSW-MODE-MANAGER-ERROR-EVENT
77.description: note:This represents the ability to react on errors occurring during mode handling. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswModeManagerErrorEvent" stereotype:atpObject

78.name: BSW-MODE-RECEIVER-POLICY
78.description: note:Specifies the details for the reception of a mode switch for the referred mode group. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswModeReceiverPolicy" stereotype:atpObject

79.name: BSW-MODE-SENDER-POLICY
79.description: note:Specifies the details for the sending of a mode switch for the referred mode group. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswModeSenderPolicy" stereotype:atpObject

80.name: BSW-MODE-SWITCH-ACK-REQUEST
80.description: note:Requests acknowledgements that a mode switch has been processed  successfully tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswModeSwitchAckRequest" stereotype:atpObject

81.name: BSW-MODE-SWITCH-EVENT
81.description: note:A BswEvent resulting from a mode switch. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswModeSwitchEvent" stereotype:atpObject

82.name: BSW-MODE-SWITCHED-ACK-EVENT
82.description: note:The event is raised after a switch of the referenced mode group has been acknowledged or an error occurs. The referenced mode group must be provided by this module. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswModeSwitchedAckEvent" stereotype:atpObject

83.name: BSW-MODULE-CLIENT-SERVER-ENTRY
83.description:
note:This meta-class represents a single API entry into the BSW module or cluster that has the ability to be called in client-server fashion via the BSW Scheduler.

In this regard it is more special than BswModuleEntry and can be seen as a wrapper around the BswModuleEntry to which it refers (property encapsulatedEntry). tag:atp.recommendedPackage="BswModuleEntrys";mmt.qualifiedName="BswModuleClientServerEntry" stereotype:atpObject

84.name: BSW-MODULE-DEPENDENCY
84.description: note:This class collects the dependencies of a BSW module or cluster on a certain other BSW module. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswModuleDependency" stereotype:atpObject

85.name: BSW-MODULE-DESCRIPTION
85.description:
note:Root element for the description of a single BSW module or BSW cluster.
In case it describes a BSW module, the short name of this element equals the name of the BSW module. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="BswModuleDescriptions";mmt.qualifiedName="BswModuleDescription" stereotype:atpObject

86.name: BSW-MODULE-DESCRIPTION-REF-CONDITIONAL
86.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswModuleDescription" stereotype:atpObject

87.name: BSW-MODULE-ENTRY
87.description:
note:This class represents a single API entry (C-function prototype) into the BSW module or cluster.

The name of the C-function is equal to the short name of this element with one exception: In case of multiple instances of a module on the same CPU, special rules for "infixes" apply, see description of class BswImplementation. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="BswModuleEntrys";mmt.qualifiedName="BswModuleEntry" stereotype:atpObject

88.name: BSW-MODULE-ENTRY-REF-CONDITIONAL
88.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswModuleEntry" stereotype:atpObject

89.name: BSW-MODULE-TIMING
89.description:
note:A model element used to define timing descriptions and constraints for the BswInternalBehavior of one BSW Module. Thereby, for each BswInternalBehavior a separate timing can be specified.

A constraint defined at this level holds true for all Implementations of that BswInternalBehavior.

TimingDescriptions aggregated by BswModuleTiming are restricted to event chains referring to events which are derived from the class TDEventBswInternalBehavior. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="TimingExtensions";mmt.qualifiedName="BswModuleTiming" stereotype:atpObject

90.name: BSW-OPERATION-INVOKED-EVENT
90.description:
note:This event is thrown on operation invocation in Client-Server-Communication via the BSW Scheduler. Its "entry" reference provides the BswClientServerEntry that is called subsequently.

Note this event is not needed in case of direct function calls. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswOperationInvokedEvent" stereotype:atpObject

91.name: BSW-PARAMETER-POLICY
91.description: note:The perInstanceParameter for which the BSW Scheduler using this policy. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswParameterPolicy" stereotype:atpObject

93.name: BSW-QUEUED-DATA-RECEPTION-POLICY
93.description: note:Reception policy attributes specific for queued receiving. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswQueuedDataReceptionPolicy" stereotype:atpObject

94.name: BSW-RELEASED-TRIGGER-POLICY
94.description: note:The Trigger for which the BSW Scheduler using this policy. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswReleasedTriggerPolicy" stereotype:atpObject

95.name: BSW-SCHEDULABLE-ENTITY
95.description: note:BSW module entity, which is designed for control by the BSW Scheduler. It may for example implement a so-called "main" function. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswSchedulableEntity" stereotype:atpObject

96.name: BSW-SCHEDULER-NAME-PREFIX
96.description: note:A prefix to be used in names of generated code artifacts which make up the interface of a BSW module to the BswScheduler. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswSchedulerNamePrefix" stereotype:atpObject

97.name: BSW-SERVICE-DEPENDENCY
97.description: note:Specialization of ServiceDependency in the context of an BswInternalBehavior. It allows to associate BswModuleEntries and data defined for a BSW module or cluster to a given ServiceNeeds element. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswServiceDependency" stereotype:atpObject

98.name: BSW-SERVICE-DEPENDENCY-IDENT
98.description: note:This meta-class is created to add the ability to become the target of a reference to the non-Referrable BswServiceDependency. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswServiceDependencyIdent" stereotype:atpObject

99.name: BSW-SYNCHRONOUS-SERVER-CALL-POINT
99.description: note:Represents a synchronous procedure call point via the BSW Scheduler. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswSynchronousServerCallPoint" stereotype:atpObject

100.name: BSW-TIMING-EVENT
100.description: note:A recurring BswEvent driven by a time period. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswTimingEvent" stereotype:atpObject

101.name: BSW-TRIGGER-DIRECT-IMPLEMENTATION
101.description: note:Specifies a released trigger to be directly implemented via OS calls, for example in a Complex Driver module. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswTriggerDirectImplementation" stereotype:atpObject

102.name: BSW-VARIABLE-ACCESS
102.description:
note:The presence of a BswVariableAccess implies that a BswModuleEntity needs access to a VariableDataPrototype via the BSW Scheduler.

The kind of access is specified by the role in which the class is used. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BswVariableAccess" stereotype:atpObject

103.name: BUFFER-PROPERTIES
103.description: note:Configuration of the buffer properties the transformer needs to work. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BufferProperties" stereotype:atpObject

104.name: BUILD-ACTION
104.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify a build action. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BuildAction" stereotype:atpObject

105.name: BUILD-ACTION-ENVIRONMENT
105.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify a build action environment. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BuildActionEnvironment" stereotype:atpObject

106.name: BUILD-ACTION-INVOCATOR
106.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify the invocation of a task in a build action. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BuildActionInvocator" stereotype:atpObject

107.name: BUILD-ACTION-IO-ELEMENT
107.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify the input/output entities of a BuildAction. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BuildActionIoElement" stereotype:atpObject

108.name: BUILD-ACTION-MANIFEST
108.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify a manifest for processing artifacts. An example use case is the processing of ECUC parameter values. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="BuildActionManifests";mmt.qualifiedName="BuildActionManifest";xml.globalElement="false" stereotype:atpObject

109.name: BUILD-ACTION-MANIFEST-REF-CONDITIONAL
109.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BuildActionManifest" stereotype:atpObject

110.name: BUILD-ENGINEERING-OBJECT
110.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to denote an artifact which is processed within a particular build action. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BuildEngineeringObject" stereotype:atpObject

111.name: BURST-PATTERN-EVENT-TRIGGERING
111.description:
note:A BurstPatternEventTriggering describes the maximum number of occurrences of the same event in a given time interval.
This is typically used to model a worst case activation scenario. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="BurstPatternEventTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

112.name: C-IDENTIFIER
112.description: note:This datatype represents a string, that follows the rules of C-identifiers. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CIdentifier";xml.xsd.customType="C-IDENTIFIER";xml.xsd.pattern="[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*";xml.xsd.type="string" stereotype:atpObject,primitive

113.name: CALIBRATION-PARAMETER-VALUE
113.description:
note:Specifies instance specific calibration parameter values used to initialize the memory objects implementing calibration parameters in the generated RTE code.

RTE generator will use the implInitValue to override the initial values specified for the DataPrototypes of a component type. 

The applInitValue is used to exchange init values with the component vendor not publishing the transformation algorithm between ApplicationDataTypes and ImplementationDataTypes or defining a instance specific initialization of components which are only defined with ApplicationDataTypes.

Note: If both representations of init values are available these need to represent the same content.

Note further that in this case an explicit mapping of ValueSpecification is not implemented because calibration parameters are delivered back after the calibration phase. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CalibrationParameterValue" stereotype:atpObject

114.name: CALIBRATION-PARAMETER-VALUE-SET
114.description: note:Specification of a constant that can be part of a package, i.e. it can be defined stand-alone. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="CalibrationParameterValueSets";mmt.qualifiedName="CalibrationParameterValueSet" stereotype:atpObject

115.name: CAN-CLUSTER
115.description: note:CAN bus specific cluster attributes. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="CommunicationClusters";mmt.qualifiedName="CanCluster" stereotype:atpObject

116.name: CAN-CLUSTER-BUS-OFF-RECOVERY
116.description: note:This element contains the attributes that are used to configure the CAN bus off monitoring / recovery at system level. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanClusterBusOffRecovery" stereotype:atpObject

117.name: CAN-CLUSTER-CONDITIONAL
117.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanClusterConditional" stereotype:atpObject

118.name: CAN-COMMUNICATION-CONNECTOR
118.description: note:CAN bus specific communication connector attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanCommunicationConnector" stereotype:atpObject

119.name: CAN-COMMUNICATION-CONTROLLER
119.description: note:CAN bus specific communication port attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanCommunicationController" stereotype:atpObject

120.name: CAN-COMMUNICATION-CONTROLLER-CONDITIONAL
120.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanCommunicationControllerConditional" stereotype:atpObject

121.name: CAN-CONTROLLER-CONFIGURATION
121.description: note:This element is used for the specification of the exact CAN Bit Timing configuration parameter values. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanControllerConfiguration" stereotype:atpObject

122.name: CAN-CONTROLLER-CONFIGURATION-REQUIREMENTS
122.description: note:This element allows the specification of ranges for the CAN Bit Timing configuration parameters. These ranges are taken as requirements and have to be respected by the ECU developer. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanControllerConfigurationRequirements" stereotype:atpObject

123.name: CAN-CONTROLLER-FD-CONFIGURATION
123.description: note:Bit timing related configuration of a CAN controller for payload and CRC of a CAN FD frame. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanControllerFdConfiguration" stereotype:atpObject

124.name: CAN-CONTROLLER-FD-CONFIGURATION-REQUIREMENTS
124.description: note:This element allows the specification of ranges for the CanFD bit timing configuration parameters. These ranges are taken as requirements and shall be respected by the ECU developer. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanControllerFdConfigurationRequirements" stereotype:atpObject

125.name: CAN-FRAME
125.description: note:CAN specific Frame element. This element shall also be used for TTCan. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Frames";mmt.qualifiedName="CanFrame" stereotype:atpObject

126.name: CAN-FRAME-TRIGGERING
126.description: note:CAN specific attributes to the FrameTriggering tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanFrameTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

127.name: CAN-NM-CLUSTER
127.description: note:Can specific NmCluster attributes tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanNmCluster" stereotype:atpObject

128.name: CAN-NM-CLUSTER-COUPLING
128.description: note:CAN attributes that are valid for each of the referenced (coupled) CAN clusters. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanNmClusterCoupling" stereotype:atpObject

130.name: CAN-NM-NODE
130.description: note:CAN specific NM Node attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanNmNode" stereotype:atpObject

131.name: CAN-NM-RANGE-CONFIG
131.description:
note:Defines the CANID ranges that are used for Nm. This range definition is redundant to the attribute "rxIdentifierRange" of CanFrameTriggering. For backward compatibility reasons this redundancy shall be preserved and both shall be defined.
In future this element will be removed from the model. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="CanNmRangeConfig" stereotype:atpObject

132.name: CAN-PHYSICAL-CHANNEL
132.description: note:CAN bus specific physical channel attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanPhysicalChannel" stereotype:atpObject

133.name: CAN-TP-ADDRESS
133.description: note:An ECUs TP address on the referenced channel. This represents the diagnostic Address. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanTpAddress" stereotype:atpObject

134.name: CAN-TP-CHANNEL
134.description: note:Configuration parameters of the CanTp channel. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanTpChannel" stereotype:atpObject

135.name: CAN-TP-CONFIG
135.description:
note:This element defines exactly one CAN TP Configuration. 

One CanTpConfig element shall be created for each CAN Network in the System. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="TpConfigs";mmt.qualifiedName="CanTpConfig" stereotype:atpObject

136.name: CAN-TP-CONNECTION
136.description:
note:A connection identifies the sender and the receiver of this particular communication. The CanTp module routes a Pdu through this connection. 

atpVariation: Derived, because TpNode can vary. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanTpConnection" stereotype:atpObject

137.name: CAN-TP-ECU
137.description: note:ECU specific TP configuration parameters. Each TpEcu element has a reference to exactly one ECUInstance in the topology. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanTpEcu" stereotype:atpObject

138.name: CAN-TP-NODE
138.description: note:TP Node (Sender or Receiver) provides the TP Address and the connection to the Topology description. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CanTpNode" stereotype:atpObject

139.name: CAPTION
139.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a caption which is a title, and a shortName. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Caption" stereotype:atpObject

140.name: CHAPTER
140.description: note:This meta-class represents a chapter of a document. Chapters are the primary structuring element in documentation. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Chapter" stereotype:atpObject

141.name: CHAPTER-CONTENT
141.description: note:This class represents the content which is directly in a chapter. It is basically the same as the one in a Topic but might have additional complex structures (e.g. Synopsis) tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ChapterContent" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

142.name: CHAPTER-MODEL
142.description:
note:This is the basic content model of a chapter except the Chapter title. This can be utilized in general chapters as well as in predefined chapters.

A chapter has content on three levels:

1. chapter content

2. topics

3. subchapters tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ChapterModel" stereotype:atpObject

143.name: CHAPTER-OR-MSR-QUERY
143.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to denote a particular chapter or a query returning a chapter. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ChapterOrMsrQuery" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

144.name: CLIENT-COM-SPEC
144.description: note:Client-specific communication attributes (RPortPrototype typed by ClientServerInterface). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ClientComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

145.name: CLIENT-ID-DEFINITION
145.description:
note:Several clients in one client-ECU can communicate via inter-ECU client-server communication with a server on a different ECU, if a client identifier is used to distinguish the different clients.
The Client Identifier of the transaction handle that is used by the RTE can be defined by this element. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ClientIdDefinition" stereotype:atpObject

146.name: CLIENT-ID-DEFINITION-SET
146.description: note:Set of Client Identifiers that are used for inter-ECU client-server communication in the System. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ClientIdDefinitionSet" stereotype:atpObject

147.name: CLIENT-ID-MAPPING
147.description:
note:In case of a server on one ECU with multiple clients on other ECUs, the client server communication shall use different unique COM signals and signal groups for each client to allow the identification of the client associated with each system signal.

The ClientId is mapped to the requestGroup and to the responseGroup. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="ClientIdMapping" stereotype:atpObject

148.name: CLIENT-ID-RANGE
148.description: note:With this element it is possible to restrict the Client Identifier of the transaction handle that is generated by the client RTE for inter-Ecu Client/Server communication to an allowed range of numerical values. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ClientIdRange" stereotype:atpObject

149.name: CLIENT-SERVER-ANNOTATION
149.description: note:Annotation to a port regarding a certain Operation. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerAnnotation" stereotype:atpObject

150.name: CLIENT-SERVER-APPLICATION-ERROR-MAPPING
150.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to map ApplicationErrors onto each other. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerApplicationErrorMapping" stereotype:atpObject

151.name: CLIENT-SERVER-ARRAY-ELEMENT-MAPPING
151.description:
note:The ApplicationArrayElement may be a primitive one or a composite one. If the element is primitive, it will be mapped to the "SystemSignal" (multiplicity 1). If the ArgumentDataPrototype that is referenced by ClientServerCompositeTypeMapping is typed by an ApplicationDataType the reference to the ApplicationArrayElement shall be used. If the VariableDataPrototype is typed by the ImplementationDataType the reference to the ImplementationArrayElement shall be used. 

If the element is composite, there will be no mapping to the "SystemSignal" (multiplicity 0). In this case the "ArrayElementMapping" Element will aggregate the "TypeMapping" Element. In that way also the composite datatypes can be mapped to SystemSignals. 

Regardless whether composite or primitive array element is mapped the indexed array element always needs to be specified. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerArrayElementMapping" stereotype:atpObject

152.name: CLIENT-SERVER-ARRAY-TYPE-MAPPING
152.description: note:If the ApplicationCompositeDataType is an Array, the "ArrayTypeMapping" will be used. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerArrayTypeMapping" stereotype:atpObject

153.name: CLIENT-SERVER-INTERFACE
153.description: note:A client/server interface declares a number of operations that can be invoked on a server by a client. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PortInterfaces";mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerInterface" stereotype:atpObject

154.name: CLIENT-SERVER-INTERFACE-MAPPING
154.description: note:Defines the mapping of ClientServerOperations in context of two different ClientServerInterfaces. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerInterfaceMapping" stereotype:atpObject

155.name: CLIENT-SERVER-OPERATION
155.description: note:An operation declared within the scope of a client/server interface. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerOperation" stereotype:atpObject

156.name: CLIENT-SERVER-OPERATION-MAPPING
156.description: note:Defines the mapping of two particular ClientServerOperations in context of two different ClientServerInterfaces. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerOperationMapping" stereotype:atpObject

157.name: CLIENT-SERVER-PRIMITIVE-TYPE-MAPPING
157.description: note:Mapping of an argument with a primitive datatype to a signal. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerPrimitiveTypeMapping" stereotype:atpObject

158.name: CLIENT-SERVER-RECORD-ELEMENT-MAPPING
158.description:
note:Mapping of a primitive record element to a SystemSignal. If the ArgumentDataPrototype that is referenced by ClientServerCompositeTypeMapping is typed by an ApplicationDataType the reference to the ApplicationRecordElement shall be used. If the VariableDataPrototype is typed by the ImplementationDataType the reference to the ImplementationRecordElement shall be used. 

If the element is composite, there will be no mapping (multiplicity 0). In this case the "RecordElementMapping" Element will aggregate the "TypeMapping" Element. In that way also the composite datatypes can be mapped to SystemSignals. 

Regardless whether composite or primitive record element is mapped the record element always needs to be specified. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerRecordElementMapping" stereotype:atpObject

159.name: CLIENT-SERVER-RECORD-TYPE-MAPPING
159.description: note:If the ApplicationCompositeDataType is a Record, the "RecordTypeMapping" will be used. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerRecordTypeMapping" stereotype:atpObject

160.name: CLIENT-SERVER-TO-SIGNAL-GROUP-MAPPING
160.description:
note:This mapping is deprecated and will be removed in future. It is replaced by the ClientServerToSignalMapping.

Old description:
Mapping of client server operation arguments to signals of a signal group. Arguments with a primitive datatype will be mapped via the "ClientServerPrimitiveTypeMapping" element. 
Arguments with composite datatypes will be mapped via the "CompositeTypeMapping" element. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerToSignalGroupMapping" stereotype:atpObject

161.name: CLIENT-SERVER-TO-SIGNAL-MAPPING
161.description: note:This element maps the ClientServerOperation to call- and return-SystemSignals. The serialization is defined by the referenced SerializationTechnology. tag:atp.Status="draft";mmt.qualifiedName="ClientServerToSignalMapping" stereotype:atpObject

162.name: CODE
162.description: note:A generic code descriptor. The type of the code (source or object) is defined via the category attribute of the associated engineering object. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Code" stereotype:atpObject

163.name: COLLECTION
163.description:
note:This meta-class specifies a collection of elements. A collection can be utilized to express additional aspects for a set of elements. 

Note that Collection is an ARElement. Therefore it is applicable e.g. for EvaluatedVariant, even if this is not obvious.

Usually the category of a Collection is "SET". On the other hand, a Collection can also express an arbitrary relationship between elements. This is denoted by the category "RELATION" (see also [TPS_GST_00347]). 

In this case the collection represents an association from "sourceElement" to "targetElement" in the role "role". tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Collections";mmt.qualifiedName="Collection" stereotype:atpObject

164.name: COLSPEC
164.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify the properties of a column in a  table. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Colspec" stereotype:atpObject

165.name: COM-MGR-USER-NEEDS
165.description: note:Specifies the abstract needs on the configuration of the Communication Manager for one "user". tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ComMgrUserNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

166.name: COMMON-SIGNAL-PATH
166.description: note:The CommonSignalPath describes that two or more SwcToSwcSignals and/or SwcToSwcOperationArguments must take the same way (Signal Path) in the topology. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CommonSignalPath" stereotype:atpObject

167.name: COMMUNICATION-CONNECTOR-REF-CONDITIONAL
167.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CommunicationConnector" stereotype:atpObject

168.name: COMMUNICATION-CONTROLLER-MAPPING
168.description:
note:CommunicationControllerMapping specifies the CommunicationPeripheral
hardware (defined in the ECU Resource Template) to realize the specified CommunicationController in a physical topology. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CommunicationControllerMapping" stereotype:atpObject

169.name: COMPILER
169.description: note:Specifies the compiler attributes. In case of source code this specifies requirements how the compiler shall be invoked. In case of object code this documents the used compiler settings. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Compiler" stereotype:atpObject

170.name: COMPLEX-DEVICE-DRIVER-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE
170.description: note:The ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType is a special AtomicSwComponentType that has direct access to hardware on an ECU and which is therefore linked to a specific ECU or specific hardware. The ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType introduces the possibility to link from the software representation to its hardware description provided by the ECU Resource Template. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwComponentTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType" stereotype:atpObject

171.name: COMPONENT-CLUSTERING
171.description: note:Constraint that forces the mapping of all referenced SW component instances  to the same ECU, Core, Partition depending on the defined mappingScope attribute.  If mappingScope is not specified then mappingScopeEcu shall be assumed. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ComponentClustering" stereotype:atpObject

172.name: COMPONENT-IN-COMPOSITION-INSTANCE-REF
172.description: note:The ComponentInCompositionInstanceRef points to a concrete SwComponentPrototype within a CompositionSwComponentType. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ComponentInCompositionInstanceRef" stereotype:atpObject,instanceRef

174.name: COMPONENT-SEPARATION
174.description:
note:Constraint that forces the two referenced SW components (called A and B in the following) not to be mapped to the same ECU, Core, Partition depending on the defined mappingScope attribute. If mappingScope is not specified then mappingScopeEcu shall be assumed. 

If a SW component (e.g. A) is a composition, none of the atomic SW components making up the A composition must be mapped together with any of the atomic SW components making up the B composition. Furthermore, A and B must be disjoint. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ComponentSeparation" stereotype:atpObject

175.name: COMPOSITE-NETWORK-REPRESENTATION
175.description: note:This meta-class is used to define the network representation of leaf elements of composite application data types. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompositeNetworkRepresentation" stereotype:atpObject

176.name: COMPOSITION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE
176.description: note:A CompositionSwComponentType aggregates SwComponentPrototypes (that in turn are typed by SwComponentTypes) as well as SwConnectors for primarily connecting SwComponentPrototypes among each others and towards the surface of the CompositionSwComponentType. By this means hierarchical structures of software-components can be created. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwComponentTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="CompositionSwComponentType" stereotype:atpObject

177.name: COMPU
177.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express one particular computation. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Compu" stereotype:atpObject

178.name: COMPU-CONST
178.description: note:This meta-class represents the fact that the value of a computation method scale is constant. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompuConst" stereotype:atpObject

179.name: COMPU-CONST-FORMULA-CONTENT
179.description: note:This meta-class represents the fact that the constant value of the computation method is represented by a variation point. This difference is due to compatibility with ASAM HDO. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompuConstFormulaContent" stereotype:atpObject

180.name: COMPU-CONST-NUMERIC-CONTENT
180.description: note:This meta-class represents the fact that the constant value of the computation method is a numerical value. It is separated from CompuConstFormulaContent to support compatibility with ASAM HDO. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompuConstNumericContent" stereotype:atpObject

181.name: COMPU-CONST-TEXT-CONTENT
181.description: note:This meta-class represents the textual content of a scale. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompuConstTextContent" stereotype:atpObject

182.name: COMPU-GENERIC-MATH
182.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify a generic formula expression. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompuGenericMath" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

183.name: COMPU-METHOD
183.description:
note:This meta-class represents the ability to express the relationship between a physical value and the mathematical representation. 

Note that this is still independent of the technical implementation in data types. It only specifies the formula how the internal value corresponds to its physical pendant. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="CompuMethods";mmt.qualifiedName="CompuMethod" stereotype:atpObject

184.name: COMPU-NOMINATOR-DENOMINATOR
184.description: note:This class represents the ability to express a polynomial either as Nominator or as Denominator. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompuNominatorDenominator" stereotype:atpObject

185.name: COMPU-RATIONAL-COEFFS
185.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a rational function by specifying the coefficients of nominator and denominator. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompuRationalCoeffs" stereotype:atpObject

186.name: COMPU-SCALE
186.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify one segment of a segmented computation method. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompuScale" stereotype:atpObject

187.name: COMPU-SCALE-CONSTANT-CONTENTS
187.description: note:This meta-class represents the fact that a particular scale of the computation method is constant. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompuScaleConstantContents" stereotype:atpObject

188.name: COMPU-SCALE-RATIONAL-FORMULA
188.description: note:This meta-class represents the fact that the computation in this scale is represented as rational term. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompuScaleRationalFormula" stereotype:atpObject

189.name: COMPU-SCALES
189.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to stepwise express a computation method. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CompuScales" stereotype:atpObject

190.name: CONCRETE-PATTERN-EVENT-TRIGGERING
190.description: note:The ConcretePatternEventTriggering describes the behavior of an event, which occurs following a precisely known pattern. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ConcretePatternEventTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

191.name: CONDITION-BY-FORMULA
191.description:
note:This class represents a condition which is computed based on system constants according to the specified expression. The expected result is considered as boolean value.

The result of the expression is interpreted as a condition. 

* "0" represents "false";  

* a value other than zero is considered "true" tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ConditionByFormula" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

192.name: CONDITIONAL-CHANGE-NAD
192.description: note:Generates an conditional change NAD request. See LIN 2.1 protocol specification for more information. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ConditionalChangeNad" stereotype:atpObject

193.name: CONFIDENCE-INTERVAL
193.description: note:Additionally to the list of measured distances of event occurrences, a confidence interval can be specified for the expected distance of two consecutive event occurrences with a given probability. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ConfidenceInterval" stereotype:atpObject

194.name: CONSISTENCY-NEEDS
194.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to define requirements on the implicit communication behavior. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ConsistencyNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

195.name: CONSISTENCY-NEEDS-BLUEPRINT-SET
195.description: note:This meta class represents the ability to specify a set of blueprint for ConsistencyNeeds. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ConsistencyNeedsBlueprintSets";mmt.qualifiedName="ConsistencyNeedsBlueprintSet" stereotype:atpObject

196.name: CONSTANT-REFERENCE
196.description: note:Instead of defining this value inline, a constant is referenced. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ConstantReference" stereotype:atpObject

197.name: CONSTANT-SPECIFICATION
197.description: note:Specification of a constant that can be part of a package, i.e. it can be defined stand-alone. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ConstantSpecifications";mmt.qualifiedName="ConstantSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

198.name: CONSTANT-SPECIFICATION-MAPPING
198.description:
note:This meta-class is used to create an association of two ConstantSpecifications. One ConstantSpecification is supposed to be defined in the application domain while the other should be defined in the implementation domain.

Hence the ConstantSpecificationMapping needs to be used where a ConstantSpecification defined in one domain needs to be associated to a ConstantSpecification in the other domain.

This information is crucial for the RTE generator. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ConstantSpecificationMapping" stereotype:atpObject

199.name: CONSTANT-SPECIFICATION-MAPPING-SET
199.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to map two ConstantSpecifications to each others. One ConstantSpecification is supposed to be described in the application domain and the other should be described in the implementation domain. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ConstantSpecificationMappingSets";mmt.qualifiedName="ConstantSpecificationMappingSet" stereotype:atpObject

200.name: CONSUMED-EVENT-GROUP
200.description: note:A Service may have event groups which can be consumed. A service consumer has to subscribe to the corresponding event-group. After the subscription the event consumer takes the role of a server and the event provider that of a client. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ConsumedEventGroup" stereotype:atpObject

201.name: CONSUMED-SERVICE-INSTANCE
201.description: note:Service instances that are consumed by the ECU that is connected via the ApplicationEndpoint to a CommunicationConnector. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ConsumedServiceInstance" stereotype:atpObject

202.name: CONTAINED-I-PDU-PROPS
202.description: note:Defines the aspects of an IPdu which can be collected inside a ContainerIPdu. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ContainedIPduProps" stereotype:atpObject

203.name: CONTAINER-I-PDU
203.description: note:Allows to collect several IPdus in one ContainerIPdu based on the IPdu.headerId. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ContainerIPdu" stereotype:atpObject

204.name: COUPLING-ELEMENT
204.description: note:A CouplingElement is used to connect EcuInstances to the VLAN of an EthernetCluster. CouplingElements can reach from a simple hub to a complex managed switch or even devices with functionalities in higher layers. A CouplingElement that is not related to an EcuInstance occurs as a dedicated single device. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="CouplingElements";mmt.qualifiedName="CouplingElement" stereotype:atpObject

205.name: COUPLING-PORT
205.description: note:A CouplingPort is used to connect a CouplingElement with an EcuInstance or two CouplingElements with each other via a CouplingPortConnection. Optionally, the CouplingPort may also have a reference to a macMulticastGroup and a defaultVLAN. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CouplingPort" stereotype:atpObject

206.name: COUPLING-PORT-CONNECTION
206.description: note:Connection between two CouplingPorts (firstPort and secondPort). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CouplingPortConnection" stereotype:atpObject

207.name: COUPLING-PORT-DETAILS
207.description:
note:Defines details of a CouplingPort.

May be used to configure the structures of a switch. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CouplingPortDetails" stereotype:atpObject

208.name: COUPLING-PORT-FIFO
208.description: note:Defines a Fifo for the CouplingPort egress structure. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CouplingPortFifo" stereotype:atpObject

209.name: COUPLING-PORT-SCHEDULER
209.description: note:Defines a scheduler for the CouplingPort egress structure. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CouplingPortScheduler" stereotype:atpObject

210.name: COUPLING-PORT-SHAPER
210.description: note:Defines a shaper for the CouplingPort egress structure. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CouplingPortShaper" stereotype:atpObject

211.name: COUPLING-PORT-TRAFFIC-CLASS-ASSIGNMENT
211.description:
note:Defines the assignment of Traffic Class to a frame.

Two use-cases are supported:
1. Only one ethernetTrafficClassAssignment is defined and NO priority is given:
--> all frames on this ingress port get assigned the trafficClass.
2. for each ethernetTrafficClass WITH a priority the frames which are coming in with this priority get assigned the trafficClass.

Constraint: 1 and 2 can not be combined for one CouplingPortDetails. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CouplingPortTrafficClassAssignment" stereotype:atpObject

212.name: CRYPTO-SERVICE-NEEDS
212.description: note:Specifies the needs on the configuration of the CryptoServiceManager for one ConfigID (see Specification AUTOSAR_SWS_CSM.doc). An instance of this class is used to find out which ports of an SWC belong to this ConfigID. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CryptoServiceNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

213.name: CYCLE-COUNTER
213.description: note:The communication cycle where the frame is send is described by the attribute "cycleCounter". tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CycleCounter" stereotype:atpObject

214.name: CYCLE-REPETITION
214.description:
note:The communication cycle where the frame is send is described by the
attributes baseCycle and cycleRepetition. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CycleRepetition" stereotype:atpObject

215.name: CYCLIC-TIMING
215.description: note:Specification of a cyclic sending behavior. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="CyclicTiming" stereotype:atpObject

216.name: DATA-CONSTR
216.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify constraints on data. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="DataConstrs";mmt.qualifiedName="DataConstr" stereotype:atpObject

217.name: DATA-CONSTR-RULE
217.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express one specific data constraint rule. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataConstrRule" stereotype:atpObject

218.name: DATA-DUMP-ENTRY
218.description: note:This service is reserved for initial configuration of a slave node by the slave node supplier and the format of this message is supplier specific. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataDumpEntry" stereotype:atpObject

219.name: DATA-FILTER
219.description: note:Base class for data filters. The type of the filter is specified in attribute dataFilterType. Some of the filter types require additional arguments which are specified as attributes of this class. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataFilter" stereotype:atpObject

220.name: DATA-PROTOTYPE-GROUP
220.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to define a collection of DataPrototypes that are subject to the formal definition of implicit communication behavior. The definition of the collection can be nested. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataPrototypeGroup" stereotype:atpObject

222.name: DATA-PROTOTYPE-MAPPING
222.description:
note:Defines the mapping of two particular VariableDataPrototypes, ParameterDataPrototypes or ArgumentDataPrototypes with unequal names and/or unequal semantic (resolution or range) in context of two different SenderReceiverInterface, NvDataInterface or ParameterInterface or Operations.

If the semantic is unequal following rules apply:
The textTableMapping is only applicable if the referred DataPrototypes are typed by AutosarDataType referring to CompuMethods of category TEXTTABLE, SCALE_LINEAR_AND_TEXTTABLE or BITFIELD_TEXTTABLE.

In the case that the  DataPrototypes are typed by AutosarDataType either referring to CompuMethods of category LINEAR, IDENTICAL or referring to no CompuMethod (which is similar as  IDENTICAL) the linear conversion factor is calculated out of the factorSiToUnit and offsetSiToUnit attributes of the referred Units and the CompuRationalCoeffs of a compuInternalToPhys of the referred CompuMethods. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataPrototypeMapping" stereotype:atpObject

223.name: DATA-RECEIVE-ERROR-EVENT
223.description: note:This event is raised by the RTE when the Com layer detects and notifies an error concerning the reception of the referenced data element. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataReceiveErrorEvent" stereotype:atpObject

224.name: DATA-RECEIVED-EVENT
224.description: note:The event is raised when the referenced data elements are received. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataReceivedEvent" stereotype:atpObject

225.name: DATA-SEND-COMPLETED-EVENT
225.description: note:The event is raised when the referenced data elements have been sent or an error occurs. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataSendCompletedEvent" stereotype:atpObject

226.name: DATA-TRANSFORMATION
226.description: note:A DataTransformation represents a transformer chain. It is an ordered list of transformers. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataTransformation" stereotype:atpObject

227.name: DATA-TRANSFORMATION-REF-CONDITIONAL
227.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataTransformation" stereotype:atpObject

228.name: DATA-TRANSFORMATION-SET
228.description: note:This element is the system wide container of DataTransformations which represent transformer chains. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataTransformationSet" stereotype:atpObject

229.name: DATA-TYPE-MAP
229.description: note:This class represents the relationship between ApplicationDataType and its implementing ImplementationDataType. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataTypeMap" stereotype:atpObject

230.name: DATA-TYPE-MAPPING-SET
230.description: note:This class represents a list of mappings between ApplicationDataTypes and ImplementationDataTypes. In addition, it can contain mappings between ImplementationDataTypes and ModeDeclarationGroups. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="DataTypeMappingSets";mmt.qualifiedName="DataTypeMappingSet" stereotype:atpObject

231.name: DATA-WRITE-COMPLETED-EVENT
231.description: note:This event is raised if an implicit write access was successful or an error occurred. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DataWriteCompletedEvent" stereotype:atpObject

232.name: DCM-I-PDU
232.description: note:Represents the IPdus handled by Dcm. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Pdus";mmt.qualifiedName="DcmIPdu" stereotype:atpObject

233.name: DEF-ITEM
233.description: note:This represents an entry in a definition list. The defined item is specified using shortName and longName. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DefItem" stereotype:atpObject

234.name: DEF-LIST
234.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a list of definitions. Note that a definition list might be rendered similar to a labeled list but has a particular semantics to denote definitions. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DefList" stereotype:atpObject

235.name: DEFAULT-VALUE-ELEMENT
235.description: note:The default value consists of a number of elements. Each element is one byte long and the number of elements is specified by SduLength. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DefaultValueElement" stereotype:atpObject

236.name: DELEGATED-PORT-ANNOTATION
236.description: note:Annotation to a "delegated port" to specify the Signal Fan In or Signal Fan Out inside the CompositionSwComponentType. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DelegatedPortAnnotation" stereotype:atpObject

237.name: DELEGATION-SW-CONNECTOR
237.description: note:A delegation connector delegates one inner PortPrototype  (a port of a component that is used inside the composition) to a outer PortPrototype of compatible type that belongs directly to the composition (a port that is owned by the composition). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DelegationSwConnector" stereotype:atpObject

238.name: DEPENDENCY-ON-ARTIFACT
238.description: note:Dependency on the existence of another artifact, e.g. a library. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DependencyOnArtifact" stereotype:atpObject

239.name: DHCP-SERVER-CONFIGURATION
239.description: note:Defines the configuration of DHCP servers that are running on the network endpoint. It is possible that an Ipv4DhcpServer and an Ipv6DhcpServer run on the same Ecu. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DhcpServerConfiguration" stereotype:atpObject

240.name: DIAG-EVENT-DEBOUNCE-COUNTER-BASED
240.description:
note:This meta-class represents the ability to indicate that the counter-based debounce algorithm shall be used by the DEM for this diagnostic monitor.

This is related to set the ECUC choice container DemDebounceAlgorithmClass to DemDebounceCounterBased. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagEventDebounceCounterBased" stereotype:atpObject

241.name: DIAG-EVENT-DEBOUNCE-MONITOR-INTERNAL
241.description:
note:This meta-class represents the ability to indicate that the pre-debounce algorithm shall be used by the DEM for this diagnostic monitor.

This is related to setting the ECUC choice container DemDebounceAlgorithmClass to DemDebounceMonitorInternal.

If the FaultDetectionAlogrithm is already known to be implemented by a specific BswModuleEntry the reference bswModuleEntry points to the function specification.

If the FaultDetectionCounter value is accessible at a PortPrototype this PortPrototype shall be referenced by an assignedPort. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagEventDebounceMonitorInternal" stereotype:atpObject

242.name: DIAG-EVENT-DEBOUNCE-TIME-BASED
242.description:
note:This meta-class represents the ability to indicate that the time-based pre-debounce algorithm shall be used by the DEM for this diagnostic monitor.

This is related to set the ECUC choice container DemDebounceAlgorithmClass to DemDebounceTimeBase. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagEventDebounceTimeBased" stereotype:atpObject

243.name: DIAGNOSTIC-ACCESS-PERMISSION
243.description:
note:This represents the specification of whether a given service can be accessed according to the existence of meta-classes referenced by a particular DiagnosticAccessPermission.

In other words, this meta-class acts as a mapping element between several (otherwise unrelated) pieces of information that are put into context for the purpose of checking for access rights. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticAccessPermission" stereotype:atpObject

244.name: DIAGNOSTIC-AGING
244.description: note:Defines the aging algorithm. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticAging" stereotype:atpObject

245.name: DIAGNOSTIC-CLEAR-DIAGNOSTIC-INFORMATION
245.description: note:This represents an instance of the "Clear Diagnostic Information" diagnostic service. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticClearDiagnosticInformation" stereotype:atpObject

246.name: DIAGNOSTIC-CLEAR-DIAGNOSTIC-INFORMATION-CLASS
246.description: note:This meta-class contains attributes shared by all instances of the "Clear Diagnostic Information" diagnostic service. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticClearDiagnosticInformationClass" stereotype:atpObject

247.name: DIAGNOSTIC-COM-CONTROL
247.description: note:This represents an instance of the "Communication Control" diagnostic service. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticComControl" stereotype:atpObject

248.name: DIAGNOSTIC-COM-CONTROL-CLASS
248.description: note:This meta-class contains attributes shared by all instances of the "Communication Control" diagnostic service. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticComControlClass" stereotype:atpObject

249.name: DIAGNOSTIC-COM-CONTROL-SPECIFIC-CHANNEL
249.description: note:This represents the ability to add further attributes to the definition of a specific channel that is subject to the diagnostic service "communication control". tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticComControlSpecificChannel" stereotype:atpObject

250.name: DIAGNOSTIC-COM-CONTROL-SUB-NODE-CHANNEL
250.description: note:This represents the ability to add further attributes to the definition of a specific sub-node channel that is subject to the diagnostic service "communication control". tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticComControlSubNodeChannel" stereotype:atpObject

251.name: DIAGNOSTIC-COMMON-ELEMENT-REF-CONDITIONAL
251.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticCommonElement" stereotype:atpObject

252.name: DIAGNOSTIC-COMMON-PROPS
252.description: note:This meta-class aggregates a number of common properties that are shared among a diagnostic extract. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticCommonProps";vh.latestBindingTime="codeGenerationTime" stereotype:atpObject

253.name: DIAGNOSTIC-COMMON-PROPS-CONDITIONAL
253.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticCommonPropsConditional" stereotype:atpObject

254.name: DIAGNOSTIC-COMMUNICATION-MANAGER-NEEDS
254.description: note:Specifies the general needs on the configuration of the  Diagnostic Communication Manager (DCM) which are not related to a particular item (e.g. a PID or DiagnosticRoutineNeeds). The main use case is the mapping of service ports to the DCM which are not related to a particular item. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticCommunicationManagerNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

255.name: DIAGNOSTIC-CONNECTED-INDICATOR
255.description: note:Description of indicators that are defined per DiagnosticEvent. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticConnectedIndicator" stereotype:atpObject

256.name: DIAGNOSTIC-CONNECTION
256.description: note:DiagnosticConncection that is used to describe the relationship between several TP connections. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticConnection" stereotype:atpObject

257.name: DIAGNOSTIC-CONNECTION-REF-CONDITIONAL
257.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticConnection" stereotype:atpObject

259.name: DIAGNOSTIC-CONTROL-DTC-SETTING
259.description: note:This represents an instance of the "Control DTC Setting" diagnostic service. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticControlDTCSetting" stereotype:atpObject

260.name: DIAGNOSTIC-CONTROL-DTC-SETTING-CLASS
260.description: note:This meta-class contains attributes shared by all instances of the "Control DTC Setting" diagnostic service. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticControlDTCSettingClass" stereotype:atpObject

261.name: DIAGNOSTIC-CUSTOM-SERVICE-CLASS
261.description: note:This represents the ability to define a custom diagnostic service class and assign an ID to it. Further configuration is not foreseen from the point of view of the diagnostic extract and consequently needs to be done on the level of ECUC. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticCustomServiceClass" stereotype:atpObject

262.name: DIAGNOSTIC-DATA-CHANGE-TRIGGER
262.description: note:This represents the ability to define a trigger based on the change of a given DiagnosticDataIdentifier. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticDataChangeTrigger" stereotype:atpObject

263.name: DIAGNOSTIC-DATA-ELEMENT
263.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to describe a concrete piece of data to be taken into account for diagnostic purposes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DiagnosticDataElement" stereotype:atpObject

note:Dynamic part of a multiplexed I-Pdu.

certain transmission of a multiplexed PDU. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DynamicPartAlternative" stereotype:atpObject

382.name: ECU-MAPPING
382.description: note:ECUMapping allows to assign an ECU hardware type (defined in the ECU Resource Template) to an ECUInstance used in a physical topology. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ECUMapping" stereotype:atpObject

383.name: EOC-EVENT-REF
383.description: note:This is used to define a reference to an RTE or BSW Event. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EOCEventRef" stereotype:atpObject

384.name: EOC-EXECUTABLE-ENTITY-REF
384.description:
note:This is used to define a reference to an ExecutableEntity

If the ExecutionOrderConstraint is defined on VFB, System or ECU level, a reference to the SwComponentPrototype, via the ComponentInCompositionInstanceRef, the referenced ExecutableEntity belongs to, must be provided as context information. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EOCExecutableEntityRef" stereotype:atpObject

385.name: EOC-EXECUTABLE-ENTITY-REF-GROUP
385.description: note:This is used to specify a group (composite) consisting of Execution Order Constraint Executable Entity References (leaves) and/or further Execution Order Constraint Executable Entity Reference Groups (composite). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EOCExecutableEntityRefGroup" stereotype:atpObject

386.name: ECU-ABSTRACTION-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE
386.description: note:The ECUAbstraction is a special AtomicSwComponentType that resides between a software-component that wants to access ECU periphery and the Microcontroller Abstraction. The EcuAbstractionSwComponentType introduces the possibility to link from the software representation to its hardware description provided by the ECU Resource Template. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwComponentTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="EcuAbstractionSwComponentType" stereotype:atpObject

387.name: ECU-INSTANCE
387.description: note:ECUInstances are used to define the ECUs used in the topology. The type of the ECU is defined by a reference to an ECU specified with the ECU resource description. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="EcuInstances";mmt.qualifiedName="EcuInstance" stereotype:atpObject

388.name: ECU-PARTITION
388.description: note:Partitions are used as error containment regions. They permit the grouping of SWCs and resources and allow to describe recovery policies individually for each partition. Partitions can be terminated or restarted during run-time as a result of a detected error. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcuPartition" stereotype:atpObject

389.name: ECU-RESOURCE-ESTIMATION
389.description: note:Resource estimations for RTE and BSW of a single ECU instance. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcuResourceEstimation" stereotype:atpObject

390.name: ECU-STATE-MGR-USER-NEEDS
390.description: note:Specifies the abstract needs on the configuration of the ECU State  Manager for one "user". This class currently contains no attributes. Its name can be regarded as a symbol identifying the user  from the viewpoint of the component or module which owns this class. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcuStateMgrUserNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

391.name: ECU-TIMING

note:A model element used to define timing descriptions and constraints within the scope of one ECU configuration.

TimingDescriptions aggregated by EcuTiming are allowed to use all events derived from the class TimingDescriptionEvent. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="TimingExtensions";mmt.qualifiedName="EcuTiming" stereotype:atpObject

395.name: ECUC-CHOICE-CONTAINER-DEF

396.name: ECUC-CHOICE-REFERENCE-DEF

397.name: ECUC-CONDITION-FORMULA
397.description: note:This formula must yield a boolean expression depending on ecuc queries. Note that the EcucConditionFormula is a mixed string. Therefore, the properties have the upper multiplicity 1. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcucConditionFormula" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

398.name: ECUC-CONDITION-SPECIFICATION
398.description: note:Allows to define existence dependencies based on the value of  parameter values. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcucConditionSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

399.name: ECUC-CONFIGURATION-CLASS-AFFECTION
