note:Specifies in the "VendorSpecificModuleDefinition" whether changes on this parameter do affect other parameters in a later configuration step.

This element is removed from the specifications and shall not be used. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="EcucConfigurationClassAffection" stereotype:atpObject

400.name: ECUC-CONTAINER-VALUE
400.description: note:Represents a Container definition in the ECU Configuration Description. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcucContainerValue" stereotype:atpObject

401.name: ECUC-DEFINITION-COLLECTION

402.name: ECUC-DERIVATION-SPECIFICATION

note:Allows to define configuration items that are calculated based on the value of

- elements (attributes/classes) defined in other AUTOSAR templates such as System template and SW component template tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcucDerivationSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

403.name: ECUC-DESTINATION-URI-DEF
403.description: note:Description of an EcucDestinationUriDef that is used as target of EcucUriReferenceDefs. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcucDestinationUriDef" stereotype:atpObject

404.name: ECUC-DESTINATION-URI-DEF-SET
404.description: note:This class represents a list of EcucDestinationUriDefs. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcucDestinationUriDefSet" stereotype:atpObject

405.name: ECUC-DESTINATION-URI-POLICY
405.description: note:The EcucDestinationUriPolicy describes the EcucContainerDef that will be targeted by EcucUriReferenceDefs. The type of the description is dependent of the destinationUriNestingContract attribute. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcucDestinationUriPolicy" stereotype:atpObject

406.name: ECUC-ENUMERATION-LITERAL-DEF
406.description: note:Configuration parameter type for enumeration literals definition. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcucEnumerationLiteralDef" stereotype:atpObject

407.name: ECUC-ENUMERATION-PARAM-DEF
407.description: note:Configuration parameter type for Enumeration. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcucEnumerationParamDef";xml.sequenceOffset="0" stereotype:atpObject

408.name: ECUC-FLOAT-PARAM-DEF

409.name: ECUC-FOREIGN-REFERENCE-DEF

412.name: ECUC-IMPLEMENTATION-CONFIGURATION-CLASS
412.description:
note:Specifies which ConfigurationClass this parameter has in the individual ConfigurationVariants.

413.name: ECUC-INSTANCE-REFERENCE-DEF
413.description: note:Specify a reference to an XML description of an entity described in another AUTOSAR template using the INSTANCE REFERENCE semantics. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcucInstanceReferenceDef" stereotype:atpObject

418.name: ECUC-MODULE-CONFIGURATION-VALUES

As part of the BSW module description, the EcucModuleConfigurationValues element has two different roles:

The recommendedConfiguration contains parameter values recommended by the BSW module vendor. 

The preconfiguredConfiguration contains values for those parameters which are fixed by the implementation and cannot be changed.

These two EcucModuleConfigurationValues are used when the base EcucModuleConfigurationValues (as part of the base ECU configuration) is created to fill parameters with initial values. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="EcucModuleConfigurationValuess";mmt.qualifiedName="EcucModuleConfigurationValues" stereotype:atpObject

419.name: ECUC-MODULE-CONFIGURATION-VALUES-REF-CONDITIONAL

420.name: ECUC-MODULE-DEF

421.name: ECUC-MULTILINE-STRING-PARAM-DEF

426.name: ECUC-PARAMETER-DERIVATION-FORMULA
426.description: note:This formula is intended to specify how an ecu parameter can be derived from other information in the Autosar Templates. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EcucParameterDerivationFormula" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

The EmptySignal can be mapped to the response group or to request group. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="EmptySignalMapping" stereotype:atpObject

441.name: END-TO-END-DESCRIPTION

442.name: END-TO-END-PROTECTION

443.name: END-TO-END-PROTECTION-I-SIGNAL-I-PDU
443.description:
note:It is possible to protect the inter-ECU data exchange of safety-related ISignalGroups at the level of COM IPdus using protection mechanisms provided by E2E Library. For each ISignalGroup to be protected, a separate EndToEndProtectionISignalIPdu element shall be created within the EndToEndProtectionSet. 

The EndToEndProtectionISignalIPdu element refers to the ISignalGroup that is to be protected and to the ISignalIPdu that transmits the protected ISignalGroup. The information how the referenced ISignalGroup shall be protected (through which E2E Profile and with which E2E settings) is defined in the EndToEndDescription element. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EndToEndProtectionISignalIPdu" stereotype:atpObject

444.name: END-TO-END-PROTECTION-SET
444.description: note:This represents a container for collection EndToEndProtectionInformation. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="EndToEndProtectionSets";mmt.qualifiedName="EndToEndProtectionSet" stereotype:atpObject

445.name: END-TO-END-PROTECTION-VARIABLE-PROTOTYPE

For this purpose, for each communication to be protected,  the user defines a separate EndToEndProtection (specifying a set of protection settings) and refers to a variableDataPrototype in the role of sender and to one or many variableDataPrototypes in the role of receiver. For details, see EndToEnd Library. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EndToEndProtectionVariablePrototype" stereotype:atpObject

459.name: ETHERNET-PRIORITY-REGENERATION

The ethernetPriorityRegeneration is optional in case no priority regeneration shall be performed.

460.name: EVALUATED-VARIANT-SET
460.description:
note:This meta class represents the ability to express if a set of ARElements is able to support one or more particular variants.

In other words, for a given set of evaluatedElements this meta class represents a table of evaluated variants, where each PredefinedVariant represents one column. In this column each descendant swSystemconstantValue resp. postbuildVariantCriterionValue represents one entry.

In a graphical representation each swSystemconstantValueSet / postBuildVariantCriterionValueSet could be used as an intermediate headline in the table column.

If the approvalStatus is "APPROVED" it expresses that the collection of CollectableElements is known be valid for the given evaluatedVariants.

Note that the EvaluatedVariantSet is a CollectableElement. This allows to establish a hierarchy of EvaluatedVariantSets. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="EvaluatedVariantSets";mmt.qualifiedName="EvaluatedVariantSet" stereotype:atpObject

If a consumed event group is referenced the configuration is only valid for this relation. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="EventHandler" stereotype:atpObject

463.name: EXCLUSIVE-AREA

465.name: EXECUTABLE-ENTITY-ACTIVATION-REASON
465.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to define the reason for the activation of the enclosing ExecutableEntity. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ExecutableEntityActivationReason" stereotype:atpObject

466.name: EXECUTION-ORDER-CONSTRAINT
466.description:
note:This constraint is used to restrict the order of execution for a set of ExecutableEntities. The ExecutionOrderConstraint can be used in any timing view.

The various scopes for ExecutionOrderConstraint are described below. Generally, each ExecutionOrderConstraint has a scope of software components and can reference all executable entities available in the corresponding internal behavior (RunnableEntity and BswModuleEntity) either directly or by the events activating respectively starting them (RteEvent and BswEvent).

On VFB level an ExecutionOrderConstraint can be specified for RunnableEntities part of the composition hierarchy referenced by the VfbTiming. The ExecutionOrderConstraint is aggregated by the VfbTiming.

On SW-C level an ExecutionOrderConstraint can be specified for RunnableEntities part of the InternalBehavior referenced by the SwcTiming. The ExecutionOrderConstraint is aggregated by the SwcTiming.

On System level an ExecutionOrderConstraint can be specified for RunnableEntities part of the composition hierarchy of the system referenced by the SystemTiming. The ExecutionOrderConstraint is aggregated by the SystemTiming.

On BSW Module level, an ExectionOrderConstraint can be specified for BswModuleEntities part of an BswInternalBehavior referenced by the BswModuleTiming. The ExecutionOrderConstraint is aggregated by the BswModuleTiming.

On ECU level an ExecutionOrderConstraint can be specified for all ExecutableEntities and Events available via the EcucValueCollection, covering ECU Extract and BSW Module Configuration, referenced by the EcuTiming. The ExecutionOrderConstraint is aggregated by the EcuTiming. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ExecutionOrderConstraint" stereotype:atpObject

467.name: EXECUTION-TIME-CONSTRAINT
467.description:
note:An ExecutionTimeConstraint is used to specify the execution time of the referenced ExecutableEntity in the referenced component. A minimum and maximum execution time can be defined. Two types of execution time semantics can be used. The desired semantics can be set by the attribute executionTimeType:
  • The "net" execution time is the time used to execute the ExecutableEntity without interruption and without external calls.
  • The "gross" execution time is the time used to execute the ExecutableEntity without interruption including external calls to other entities.
The time to execute the ExecutableEntity including interruptions by other entities and including external calls is commonly called "response time". The TimingExtensions provide the concept of event chains and latency constraints for that purpose. An event chain from the start of the entity to the termination of the entity with according latency constraint represents a response time constraint for that executable entity. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ExecutionTimeConstraint" stereotype:atpObject

468.name: EXTERNAL-TRIGGER-OCCURRED-EVENT

469.name: EXTERNAL-TRIGGERING-POINT

470.name: EXTERNAL-TRIGGERING-POINT-IDENT

471.name: FM-ATTRIBUTE-DEF

473.name: FM-CONDITION-BY-FEATURES-AND-ATTRIBUTES

475.name: FM-FEATURE

476.name: FM-FEATURE-DECOMPOSITION

note:A FMFeatureDecomposition describes dependencies between a list of

aggregates the FMFeatureDecomposition). The kind of dependency is
defined by the attribute category. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FMFeatureDecomposition" stereotype:atpObject

477.name: FM-FEATURE-MAP

AUTOSAR model. To do this, it defines value sets for system

whenever a certain combination of features (and system constants) is encountered. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="FMFeatureMaps";mmt.qualifiedName="FMFeatureMap" stereotype:atpObject

478.name: FM-FEATURE-MAP-ASSERTION

479.name: FM-FEATURE-MAP-CONDITION

480.name: FM-FEATURE-MAP-ELEMENT
480.description:
note:Defines value sets for system constants and postbuild variant
criterions that shall be chosen whenever a certain combination
of features (and system constants) is encountered. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FMFeatureMapElement" stereotype:atpObject

481.name: FM-FEATURE-MODEL
481.description: note:A Feature model describes the features of a product line and their dependencies. Feature models are an optional part of an AUTOSAR model. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="FMFeatureModels";mmt.qualifiedName="FMFeatureModel" stereotype:atpObject

482.name: FM-FEATURE-RELATION
482.description:
note:Defines relations for FMFeatures, for example dependencies on
other FMFeatures, or conflicts with other FMFeatures. A FMFeature
can only be part of a FMFeatureSelectionSet if all its
relations are fulfilled. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FMFeatureRelation" stereotype:atpObject

483.name: FM-FEATURE-RESTRICTION
483.description:
note:Defines restrictions for FMFeatures. A FMFeature can only be part
of a FMFeatureSelectionSet if at least one of its restrictions evaluate to true. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FMFeatureRestriction" stereotype:atpObject

484.name: FM-FEATURE-SELECTION
484.description:
note:A FMFeatureSelection represents the state of a particular
FMFeature within a FMFeatureSelectionSet. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FMFeatureSelection" stereotype:atpObject

485.name: FM-FEATURE-SELECTION-SET
485.description: note:A FMFeatureSelectionSet is a set of FMFeatures that describes a specific product. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="FMFeatureModelSelectionSets";mmt.qualifiedName="FMFeatureSelectionSet" stereotype:atpObject

486.name: FIBEX-ELEMENT-REF-CONDITIONAL
486.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FibexElement" stereotype:atpObject

487.name: FLAT-INSTANCE-DESCRIPTOR
487.description:
note:Represents exactly one node (e.g. a component instance or data element) of the instance tree of a software system. The purpose of this element is to map the various nested representations of this instance to a flat representation and assign a unique name (shortName) to it.

Use cases: 
* Specify unique names of measurable data to be used by MCD tools
* Specify unique names of calibration data to be used by MCD tool
* Specify a unique name for an instance of a component prototype in the ECU extract of the system description

Note that in addition it is possible to assign alias names via AliasNameAssignment. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlatInstanceDescriptor" stereotype:atpObject

488.name: FLAT-MAP
488.description:
note:Contains a flat list of references to software objects. This list is used to identify instances and to resolve name conflicts. The scope is given by the RootSwCompositionPrototype for which it is used, i.e. it can be applied to a system, system extract or ECU-extract.

An instance of FlatMap may also be used in a preliminary context, e.g. in the scope of a software component before integration into a system. In this case it is not referred by a RootSwCompositionPrototype. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="FlatMaps";mmt.qualifiedName="FlatMap" stereotype:atpObject

489.name: FLEXRAY-ABSOLUTELY-SCHEDULED-TIMING
489.description:
note:Each frame in FlexRay is identified by its slot id and communication cycle. A description is provided by the usage of AbsolutelyScheduledTiming. 

In the static segment a frame can be sent multiple times within one communication cycle. For describing this case multiple AbsolutelyScheduledTimings have to be used. The main use case would be that a frame is sent twice within one communication cycle. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayAbsolutelyScheduledTiming" stereotype:atpObject

490.name: FLEXRAY-AR-TP-CHANNEL
490.description:
note:A channel is a group of connections sharing several properties.

The FlexRay AutosarTransport Layer supports several channels. These channels can work concurrently, thus each of them requires its own state machine and management data structures and its own PDU-IDs. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayArTpChannel" stereotype:atpObject

491.name: FLEXRAY-AR-TP-CONFIG
491.description:
note:This element defines exactly one FlexRay Autosar TP Configuration. 

One FlexrayArTpConfig element shall be created for each FlexRay Network in the System that uses FlexRay Autosar TP. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="TpConfigs";mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayArTpConfig" stereotype:atpObject

492.name: FLEXRAY-AR-TP-CONNECTION
492.description:
note:A connection within a channel identifies the sender and the receiver of this particular communication.

The FlexRay Autosar Tp module routes a Pdu through this connection. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayArTpConnection" stereotype:atpObject

493.name: FLEXRAY-AR-TP-NODE
493.description: note:TP Node (Sender or Receiver) provides the TP Address and the connection to the Topology description. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayArTpNode" stereotype:atpObject

494.name: FLEXRAY-CLUSTER
494.description: note:FlexRay specific attributes to the physicalCluster tag:atp.recommendedPackage="CommunicationClusters";mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayCluster" stereotype:atpObject

495.name: FLEXRAY-CLUSTER-CONDITIONAL
495.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayClusterConditional" stereotype:atpObject

496.name: FLEXRAY-COMMUNICATION-CONNECTOR
496.description: note:FlexRay specific attributes to the CommunicationConnector tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayCommunicationConnector" stereotype:atpObject

497.name: FLEXRAY-COMMUNICATION-CONTROLLER
497.description: note:FlexRay bus specific communication port attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayCommunicationController" stereotype:atpObject

498.name: FLEXRAY-COMMUNICATION-CONTROLLER-CONDITIONAL
498.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayCommunicationControllerConditional" stereotype:atpObject

499.name: FLEXRAY-FIFO-CONFIGURATION
499.description: note:One First In First Out (FIFO) queued receive structure, defining the admittance criteria to the FIFO, and mandating the ability to admit messages into the FIFO based on Message Id filtering criteria. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayFifoConfiguration" stereotype:atpObject

500.name: FLEXRAY-FIFO-RANGE
500.description: note:FIFO Frame Id range acceptance criteria. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayFifoRange" stereotype:atpObject

502.name: FLEXRAY-FRAME-TRIGGERING
502.description: note:FlexRay specific attributes to the FrameTriggering tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayFrameTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

503.name: FLEXRAY-NM-CLUSTER
503.description: note:FlexRay specific NM cluster attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayNmCluster" stereotype:atpObject

504.name: FLEXRAY-NM-CLUSTER-COUPLING
504.description: note:FlexRay attributes that are valid for each of the referenced (coupled) FlexRay clusters. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayNmClusterCoupling" stereotype:atpObject

506.name: FLEXRAY-NM-NODE
506.description: note:FlexRay specific NM Node attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayNmNode" stereotype:atpObject

507.name: FLEXRAY-PHYSICAL-CHANNEL
507.description: note:FlexRay specific attributes to the physicalChannel tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayPhysicalChannel" stereotype:atpObject

508.name: FLEXRAY-TP-CONFIG
508.description:
note:This element defines exactly one FlexRay ISO TP Configuration. 

One FlexRayTpConfig element shall be created for each FlexRay Network in the System that uses FlexRay Iso Tp. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="TpConfigs";mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayTpConfig" stereotype:atpObject

509.name: FLEXRAY-TP-CONNECTION
509.description:
note:A connection identifies the sender and the receiver of this particular communication. The FlexRayTp module routes a Pdu through this connection. 

In a System Description the references to the PduPools are mandatory. In an ECU Extract these references can be optional:
On unicast connections these references are always mandatory.
On multicast the txPduPool is mandatory on the sender side. The rxPduPool is mandatory on the receiver side. On Gateway ECUs both references are mandatory. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayTpConnection" stereotype:atpObject

510.name: FLEXRAY-TP-CONNECTION-CONTROL
510.description: note:Configuration parameters to control a FlexRay TP connection. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayTpConnectionControl" stereotype:atpObject

511.name: FLEXRAY-TP-ECU
511.description: note:ECU specific TP configuration parameters. Each TpEcu element has a reference to exactly one ECUInstance in the topology. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayTpEcu" stereotype:atpObject

512.name: FLEXRAY-TP-NODE
512.description: note:TP Node (Sender or Receiver) provides the TP Address and the connection to the Topology description. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayTpNode" stereotype:atpObject

513.name: FLEXRAY-TP-PDU-POOL
513.description: note:FlexrayTpPduPool is a set of N-PDUs which are defined for FrTp sending or receiving purpose. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FlexrayTpPduPool" stereotype:atpObject

514.name: FLOAT-VALUE-VARIATION-POINT
514.description:
note:This class represents an attribute value variation point for Float attributes.

Note that this class might be used in the extended meta-model only tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FloatValueVariationPoint" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

515.name: FORBIDDEN-SIGNAL-PATH
515.description: note:The ForbiddenSignalPath describes the physical channels which an element must not take in the topology. Such a signal path can be a constraint for the communication matrix,  because such a path has an effect on the frame generation and the frame path. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ForbiddenSignalPath" stereotype:atpObject

516.name: FOREIGN-MODEL-REFERENCE
516.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a late binding reference to a foreign model element. The foreign model element can be from every model. Even if it is modeled according to the association representation, it is not limited to refer to AUTOSAR model elements. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ForeignModelReference" stereotype:atpObject

517.name: FRAME-MAPPING
517.description:
note:The entire source frame is mapped as it is onto the target frame (what in general is only possible inside of a common platform). In this case source and target frame should be the identical object.

Each pair consists in a SOURCE and a TARGET referencing to a FrameTriggering.

The Frame Mapping is not supported by the Autosar BSW. The existence is optional and has been incorporated into the System Template mainly for compatibility in order to allow interchange between FIBEX and AUTOSAR descriptions. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FrameMapping" stereotype:atpObject

518.name: FRAME-PID
518.description: note:Frame_PIDs that are included in the request. The "pid" attribute describes the value and the "index" attribute the position of the frame_PID in the request. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FramePid" stereotype:atpObject

519.name: FRAME-PORT
519.description: note:Connectors reception or send port on the referenced channel referenced by a FrameTriggering. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FramePort" stereotype:atpObject

520.name: FREE-FORMAT
520.description: note:Representing freely defined data. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FreeFormat" stereotype:atpObject

521.name: FUNCTION-INHIBITION-NEEDS
521.description: note:Specifies the abstract needs on the configuration of the Function Inhibition Manager for one Function Identifier (FID). This class currently contains no attributes. Its name can be regarded as a symbol identifying the FID  from the viewpoint of the component or module which owns this class. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="FunctionInhibitionNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

522.name: GATEWAY
522.description: note:A gateway is an ECU that is connected to two or more clusters (channels, but not redundant), and performs a frame, Pdu or signal mapping between them. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Gateways";mmt.qualifiedName="Gateway" stereotype:atpObject

523.name: GENERAL-PARAMETER
523.description: note:This represents a parameter in general e.g. an entry in a data sheet. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GeneralParameter" stereotype:atpObject

524.name: GENERAL-PURPOSE-I-PDU
524.description: note:This element is used for AUTOSAR Pdus without attributes that are routed by the PduR. Please note that the category name of such Pdus is standardized in the AUTOSAR System Template. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Pdus";mmt.qualifiedName="GeneralPurposeIPdu" stereotype:atpObject

525.name: GENERAL-PURPOSE-PDU
525.description: note:This element is used for AUTOSAR Pdus without additional attributes that are routed by a bus interface. Please note that the category name of such Pdus is standardized in the AUTOSAR System Template. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Pdus";mmt.qualifiedName="GeneralPurposePdu" stereotype:atpObject

526.name: GENERIC-ETHERNET-FRAME
526.description: note:This element is used for EthernetFrames without additional attributes that are routed by the EthIf. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GenericEthernetFrame" stereotype:atpObject

527.name: GENERIC-MODEL-REFERENCE
527.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a late binding reference to a model element. The model element can be from every model. Even if it is modeled according to the association representation, it is not limited to refer to AUTOSAR model elements. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GenericModelReference" stereotype:atpObject

528.name: GENERIC-TP
528.description: note:Content Model for a generic transport protocol. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GenericTp" stereotype:atpObject

529.name: GLOBAL-TIME-CAN-MASTER
529.description: note:This represents the specialization of the GlobalTimeMaster for the CAN communication. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GlobalTimeCanMaster" stereotype:atpObject

530.name: GLOBAL-TIME-CAN-SLAVE
530.description: note:This represents the specialization of the GlobalTimeSlave for the CAN communication. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GlobalTimeCanSlave" stereotype:atpObject

531.name: GLOBAL-TIME-DOMAIN
531.description: note:This represents the ability to define a global time domain. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GlobalTimeDomain" stereotype:atpObject

532.name: GLOBAL-TIME-ETH-MASTER
532.description: note:This represents the specialization of the GlobalTimeMaster for Ethernet communication. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GlobalTimeEthMaster" stereotype:atpObject

533.name: GLOBAL-TIME-ETH-SLAVE
533.description: note:This represents the specialization of the GlobalTimeSlave for Ethernet communication. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GlobalTimeEthSlave" stereotype:atpObject

534.name: GLOBAL-TIME-FR-MASTER
534.description: note:This represents the specialization of the GlobalTimeMaster for Flexray communication. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GlobalTimeFrMaster" stereotype:atpObject

535.name: GLOBAL-TIME-FR-SLAVE
535.description: note:This represents the specialization of the GlobalTimeSlave for Flexray communication. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GlobalTimeFrSlave" stereotype:atpObject

536.name: GLOBAL-TIME-GATEWAY
536.description: note:This represents the ability to define a time gateway for establishing a global time domain over several communication clusters. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="GlobalTimeGateway" stereotype:atpObject

537.name: GRAPHIC
537.description: note:This class represents an artifact containing the image to be inserted in the document tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Graphic" stereotype:atpObject

538.name: HARDWARE-CONFIGURATION
538.description: note:Describes in which mode the hardware is operating while needing this resource consumption. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HardwareConfiguration" stereotype:atpObject

539.name: HTTP-TP
539.description: note:Http over TCP as transport protocol. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HttpTp" stereotype:atpObject

540.name: HW-ATTRIBUTE-DEF
540.description:
note:This metaclass represents the ability to define a particular hardware attribute.

The category of this element defines the type of the attributeValue. If the category is Enumeration the hwAttributeEnumerationLiterals specify the available literals. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HwAttributeDef" stereotype:atpObject

541.name: HW-ATTRIBUTE-LITERAL-DEF
541.description: note:One available EnumerationLiteral of the Enumeration definition. Only applicable if the category of the HwAttributeDef equals Enumeration. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HwAttributeLiteralDef" stereotype:atpObject

542.name: HW-ATTRIBUTE-VALUE
542.description: note:This metaclass represents the ability to assign a hardware attribute value. Note that v and vt are mutually exclusive. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HwAttributeValue" stereotype:atpObject

543.name: HW-CATEGORY
543.description: note:This metaclass represents the ability to declare hardware categories and its particular attributes. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="HwCategorys";mmt.qualifiedName="HwCategory" stereotype:atpObject

544.name: HW-ELEMENT
544.description: note:This represents the ability to describe Hardware Elements on an instance level. The particular types of hardware are distinguished by the category. This category determines the applicable attributes. The possible categories and attributes are defined in HwCategory. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="HwElements";mmt.qualifiedName="HwElement" stereotype:atpObject

545.name: HW-ELEMENT-CONNECTOR
545.description:
note:This meta-class represents the ability to connect two hardware elements. 
The details of the connection can be refined by hwPinGroupConnection. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HwElementConnector" stereotype:atpObject

546.name: HW-ELEMENT-REF-CONDITIONAL
546.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HwElement" stereotype:atpObject

547.name: HW-PIN
547.description: note:This meta-class represents the possibility to describe a hardware pin. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HwPin" stereotype:atpObject

548.name: HW-PIN-CONNECTOR
548.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to connect two pins. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HwPinConnector" stereotype:atpObject

549.name: HW-PIN-GROUP
549.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to describe groups of pins which are used to connect hardware elements. This group acts as a bundle of pins. Thereby they allow to describe high level connections. Pin groups can even be nested. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HwPinGroup" stereotype:atpObject

550.name: HW-PIN-GROUP-CONNECTOR
550.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to connect two pin groups. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HwPinGroupConnector" stereotype:atpObject

551.name: HW-PIN-GROUP-CONTENT
551.description: note:This meta-class specifies a mixture of hwPins and hwPinGroups. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HwPinGroupContent" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

552.name: HW-PORT-MAPPING
552.description: note:HWPortMapping specifies the hwCommunicationPort (defined in the ECU Resource Template) to realize the specified CommunicationConnector in a physical topology. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="HwPortMapping" stereotype:atpObject

553.name: HW-TYPE
553.description: note:This represents the ability to describe Hardware types on an abstract level. The particular types of hardware are distinguished by the category. This category determines the applicable attributes. The possible categories and attributes are defined in HwCategory. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="HwTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="HwType" stereotype:atpObject

554.name: I-PDU-MAPPING
554.description: note:Arranges those IPdus that are transferred by the gateway from one channel to the other in pairs and defines the mapping between them. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="IPduMapping" stereotype:atpObject

555.name: I-PDU-PORT
555.description: note:Connectors reception or send port on the referenced channel referenced by a PduTriggering. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="IPduPort" stereotype:atpObject

556.name: I-PDU-TIMING
556.description:
note:AUTOSAR COM provides the possibility to define two different TRANSMISSION MODES for each IPdu.

The Transmission Mode of an IPdu that is valid at a specific point in time is selected using the values of the signals that are mapped to this IPdu. For each IPdu a Transmission Mode Selector is defined. The Transmission Mode Selector is calculated by evaluating the conditions for a subset of signals  (class TransmissionModeCondition in the System Template).

The Transmission Mode Selector is defined to be true, if at least one Condition evaluates to true and is defined to be false, if all Conditions evaluate to false. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="IPduTiming" stereotype:atpObject

557.name: I-SIGNAL
557.description:
note:Signal of the Interaction Layer. The RTE supports a "signal fan-out" where the same System Signal is sent in different SignalIPdus to multiple receivers. 

To support the RTE "signal fan-out" each SignalIPdu  contains ISignals. If the same System Signal is to be mapped into several SignalIPdus there is one ISignal needed for each ISignalToIPduMapping. 

ISignals describe the Interface between the Precompile configured RTE and the potentially Postbuild configured Com Stack (see ECUC Parameter Mapping). 

In case of the SystemSignalGroup an ISignal must be created for each SystemSignal contained in the SystemSignalGroup. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ISignals";mmt.qualifiedName="ISignal" stereotype:atpObject

558.name: I-SIGNAL-GROUP
558.description:
note:SignalGroup of the Interaction Layer. The RTE supports a "signal fan-out" where the same System Signal Group is sent in different SignalIPdus to multiple receivers.   

An ISignalGroup refers to a set of ISignals that shall always be kept together. A ISignalGroup represents a COM Signal Group.  

Therefore it is recommended to put the ISignalGroup in the same Package as ISignals (see atp.recommendedPackage) tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ISignalGroup";mmt.qualifiedName="ISignalGroup" stereotype:atpObject

559.name: I-SIGNAL-I-PDU
559.description:
note:Represents the IPdus handled by Com. The ISignalIPdu assembled and disassembled in AUTOSAR COM consists of one or more signals.
In case no multiplexing is performed this IPdu is routed to/from the Interface Layer.

A maximum of one dynamic length signal per IPdu is allowed. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Pdus";mmt.qualifiedName="ISignalIPdu" stereotype:atpObject

560.name: I-SIGNAL-I-PDU-GROUP
560.description: note:The AUTOSAR COM Layer is able to start and to stop sending and receiving  configurable groups of I-Pdus during runtime. An ISignalIPduGroup contains either ISignalIPdus or ISignalIPduGroups. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ISignaliPduGroup";mmt.qualifiedName="ISignalIPduGroup" stereotype:atpObject

561.name: I-SIGNAL-I-PDU-REF-CONDITIONAL
561.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ISignalIPdu" stereotype:atpObject

562.name: I-SIGNAL-MAPPING
562.description:
note:Arranges those signals (or SignalGroups) that are transferred by the gateway from one channel to the other in pairs and defines the mapping between them.
Each pair consists in a source and a target referencing to a ISignalTriggering. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ISignalMapping" stereotype:atpObject

563.name: I-SIGNAL-PORT
563.description:
note:Connectors reception or send port on the referenced channel referenced by an ISignalTriggering. 
If different timeouts or DataFilters for ISignals need to be specified several ISignalPorts may be created. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ISignalPort" stereotype:atpObject

564.name: I-SIGNAL-PROPS
564.description: note:Additional ISignal properties that may be stored in different files. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ISignalProps" stereotype:atpObject

565.name: I-SIGNAL-TO-I-PDU-MAPPING
565.description: note:An ISignalToIPduMapping describes the mapping of ISignals to ISignalIPdus and defines the position of the ISignal within an ISignalIPdu. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ISignalToIPduMapping" stereotype:atpObject

566.name: I-SIGNAL-TRIGGERING
566.description: note:A ISignalTriggering allows an assignment of ISignals to physical channels. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ISignalTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

567.name: I-SIGNAL-TRIGGERING-REF-CONDITIONAL
567.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ISignalTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

568.name: IDENTIFIER
568.description:
note:An Identifier is a string with a number of constraints on its appearance, satisfying the requirements typical programming languages define for their Identifiers.

This datatype represents a string, that can be used as a c-Identifier.

It shall start with a letter, may consist of letters, digits and underscores. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Identifier";xml.xsd.customType="IDENTIFIER";xml.xsd.maxLength="128";xml.xsd.pattern="[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*";xml.xsd.type="string" stereotype:atpObject,primitive

569.name: IEEE-1722-TP
569.description: note:Content Model for IEEE 1722 configuration. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Ieee1722Tp" stereotype:atpObject

571.name: IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE
571.description: note:Describes a reusable data type on the implementation level. This will typically correspond to a typedef in C-code. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ImplementationDataTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="ImplementationDataType" stereotype:atpObject

572.name: IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE-ELEMENT
572.description:
note:Declares a data object which is locally aggregated. Such an element can only be used within the scope where it is aggregated. 

This element either consists of further subElements or it is further defined via its swDataDefProps.

There are several use cases within the system of ImplementationDataTypes fur such a local declaration:
* It can represent the elements of an array, defining the element type and array size
* It can represent an element of a struct, defining its type
* It can be the local declaration of a debug element. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ImplementationDataTypeElement" stereotype:atpObject

573.name: IMPLEMENTATION-DATA-TYPE-SUB-ELEMENT-REF
573.description: note:This meta-class represents the specialization of SubElementMapping with respect to ImplementationDataTypes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ImplementationDataTypeSubElementRef" stereotype:atpObject

574.name: IMPLEMENTATION-ELEMENT-IN-PARAMETER-INSTANCE-REF
574.description:
note:Describes a reference to a particular ImplementationDataTypeElement instance in the context of a given ParameterDataPrototype.
Thus it refers to a particular element in the implementation description of a software data structure.

Use Case:
The RTE generator publishes its generated structure of calibration parameters in its BSW module description using the "constantMemory" role of ParameterDataPrototypes. Each ParameterDataPrototype describes a group of single calibration parameters. In order to point to these single parameters, this "instance ref" is needed.

Note that this class follows the pattern of an InstanceRef but is not implemented based on the abstract classes because the ImplementationDataType isn't either, especially because ImplementationDataTypeElement isn't derived from AtpPrototype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ImplementationElementInParameterInstanceRef" stereotype:atpObject

575.name: INCLUDED-DATA-TYPE-SET
575.description:
note:An includedDataTypeSet declares that a set of AutosarDataType is used by a basic software module or a software component for its implementation and the AutosarDataType becomes part of the contract. 

This information is required if the AutosarDataType is not used for any DataPrototype owned by this software component or if the enumeration literals, lowerLimit and upperLimit constants shall be generated with a literalPrefix.

The optional literalPrefix is used to add a common prefix on enumeration literals, lowerLimit and upperLimit constants created by the RTE. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="IncludedDataTypeSet" stereotype:atpObject

576.name: INCLUDED-MODE-DECLARATION-GROUP-SET
576.description: note:An IncludedModeDeclarationGroupSet declares that a set of ModeDeclarationGroups used by the software component for its implementation and consequently these ModeDeclarationGroups become part of the contract. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="IncludedModeDeclarationGroupSet" stereotype:atpObject

577.name: INDENT-SAMPLE
577.description: note:This represents the ability to specify indentation of a labeled list by providing a sample content. This content can be measured by the rendering system in order to determine the width of indentation. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="IndentSample" stereotype:atpObject

578.name: INDEX-ENTRY
578.description: note:This class represents an index entry. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="IndexEntry" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

579.name: INDEXED-ARRAY-ELEMENT
579.description: note:This element represents exactly one indexed element in the array.  Either the applicationArrayElement or implementationArrayElement reference shall be used. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="IndexedArrayElement" stereotype:atpObject

580.name: INFRASTRUCTURE-SERVICES
580.description: note:Defines the network infrastructure services provided or consumed. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InfrastructureServices" stereotype:atpObject

581.name: INIT-EVENT
581.description: note:This RTEEvent is supposed to be used for initialization purposes, i.e. for starting and restarting a partition. It is not guaranteed that all RunnableEntities referenced by this InitEvent are executed before the 'regular' RunnableEntities are executed for the first time. The execution order depends on the task mapping. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InitEvent" stereotype:atpObject

582.name: INITIAL-SD-DELAY-CONFIG
582.description: note:This element is used to configure the offer behavior of the server and the find behavior on the client. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InitialSdDelayConfig" stereotype:atpObject

583.name: INNER-DATA-PROTOTYPE-GROUP-IN-COMPOSITION-INSTANCE-REF
583.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to define an InstanceRef to a nested DataPrototypeGroup tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InnerDataPrototypeGroupInCompositionInstanceRef" stereotype:atpObject,instanceRef

585.name: INNER-RUNNABLE-ENTITY-GROUP-IN-COMPOSITION-INSTANCE-REF
585.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to define an InstanceRef to a nested RunnableEntityGroup. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InnerRunnableEntityGroupInCompositionInstanceRef" stereotype:atpObject,instanceRef

587.name: INSTANTIATION-DATA-DEF-PROPS
587.description:
note:This is a general class allowing to apply additional SwDataDefProps to particular instantiations of a DataPrototype.

Typically the accessibility and further information like alias names for a  particular data is modeled on the level of DataPrototypes (especially  VariableDataPrototypes, ParameterDataPrototypes). But due to the recursive  structure of the meta-model concerning data types (a composite (data) type consists  out of data prototypes) a part of the MCD information is described in the data  type (in case of ApplicationCompositeDataType).

This is a strong restriction in the reuse of data typed because the data type should be re-used  for different VariableDataPrototypes and ParameterDataPrototypes to guarantee type  compatibility on C-implementation level (e.g. data of a Port is stored in PIM  or a ParameterDataPrototype used as ROM Block and shall be typed by the same data type as NVRAM Block).

This class overcomes such a restriction if applied properly. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InstantiationDataDefProps" stereotype:atpObject

588.name: INSTANTIATION-TIMING-EVENT-PROPS
588.description: note:This meta class represents the ability to refine a timing event for particular instances of a software component. This supports then an instance specific timing. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InstantiationTimingEventProps" stereotype:atpObject

589.name: INTEGER-VALUE-VARIATION-POINT
589.description:
note:This class represents an attribute value variation point for Integer attributes.

Note that this class might be used in the extended meta-model only. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="IntegerValueVariationPoint" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

590.name: INTERNAL-CONSTRS
590.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express internal constraints. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InternalConstrs" stereotype:atpObject

591.name: INTERNAL-TRIGGER-OCCURRED-EVENT
591.description: note:The event is raised when the referenced internal trigger have been occurred. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InternalTriggerOccurredEvent" stereotype:atpObject

592.name: INTERNAL-TRIGGERING-POINT
592.description: note:If a RunnableEntity owns a InternalTriggeringPoint it is entitled to trigger the execution of RunnableEntities of the corresponding software-component. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InternalTriggeringPoint" stereotype:atpObject

593.name: INTERPOLATION-ROUTINE
593.description: note:This represents an interpolation routine taken to evaluate the contents of a curve or map against a specific input value. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InterpolationRoutine" stereotype:atpObject

594.name: INTERPOLATION-ROUTINE-MAPPING
594.description:
note:This meta-class provides a mapping between one record layout and its matching interpolation routines. This allows to formally specify the semantics of the interpolation routines. 

The use case is such that the curves/Maps define an interpolation method. This mapping table specifies which interpolation routine implements methods for a particular record layout. Using this information, the implementer of a software-component can select the appropriate interpolation routine. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InterpolationRoutineMapping" stereotype:atpObject

595.name: INTERPOLATION-ROUTINE-MAPPING-SET
595.description: note:This meta-class specifies a set of interpolation routine mappings. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="InterpolationRoutineMappingSets";mmt.qualifiedName="InterpolationRoutineMappingSet" stereotype:atpObject

596.name: INVALIDATION-POLICY
596.description:
note:Specifies whether the component can actively invalidate a particular dataElement.

If no invalidationPolicy points to a dataElement this is considered to yield the identical result as if the handleInvalid attribute was set to dontInvalidate. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="InvalidationPolicy" stereotype:atpObject

597.name: IO-HW-ABSTRACTION-SERVER-ANNOTATION
597.description:
note:The IoHwAbstractionServerAnnotation will only be used from a sensor- or an actuator component while interacting with the IoHwAbstraction layer.

Note that the "server" in the name of this meta-class is not meant to restrict the usage to ClientServerInterfaces. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="IoHwAbstractionServerAnnotation" stereotype:atpObject

598.name: IPV-4-CONFIGURATION
598.description: note:Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4) configuration. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Ipv4Configuration" stereotype:atpObject

599.name: IPV-4-DHCP-SERVER-CONFIGURATION
599.description: note:Defines the configuration of a IPv4 DHCP server that runs on the network endpoint. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Ipv4DhcpServerConfiguration" stereotype:atpObject

600.name: IPV-6-CONFIGURATION
600.description: note:Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) configuration. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Ipv6Configuration" stereotype:atpObject

601.name: IPV-6-DHCP-SERVER-CONFIGURATION
601.description: note:Defines the configuration of a IPv6 DHCP server that runs on the network endpoint. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Ipv6DhcpServerConfiguration" stereotype:atpObject

602.name: ITEM
602.description: note:This meta-class represents one particular item in a list. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Item" stereotype:atpObject

604.name: J-1939-CLUSTER-CONDITIONAL
604.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="J1939ClusterConditional" stereotype:atpObject

605.name: J-1939-DCM-I-PDU
605.description: note:Represents the IPdus handled by J1939Dcm. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Pdus";mmt.qualifiedName="J1939DcmIPdu" stereotype:atpObject

606.name: J-1939-NM-CLUSTER
606.description: note:J1939 specific NmCluster attributes tag:mmt.qualifiedName="J1939NmCluster" stereotype:atpObject

607.name: J-1939-NM-ECU
607.description: note:J1939 NmEcu specific attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="J1939NmEcu" stereotype:atpObject

608.name: J-1939-NM-NODE
608.description: note:J1939 specific NM Node attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="J1939NmNode" stereotype:atpObject

609.name: J-1939-NODE-NAME
609.description: note:This element contains attributes to configure the J1939NmNode NAME. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="J1939NodeName" stereotype:atpObject

610.name: J-1939-TP-CONFIG
610.description:
note:This element defines exactly one J1939 TP Configuration. 

One J1939TpConfig element shall be created for each J1939 Network in the System. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="TpConfigs";mmt.qualifiedName="J1939TpConfig" stereotype:atpObject

611.name: J-1939-TP-CONNECTION
611.description: note:A J1939TpConnection represents an internal path for the transmission or reception of a Pdu via J1939Tp and describes the the sender and the receiver of this particular communication. The J1939Tp module routes a Pdu (J1939 PGN) through the connection. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="J1939TpConnection" stereotype:atpObject

612.name: J-1939-TP-NODE
612.description: note:TP Node (Sender or Receiver) provides the TP Address and the connection to the Topology description. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="J1939TpNode" stereotype:atpObject

613.name: J-1939-TP-PG
613.description: note:A J1939TpPg represents one J1939 message (parameter group, PG) identified by the PGN (parameter group number) that can be received or transmitted via J1939Tp. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="J1939TpPg" stereotype:atpObject

614.name: KEYWORD
614.description:
note:This meta-class represents the ability to predefine keywords which may subsequently be used to construct names following a given naming convention, e.g. the AUTOSAR naming conventions.

Note that such names is not only shortName. It could be symbol, or even longName. Application of keywords is not limited to particular names. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Keyword" stereotype:atpObject

615.name: KEYWORD-SET
615.description: note:This meta--class represents the ability to collect a set of predefined keywords. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="KeywordSets";mmt.qualifiedName="KeywordSet" stereotype:atpObject

616.name: L-GRAPHIC
616.description: note:This meta-class represents the figure in one particular language. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LGraphic" stereotype:atpObject

617.name: L-LONG-NAME
617.description: note:MixedContentForLongNames  in one particular language. The language is denoted in the attribute l. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LLongName" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

618.name: L-OVERVIEW-PARAGRAPH
618.description: note:MixedContentForOverviewParagraph in one particular language. The language is denoted in the attribute l. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LOverviewParagraph" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

619.name: L-PARAGRAPH
619.description: note:This is the text for a paragraph in one particular language. The language is denoted in the attribute l. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LParagraph" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

620.name: L-PLAIN-TEXT
620.description: note:This represents plain string in one particular language. The language is denoted in the attribute l. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LPlainText" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

621.name: L-VERBATIM
621.description: note:MixedContentForVerbatim in one particular language. The language is denoted in the attribute l. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LVerbatim" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

622.name: LABELED-ITEM
622.description: note:this represents an item of a labeled list. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LabeledItem" stereotype:atpObject

623.name: LABELED-LIST
623.description: note:This meta-class represents a labeled list, in which items have a label and a content. The policy how to render such items is specified in the labeled list. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LabeledList" stereotype:atpObject

624.name: LATENCY-TIMING-CONSTRAINT
624.description:
note:This constraint type restricts the time duration between the occurrence of the stimulus and the occurrence of the corresponding response of that chain.

Two latency constraint types are of interest for automotive systems. These are the age of a certain response and the reaction to a certain stimulus.

In contrast to OffsetTimingConstraint, a causal dependency between the stimulus and response event of the associated event chain is required. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LatencyTimingConstraint" stereotype:atpObject

625.name: LIFE-CYCLE-INFO
625.description: note:LifeCycleInfo describes the life cycle state of an element together with additional information like what to use instead tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LifeCycleInfo" stereotype:atpObject

626.name: LIFE-CYCLE-INFO-SET
626.description:
note:This meta class represents the ability to attach a life cycle  information to a particular set of elements.

The information can be defined for a particular period. This supports the definition of transition plans.

If no period is specified, the life cycle state applies forever. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="LifeCycleInfoSets";mmt.qualifiedName="LifeCycleInfoSet" stereotype:atpObject

627.name: LIFE-CYCLE-PERIOD
627.description: note:This meta class represents the ability to specify a point of time within a specified period, e.g. the starting or end point, in which a specific life cycle state is valid/applies to. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LifeCyclePeriod" stereotype:atpObject

628.name: LIFE-CYCLE-STATE
628.description: note:This meta class represents one particular state in the LifeCycle. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LifeCycleState" stereotype:atpObject

629.name: LIFE-CYCLE-STATE-DEFINITION-GROUP
629.description: note:This meta class represents the ability to define the states and properties of one particular life cycle. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="LifeCycleStateDefintionGroups";mmt.qualifiedName="LifeCycleStateDefinitionGroup" stereotype:atpObject

630.name: LIMIT-VALUE
630.description: note:This class represents the ability to express a numerical limit.  Note that this is in fact a NumericalVariationPoint but has the additional attribute intervalType. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Limit";xml.xsd.customType="LIMIT-VALUE";xml.xsd.pattern="(0x[0-9a-f]+)|(0[0-7]+)|(0b[0-1]+)|(([+\-]?[1-9][0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?|[+\-]?[0-9](\.[0-9]+)?)(E([+\-]?)[0-9]+)?)|\.0|INF|-INF|NaN";xml.xsd.type="string" stereotype:atpObject,primitive

631.name: LIMIT
631.description:
note:This class represents the ability to express a numerical limit.  Note that this is in fact a NumericalValuationPoint but has the additional attribute intervalType.

Note that the xml.name is "LIMIT" for backward compatibility reasons. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LimitValueVariationPoint";xml.name="LIMIT" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

633.name: LIN-CLUSTER-CONDITIONAL
633.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinClusterConditional" stereotype:atpObject

634.name: LIN-COMMUNICATION-CONNECTOR
634.description: note:LIN bus specific communication connector attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinCommunicationConnector" stereotype:atpObject

635.name: LIN-CONFIGURABLE-FRAME
635.description:
note:Assignment of messageIds to Frames. 
This element shall be used for the LIN 2.0 Assign-Frame command. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinConfigurableFrame" stereotype:atpObject

636.name: LIN-ERROR-RESPONSE
636.description: note:Each slave node shall publish a one bit signal, named response_error, to the master node in one of its transmitted unconditional frames. The response_error signal shall be set whenever a frame (except for event triggered frame responses) that is transmitted or received by the slave node contains an error in the frame response. The response_error signal shall be cleared when the unconditional frame containing the response_error signal is successfully transmitted. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinErrorResponse" stereotype:atpObject

637.name: LIN-EVENT-TRIGGERED-FRAME
637.description:
note:An event triggered frame is used as a placeholder to allow multiple slave nodes to provide its response.

The header of an event triggered frame is transmitted when a frame slot allocated to the event triggered frame is processed. The publisher of an associated unconditional frame shall only transmit the response if at least one of the signals carried in its unconditional frame is updated. The LIN Master discovers and purges collisions with the collisionResolvingScheduleTable. 

The event controlled frame shall not contain any Pdus. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Frames";mmt.qualifiedName="LinEventTriggeredFrame" stereotype:atpObject

638.name: LIN-FRAME-TRIGGERING
638.description: note:LIN specific attributes to the FrameTriggering tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinFrameTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

639.name: LIN-MASTER
639.description: note:Describing the properties of the refering ecu as a LIN master. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinMaster" stereotype:atpObject

640.name: LIN-MASTER-CONDITIONAL
640.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinMasterConditional" stereotype:atpObject

641.name: LIN-ORDERED-CONFIGURABLE-FRAME
641.description: note:With the assignment of the index to a frame a mapping of Pids to Frames is possible. This element shall be used for the LIN 2.1 Assign-Frame-PID-Range command. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinOrderedConfigurableFrame" stereotype:atpObject

642.name: LIN-PHYSICAL-CHANNEL
642.description: note:LIN specific attributes to the physicalChannel tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinPhysicalChannel" stereotype:atpObject

643.name: LIN-SCHEDULE-TABLE
643.description: note:The master task (in the master node) transmits frame headers based on a schedule table. The schedule table specifies the identifiers for each header and the interval between the start of a frame and the start of the following frame. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinScheduleTable" stereotype:atpObject

644.name: LIN-SLAVE
644.description: note:Describing the properties of the referring ecu as a LIN slave. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinSlave" stereotype:atpObject

645.name: LIN-SLAVE-CONDITIONAL
645.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinSlaveConditional" stereotype:atpObject

646.name: LIN-SLAVE-CONFIG
646.description:
note:Node attributes of LIN slaves that are handled by the LinMaster. 

In the System Description LIN slaves may be described as non AUTOSAR ECUs (linSlaveEcu reference). But in an Ecu Extract of the LinMaster the LinSlaveEcus will not be available. The information that is described here is necessary in the ECU Extract for the configuration of the LinMaster. 

The values of attributes of LinSlaveConfig and LinSlave shall be identical for each LinSlaveConfig that points to a LinSlave. Please note that this causes redundancy which is intended to support flexible development methodology. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinSlaveConfig" stereotype:atpObject

647.name: LIN-SLAVE-CONFIG-IDENT
647.description: note:This meta-class is created to add the ability to become the target of a reference to the non-Referrable LinSlaveConfig. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinSlaveConfigIdent" stereotype:atpObject

648.name: LIN-SPORADIC-FRAME
648.description: note:A sporadic frame is a group of unconditional frames that share the same frame slot. The sporadic frame shall not contain any Pdus. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Frames";mmt.qualifiedName="LinSporadicFrame" stereotype:atpObject

649.name: LIN-TP-CONFIG
649.description:
note:This element defines exactly one Lin TP Configuration. 

One LinTpConfig element shall be created for each Lin Network in the System. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="TpConfigs";mmt.qualifiedName="LinTpConfig" stereotype:atpObject

650.name: LIN-TP-CONNECTION
650.description:
note:A LinTP channel represents an internal path for the transmission or reception of a Pdu via LinTp and describes the the sender and the receiver of this particular communication. 

LinTp supports (per Lin Cluster) the configuration of one Rx Tp-SDU and one Tx Tp-SDU per NAD the LinMaster uses to address one or more of its Lin Slaves. To support this an arbitrary number of LinTpConnections shall be described. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinTpConnection" stereotype:atpObject

651.name: LIN-TP-NODE
651.description: note:TP Node (Sender or Receiver) provides the TP Address and the connection to the Topology description. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="LinTpNode" stereotype:atpObject

652.name: LIN-UNCONDITIONAL-FRAME
652.description: note:Unconditional frames carry signals. The master sends a frame header in a scheduled frame slot and the designated slave node fills the frame with data. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Frames";mmt.qualifiedName="LinUnconditionalFrame" stereotype:atpObject

653.name: LINKER
653.description: note:Specifies the linker attributes used to describe how the linker shall be invoked. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Linker" stereotype:atpObject

654.name: LIST
654.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a list. The kind of list is specified in the attribute. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="List" stereotype:atpObject

655.name: LOGIC-ADDRESS
655.description: note:The logical DoIP address. This element shall only be used for DoIP (Diagnosis over IP). tag:atp.Status="obsolete";atp.StatusRevisionBegin="4.2.2";mmt.qualifiedName="LogicAddress" stereotype:atpObject

656.name: MAC-MULTICAST-CONFIGURATION
656.description: note:References a per cluster globally defined MAC-Multicast-Group. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MacMulticastConfiguration" stereotype:atpObject

657.name: MAC-MULTICAST-GROUP
657.description: note:Per EthernetCluster globally defined MacMulticastGroup. One sender can handle many receivers simultaneously if the receivers have all the same macMulticastAddress. The addresses need to be unique for the particular EthernetCluster. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MacMulticastGroup" stereotype:atpObject

658.name: MAP
658.description:
note:Image maps enable authors to specify regions of an image or object and assign a specific action to each region (e.g., retrieve a document, run a program, etc.) When the region is activated by the user, the action is executed.

The class follows the html approach and is intended to support interactive documents. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Map" stereotype:atpObject

659.name: MC-DATA-ACCESS-DETAILS
659.description:
note:This meta-class allows to attach detailed information about the usage of a data buffer by the RTE to a corresponding McDataInstance.

Use Case:  Direct memory access to RTE internal buffers for rapid prototyping. In case of implicit communication, the various task local buffers need to be identified in relation to RTE events and variable access points.

Note that the SwComponentPrototype, the RunnableEntity and the VariableDataPrototype are implicitly given be the referred instances of RTEEvent and VariableAccess. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="McDataAccessDetails" stereotype:atpObject

660.name: MC-DATA-INSTANCE
660.description:
note:Describes the specific properties of one data instance in order to support measurement and/or calibration of this data instance.

The most important attributes are:
* Its shortName is copied from the ECU Flat map (if applicable) and will be used as identifier and for display by the MC system.
* The category is copied from the corresponding data type (ApplicationDataType if defined, otherwise ImplementationDataType) as far as applicable.
* The symbol is the one used in the programming language. It will be used to find out the actual memory address by the final generation tool with the help of linker generated information.

It is assumed that in the M1 model this part and all the aggregated and referred elements (with the exception of the Flat Map and the references from ImplementationElementInParameterInstanceRef and McAccessDetails) are completely generated from "upstream" information. This means, that even if an element like e.g. a CompuMethod is only used via reference here, it will be copied into the M1 artifact which holds the complete McSupportData for a given Implementation. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="McDataInstance" stereotype:atpObject

661.name: MC-FUNCTION
661.description:
note:Represents a functional element to be used as input to support measurement and calibration. It is used to
* assign calibration parameters to a logical function
* assign measurement variables to a logical function
* structure functions hierarchically tag:atp.recommendedPackage="McFunctions";mmt.qualifiedName="McFunction" stereotype:atpObject

662.name: MC-FUNCTION-DATA-REF-SET
662.description:
note:Refers to a set of data assigned to an McFunction in a particular role. The data are given
* either by entries in a FlatMap
* or by data instances that are part of MC support data.
These two possibilities are exclusive within a given McFunctionDataRefSet. Which one to use depends on the process and tool environment. 

The set is subject to variability because the same functional model may be used with various representation of the data. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="McFunctionDataRefSet";vh.latestBindingTime="preCompileTime" stereotype:atpObject

663.name: MC-FUNCTION-DATA-REF-SET-CONDITIONAL
663.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="McFunctionDataRefSetConditional" stereotype:atpObject

664.name: MC-PARAMETER-ELEMENT-GROUP
664.description: note:Denotes a group of calibration parameters which are handled by the RTE as one data structure. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="McParameterElementGroup" stereotype:atpObject

665.name: MC-SUPPORT-DATA
665.description: note:Root element for all measurement and calibration support data related to one Implementation artifact on an ECU. There shall be one such element related to the RTE implementation (if it owns MC data) and a separate one for each module or component, which owns private MC data. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="McSupportData" stereotype:atpObject

666.name: MC-SW-EMULATION-METHOD-SUPPORT
666.description:
note:This denotes the method used by the RTE to handle the calibration data. It is published by the RTE generator and can be used e.g. to generate the corresponding emulation method in a Complex Driver.

According to the actual method given by the category attribute,  not all attributes are always needed:

* double pointered method: only baseReference is mandatory
* single pointered method: only referenceTable is mandatory
* initRam method: only elementGroup(s) are mandatory

Note: For single/double pointered method the group locations are implicitly accessed via the reference table and their location can be found from the initial values in the M1 model of the respective pointers. Therefore, the description of elementGroups is not needed in these cases.  Likewise, for double pointered method the reference table description can be accessed via the M1 model under baseReference. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="McSwEmulationMethodSupport" stereotype:atpObject

667.name: MEASURED-EXECUTION-TIME
667.description: note:Specifies the ExecutionTime which has been gathered using measurement means. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MeasuredExecutionTime" stereotype:atpObject

668.name: MEASURED-HEAP-USAGE
668.description: note:The heap usage has been measured. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MeasuredHeapUsage" stereotype:atpObject

669.name: MEASURED-STACK-USAGE
669.description: note:The stack usage has been measured. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MeasuredStackUsage" stereotype:atpObject

670.name: MEMORY-SECTION
670.description:
note:Provides a description of an abstract memory section used in the Implementation for code or data. It shall be declared by the Implementation Description of the module or component, which actually allocates the memory in its code. This means in case of data prototypes which are allocated by the RTE, that the generated Implementation Description of the RTE shall contain the corresponding MemorySections.

The attribute "symbol" (if symbol is missing: "shortName") defines the module or component specific section name used in the code. For details see the document "Specification of Memory Mapping".
Typically the section name is build according the pattern:

<SwAddrMethod shortName>[_<further specialization nominator>][_<alignment>] 
where
* '''[<SwAddrMethod shortName>]''' is the shortName of the referenced SwAddrMethod
* '''[_<further specialization nominator>]''' is an optional infix to indicate the specialization in the case that several MemorySections for different purpose of the same Implementation Description referring to the same or equally named SwAddrMethods. 
* '''[_<alignment>]''' is the alignment attributes value and is only applicable in the case that the memoryAllocationKeywordPolicy value of the referenced SwAddrMethod is set to addrMethodShortNameAndAlignment 

MemorySection used to Implement the code of RunnableEntitys and BswSchedulableEntitys shall have a symbol (if missing: shortName) identical to the referred SwAddrMethod to conform to the generated RTE header files.   

In addition to the section name described above, a prefix is used in the corresponding macro code in order to define a name space. This prefix is by default given by the shortName of the BswModuleDescription resp. the SwComponentType. It can be superseded by  the prefix attribute. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MemorySection" stereotype:atpObject

671.name: MEMORY-SECTION-LOCATION
671.description: note:Specifies in which hardware ProvidedMemorySegment the softwareMemorySection is located. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MemorySectionLocation" stereotype:atpObject

672.name: ML-FIGURE
672.description: note:This metaclass represents the ability to embed a figure. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MlFigure" stereotype:atpObject

673.name: ML-FORMULA
673.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a formula in a documentation. The formula can be expressed by various means. If more than one representation is available, they need to be consistent. The rendering system can use the representation which is most appropriate. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MlFormula" stereotype:atpObject

674.name: MODE-ACCESS-POINT
674.description:
note:A ModeAccessPoint is required by a RunnableEntity owned by a Mode Manager or Mode User.
Its semantics implies the ability to access the current mode (provided by the RTE)  of a ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype's ModeDeclarationGroup. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeAccessPoint" stereotype:atpObject

675.name: MODE-ACCESS-POINT-IDENT
675.description: note:This meta-class has been created to introduce the ability to become referenced into the meta-class ModeAccessPoint without breaking backwards compatibility. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeAccessPointIdent" stereotype:atpObject

676.name: MODE-DECLARATION
676.description: note:Declaration of one Mode. The name and semantics of a specific mode is not defined in the meta-model. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeDeclaration" stereotype:atpObject

677.name: MODE-DECLARATION-GROUP
677.description: note:A collection of Mode Declarations. Also, the initial mode is explicitly identified. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ModeDeclarationGroups";mmt.qualifiedName="ModeDeclarationGroup" stereotype:atpObject

678.name: MODE-DECLARATION-GROUP-PROTOTYPE
678.description: note:The ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype specifies a set of Modes (ModeDeclarationGroup) which is provided or required in the given context. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

679.name: MODE-DECLARATION-GROUP-PROTOTYPE-MAPPING
679.description: note:Defines the mapping of two particular ModeDeclarationGroupPrototypes (in the given context) that are unequally named and/or require a reference to a ModeDeclarationMappingSet in order to become compatible by definition of ModeDeclarationMappings. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeDeclarationGroupPrototypeMapping" stereotype:atpObject

680.name: MODE-DECLARATION-GROUP-PROTOTYPE-REF-CONDITIONAL
680.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

681.name: MODE-DECLARATION-MAPPING
681.description: note:This meta-class implements a concrete mapping of two ModeDeclarations. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeDeclarationMapping" stereotype:atpObject

682.name: MODE-DECLARATION-MAPPING-SET
682.description: note:This meta-class implements a container for ModeDeclarationGroupMappings tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PortInterfaceMappingSets";mmt.qualifiedName="ModeDeclarationMappingSet" stereotype:atpObject

683.name: MODE-DRIVEN-TRANSMISSION-MODE-CONDITION
683.description:
note:The condition defined by this class evaluates to true if one of the referenced modeDeclarations (OR associated) is active. All referenced modeDeclarations shall be from the same ModeDeclarationGroup.

The condition is used to define which TransmissionMode shall be activated using Com_SwitchIpduTxMode. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeDrivenTransmissionModeCondition" stereotype:atpObject

684.name: MODE-ERROR-BEHAVIOR
684.description: note:This represents the ability to define the error behavior in the context of mode handling. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeErrorBehavior" stereotype:atpObject

686.name: MODE-INTERFACE-MAPPING
686.description: note:Defines the mapping of ModeDeclarationGroupPrototypes in context of two different ModeInterfaces. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeInterfaceMapping" stereotype:atpObject

687.name: MODE-PORT-ANNOTATION
687.description: note:Annotation to a port used for calibration regarding a certain ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModePortAnnotation" stereotype:atpObject

688.name: MODE-REQUEST-TYPE-MAP
688.description: note:Specifies a mapping between a ModeDeclarationGroup and an ImplementationDataType. This ImplementationDataType shall be used to implement the ModeDeclarationGroup. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeRequestTypeMap" stereotype:atpObject

689.name: MODE-SWITCH-INTERFACE
689.description: note:A mode switch interface declares a ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype to be sent and received. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PortInterfaces";mmt.qualifiedName="ModeSwitchInterface" stereotype:atpObject

690.name: MODE-SWITCH-POINT
690.description: note:A ModeSwitchPoint is required by a RunnableEntity owned a Mode Manager. Its semantics implies the ability to initiate a mode switch. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeSwitchPoint" stereotype:atpObject

691.name: MODE-SWITCH-RECEIVER-COM-SPEC
691.description: note:Communication attributes of RPortPrototypes with respect to mode communication tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeSwitchReceiverComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

692.name: MODE-SWITCH-SENDER-COM-SPEC
692.description: note:Communication attributes of PPortPrototypes with respect to mode communication tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeSwitchSenderComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

693.name: MODE-SWITCHED-ACK-EVENT
693.description: note:The event is raised when the referenced modes have been received or an error occurs. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeSwitchedAckEvent" stereotype:atpObject

694.name: MODE-SWITCHED-ACK-REQUEST
694.description: note:Requests acknowledgements that a mode switch has been proceeded successfully tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeSwitchedAckRequest" stereotype:atpObject

695.name: MODE-TRANSITION
695.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to describe possible ModeTransitions in the context of a ModeDeclarationGroup. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ModeTransition" stereotype:atpObject

696.name: MODIFICATION
696.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability  to record what has changed in a document in comparison to its predecessor. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Modification" stereotype:atpObject

697.name: MSR-QUERY-ARG
697.description: note:This represents an argument to the query. Note that the arguments are not standardized and therefore subject to mutual agreement. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MsrQueryArg" stereotype:atpObject

698.name: MSR-QUERY-CHAPTER
698.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a query which yields a set of chapters as a result. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MsrQueryChapter" stereotype:atpObject

699.name: MSR-QUERY-P-1
699.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a query which yields the content of a topic as a result. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MsrQueryP1" stereotype:atpObject

700.name: MSR-QUERY-P-2
700.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a query which yields the content of a DocumentationBlock as a result. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MsrQueryP2" stereotype:atpObject

701.name: MSR-QUERY-PROPS
701.description: note:This metaclass represents the ability to specificy a query which yields some documentation text. The qualities of the result are determined by the context in which the query is used. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MsrQueryProps" stereotype:atpObject

702.name: MSR-QUERY-RESULT-CHAPTER
702.description: note:This metaclass represents the result of an msrquery which is a set of chapters. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MsrQueryResultChapter" stereotype:atpObject

703.name: MSR-QUERY-RESULT-TOPIC-1
703.description: note:This metaclass represents the ability to express the result of a query which is a set of topics. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MsrQueryResultTopic1" stereotype:atpObject

704.name: MSR-QUERY-TOPIC-1
704.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify a query which yields a set of topics as a result. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MsrQueryTopic1" stereotype:atpObject

705.name: MULTI-LANGUAGE-OVERVIEW-PARAGRAPH
705.description: note:This is the content of a multilingual paragraph in an overview item. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MultiLanguageOverviewParagraph" stereotype:atpObject

706.name: MULTI-LANGUAGE-PARAGRAPH
706.description: note:This is the content model of a multilingual paragraph in a documentation. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MultiLanguageParagraph" stereotype:atpObject

707.name: MULTI-LANGUAGE-PLAIN-TEXT
707.description: note:This is a multilingual plaint Text.It is intended to be rendered as a paragraph. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MultiLanguagePlainText" stereotype:atpObject

708.name: MULTI-LANGUAGE-VERBATIM
708.description: note:This class represents multilingual Verbatim. Verbatim means, that white-space is maintained. When Verbatim is rendered in PDF or Online media, white-space is obeyed. Blanks are rendered as well as newline characters. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MultiLanguageVerbatim" stereotype:atpObject

709.name: MULTIDIMENSIONAL-TIME
709.description:
note:This is used to specify a multidimensional time value based on ASAM CSE codes. It is specified by a code which defined the basis of the time and a scaling factor which finally determines the time value.

If for example the cseCode is 100 and the cseCodeFactor is 360, it represents 360 angular degrees.
If the cseCode is 2 and the cseCodeFactor is 50 it represents 50 microseconds tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MultidimensionalTime" stereotype:atpObject

710.name: MULTILANGUAGE-LONG-NAME
710.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify a long name which acts in the role of a headline. It is intended for human readers. Per language it should be around max 80 characters. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="MultilanguageLongName" stereotype:atpObject

711.name: MULTIPLEXED-I-PDU
711.description:
note:A MultiplexedPdu (i.e. NOT a COM I-PDU) contains a DynamicPart, an optional StaticPart and a selectorField. In case of multiplexing this IPdu is routed between the Pdu Multiplexer and the Interface Layer. 

A multiplexer is used to define variable parts within an IPdu that may carry different signals. The receivers of such a IPdu can determine which signalPdus are transmitted by evaluating the selector field, which carries a unique selector code for each sub-part. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Pdus";mmt.qualifiedName="MultiplexedIPdu" stereotype:atpObject

712.name: N-PDU
712.description:
note:This is a Pdu of the Transport Layer.
The main purpose of the TP Layer is to segment and reassemble IPdus. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Pdus";mmt.qualifiedName="NPdu" stereotype:atpObject

713.name: NETWORK-ENDPOINT
713.description: note:The network endpoint defines the network addressing (e.g. IP-Address or MAC multicast address). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NetworkEndpoint" stereotype:atpObject

714.name: NM-CONFIG
714.description: note:Contains the all configuration elements for AUTOSAR Nm. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="NmConfigs";mmt.qualifiedName="NmConfig" stereotype:atpObject

715.name: NM-COORDINATOR
715.description: note:A NM coordinator is an ECU, which is connected to at least two busses, and where the requirement exists that shutdown of NM of at least two of these busses (also referred to as coordinated busses) has to be performed synchronously. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NmCoordinator" stereotype:atpObject

716.name: NM-ECU
716.description: note:ECU on which NM is running. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NmEcu" stereotype:atpObject

718.name: NM-PDU-REF-CONDITIONAL
