718.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NmPdu" stereotype:atpObject

719.name: NONQUEUED-RECEIVER-COM-SPEC
719.description: note:Communication attributes specific to non-queued receiving. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NonqueuedReceiverComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

720.name: NONQUEUED-SENDER-COM-SPEC
720.description: note:Communication attributes for non-queued sender/receiver communication (sender side) tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NonqueuedSenderComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

721.name: NOTE
721.description:
note:This represents a note in a documentation, which may be used to highlight specific issues such as hints or caution notes.

N.B., Documentation notes can be nested recursively, even if this is not really intended. In case of nested notes e.g. the note icon of inner notes might be omitted while rendering the note. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Note" stereotype:atpObject

722.name: NUMERICAL-OR-TEXT
722.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to yield either a numerical or a string. A typical use case is that two or more instances of this meta-class are aggregated with a VariationPoint where some instances yield strings while other instances yield numerical depending on the resolution of the binding expression. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NumericalOrText" stereotype:atpObject

723.name: NUMERICAL-RULE-BASED-VALUE-SPECIFICATION
723.description: note:This meta-class is used to support a rule-based initialization approach for data types with an array-nature (ImplementationDataType of category ARRAY). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NumericalRuleBasedValueSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

724.name: NUMERICAL-VALUE-SPECIFICATION
724.description:
note:A numerical  ValueSpecification which is intended to be assigned to a Primitive data element.
Note that the numerical value is a variant, it can be computed by a formula. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NumericalValueSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

725.name: NUMERICAL-VALUE-VARIATION-POINT
725.description:
note:This class represents an attribute value variation point for Numerical attributes.

Note that this class might be used in the extended meta-model only. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NumericalValueVariationPoint" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

726.name: NV-BLOCK-DATA-MAPPING
726.description:
note:Defines the mapping between the VariableDataPrototypes in the NvBlockComponents ports and the VariableDataPrototypes of the RAM Block.

The data types of the referenced VariableDataPrototypes in the ports and the referenced sub-element (inside a CompositeDataType) of the VariableDataPrototype representing the RAM Block shall be compatible. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NvBlockDataMapping" stereotype:atpObject

727.name: NV-BLOCK-DESCRIPTOR
727.description: note:Specifies the properties of exactly on NVRAM Block. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NvBlockDescriptor" stereotype:atpObject

728.name: NV-BLOCK-NEEDS
728.description: note:Specifies the abstract needs on the configuration of a single NVRAM Block. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NvBlockNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

729.name: NV-BLOCK-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE
729.description: note:The NvBlockSwComponentType defines non volatile data which data can be shared between SwComponentPrototypes. The non volatile data of the NvBlockSwComponentType are accessible via provided and required ports. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwComponentTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="NvBlockSwComponentType" stereotype:atpObject

730.name: NV-DATA-INTERFACE
730.description: note:A non volatile data interface declares a number of VariableDataPrototypes to be exchanged between non volatile block components and atomic software components. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PortInterfaces";mmt.qualifiedName="NvDataInterface" stereotype:atpObject

731.name: NV-DATA-PORT-ANNOTATION
731.description: note:Annotation to a port regarding a certain VariableDataPrototype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NvDataPortAnnotation" stereotype:atpObject

732.name: NV-PROVIDE-COM-SPEC
732.description: note:Communication attributes of PPortPrototypes with respect to Nv data communication on the provided side. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NvProvideComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

733.name: NV-REQUIRE-COM-SPEC
733.description: note:Communication attributes of RPortPrototypes with respect to Nv data communication on the required side. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="NvRequireComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

734.name: OBD-CONTROL-SERVICE-NEEDS
734.description: note:Specifies the abstract needs of a component or module on the configuration of OBD Service 08 (request control of on-board system) in relation to a particular test-Identifier (TID) supported by this component or module. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ObdControlServiceNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

735.name: OBD-INFO-SERVICE-NEEDS
735.description: note:Specifies the abstract needs of a component or module on the configuration of OBD Services in relation to a given InfoType (OBD Service 09) which is supported by this component or module. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ObdInfoServiceNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

736.name: OBD-MONITOR-SERVICE-NEEDS
736.description: note:Specifies the abstract needs of a component or module on the configuration of OBD Services in relation to a particular on-board monitoring test supported by this component or module. (OBD Service 06). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ObdMonitorServiceNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

737.name: OBD-PID-SERVICE-NEEDS
737.description:
note:Specifies the abstract needs of a component or module on the configuration of OBD Services in relation to a particular PID (parameter identifier) which is supported by this component or module.

In case of using a client/server communicated value, the related value shall be communicated via the port referenced by asssignedPort. The details of this communication (e.g. appropriate naming conventions) are specified in the related software specifications (SWS). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ObdPidServiceNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

738.name: OBD-RATIO-SERVICE-NEEDS
738.description: note:Specifies the abstract needs of a component or module on the configuration of OBD Services in relation to a particular "ratio monitoring" which is supported by this component or module. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ObdRatioServiceNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

739.name: OFFSET-TIMING-CONSTRAINT
739.description:
note:Bounds the time offset between the occurrence of two timing events, without requiring a direct functional dependency between the source and the target.

If the target event occurs, it is expected to occur earliest with the minimum, and latest with the maximum offset relatively after the occurrence of the source event. Note: not every source event occurrence must be followed by a target event occurrence.

In contrast to LatencyTimingConstraint, there must not necessarily be a causal dependency between the source and target event. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="OffsetTimingConstraint" stereotype:atpObject

742.name: OPERATION-INVOKED-EVENT
742.description: note:The OperationInvokedEvent references the ClientServerOperation invoked by the client. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="OperationInvokedEvent" stereotype:atpObject

743.name: ORDERED-MASTER
743.description: note:Element in the network endpoint list. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="OrderedMaster" stereotype:atpObject

747.name: P-PORT-PROTOTYPE
747.description: note:Component port providing a certain port interface. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PPortPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

748.name: PR-PORT-PROTOTYPE
748.description: note:This kind of PortPrototype can take the role of both a required and a provided PortPrototype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PRPortPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

750.name: PARAMETER-ACCESS
750.description: note:The presence of a ParameterAccess implies that a RunnableEntity needs access to a ParameterDataPrototype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ParameterAccess" stereotype:atpObject

751.name: PARAMETER-DATA-PROTOTYPE
751.description: note:A parameter element used for parameter interface and internal behavior, supporting signal like parameter and characteristic value communication patterns and parameter and characteristic value definition. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ParameterDataPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

752.name: PARAMETER-IN-ATOMIC-SWC-TYPE-INSTANCE-REF
752.description: note:This class implements an instance reference which can be applied for variables as well as for parameters. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ParameterInAtomicSWCTypeInstanceRef" stereotype:atpObject,instanceRef

753.name: PARAMETER-INTERFACE
753.description: note:A parameter interface declares a number of parameter and characteristic values to be exchanged between parameter components and software components. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PortInterfaces";mmt.qualifiedName="ParameterInterface" stereotype:atpObject

754.name: PARAMETER-PORT-ANNOTATION
754.description: note:Annotation to a port used for calibration regarding a certain ParameterDataPrototype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ParameterPortAnnotation" stereotype:atpObject

755.name: PARAMETER-PROVIDE-COM-SPEC
755.description: note:"Communication" specification that applies to parameters on the provided side of a connection. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ParameterProvideComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

756.name: PARAMETER-REQUIRE-COM-SPEC
756.description: note:"Communication" specification that applies to parameters on the required side of a connection. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ParameterRequireComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

757.name: PARAMETER-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE
757.description: note:The ParameterSwComponentType defines parameters and characteristic values accessible via provided Ports. The provided values are the same for all connected SwComponentPrototypes tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwComponentTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="ParameterSwComponentType" stereotype:atpObject

758.name: PASS-THROUGH-SW-CONNECTOR
758.description: note:This kind of SwConnector can be used inside a CompositionSwComponentType to connect two delegation PortPrototypes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PassThroughSwConnector" stereotype:atpObject

759.name: PDU-MAPPING-DEFAULT-VALUE
759.description: note:Default Value which will be distributed if no I-Pdu has been received since last sending. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PduMappingDefaultValue" stereotype:atpObject

760.name: PDU-TO-FRAME-MAPPING
760.description: note:A PduToFrameMapping defines the composition of Pdus in each frame. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PduToFrameMapping" stereotype:atpObject,atpPrototype

761.name: PDU-TRIGGERING
761.description:
note:The PduTriggering describes on which channel the IPdu is transmitted.
The Pdu routing by the PduR is only allowed for subclasses of IPdu.

Depending on its relation to entities such channels and clusters it can be unambiguously deduced whether a fan-out is handled by the Pdu router or the Bus Interface. 

If the fan-out is specified between different clusters it shall be handled by the Pdu Router. If the fan-out is specified between different channels of the same cluster it shall be handled by the Bus Interface. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PduTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

762.name: PDU-TRIGGERING-REF-CONDITIONAL
762.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PduTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

763.name: PDUR-I-PDU-GROUP
763.description: note:The AUTOSAR PduR will enable and disable the sending of configurable groups of IPdus during runtime according to the AUTOSAR PduR specification. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PdurIPduGroups";mmt.qualifiedName="PdurIPduGroup" stereotype:atpObject

764.name: PER-INSTANCE-MEMORY
764.description: note:Defines a 'C' typed memory-block that needs to be available for each instance of the SW-component.  This is typically only useful if supportsMultipleInstantiation is set to "true" or if the software-component defines NVRAM access via permanent blocks. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PerInstanceMemory" stereotype:atpObject

765.name: PER-INSTANCE-MEMORY-SIZE
765.description: note:Resources needed by the allocation of PerInstanceMemory for each SWC instance. Note that these resources are not covered by an ObjectFileSection, because they are supposed to be allocated by the RTE. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PerInstanceMemorySize" stereotype:atpObject

766.name: PERIODIC-EVENT-TRIGGERING
766.description:
note:The PeriodicEventTriggering describes the behavior of an event with a strict periodic occurrence pattern, given by the period attribute.

Additionally, it is possible to soften the strictness of the periodic occurrence behavior by specifying a jitter, so that there can be a deviation from the period up to the size of the jitter. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PeriodicEventTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

767.name: PERMISSIBLE-SIGNAL-PATH
767.description:
note:The PermissibleSignalPath describes the way a data element shall take in the topology. The path is described by ordered references to PhysicalChannels. 

If more than one PermissibleSignalPath is defined for the same
signal/operation attributes, any of them can be chosen. Such a signal path can be a constraint for the communication matrix . This path describes that one data element should take path A (e.g. 1. CAN channel, 2. LIN channel) 
and not path B (1. CAN channel, FlexRay channel A). 

This has an effect on the frame generation and the frame path. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PermissibleSignalPath" stereotype:atpObject

768.name: PHYS-CONSTRS
768.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express physical constraints. Therefore it has (in opposite to InternalConstrs) a reference to a Unit. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PhysConstrs" stereotype:atpObject

769.name: PHYSICAL-DIMENSION
769.description:
note:This class represents a physical dimension.
If the physical dimension of two units is identical, then a conversion between them is possible. The conversion between units is related to the definition of the physical dimension.

Note that the equivalence of the exponents does not per se define the convertibility. For example Energy and Torque share the same exponents (Nm).

Please note further the value of an exponent does not necessarily have to be an integer number. It is also possible that the value yields a rational number, e.g. to compute the square root of a given physical quantity. In this case the exponent value would be a rational number where the numerator value is 1 and the denominator value is 2. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PhysicalDimensions";mmt.qualifiedName="PhysicalDimension" stereotype:atpObject

770.name: PHYSICAL-DIMENSION-MAPPING
770.description: note:This class represents a specific mapping between two PhysicalDimensions. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PhysicalDimensionMapping" stereotype:atpObject

771.name: PHYSICAL-DIMENSION-MAPPING-SET
771.description: note:This class represents a container for a list of mappings between PhysicalDimensions. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PhysicalDimensionMappingSets";mmt.qualifiedName="PhysicalDimensionMappingSet" stereotype:atpObject

772.name: PNC-MAPPING
772.description: note:Describes a mapping between one or several Virtual Function Clusters onto Partial Network Clusters. A Virtual Function Cluster is realized by a PortGroup. A Partial Network Cluster is realized by one or more IPduGroups. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PncMapping" stereotype:atpObject

773.name: PORT-API-OPTION
773.description: note:Options how to generate the signatures of calls for an AtomicSwComponentType in order to communicate over a PortPrototype (for calls into a RunnableEntity as well as for calls from a RunnableEntity to the PortPrototype). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PortAPIOption" stereotype:atpObject

774.name: PORT-DEFINED-ARGUMENT-VALUE
774.description: note:A PortDefinedArgumentValue is passed to a RunnableEntity dealing with the ClientServerOperations provided by a given PortPrototype. Note that this is restricted to PPortPrototypes of a ClientServerInterface. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PortDefinedArgumentValue" stereotype:atpObject

775.name: PORT-GROUP
775.description: note:Group of ports which share a common functionality, e.g. need specific network resources. This information shall be available on the VFB level in order to delegate it properly via compositions. When propagated into the ECU extract, this information is used as input for the configuration of Services like the Communication Manager. A PortGroup is defined locally in a component (which can be a composition) and refers to the "outer" ports belonging to the group as well as to the "inner" groups which propagate  this group into the components which are part of a composition. A PortGroup within an atomic SWC cannot be linked to inner groups. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PortGroup" stereotype:atpObject

777.name: PORT-INTERFACE-BLUEPRINT-MAPPING
777.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to map two PortInterfaces of which one acts as the blueprint for the other. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="PortInterfaceBlueprintMapping" stereotype:atpObject

778.name: PORT-INTERFACE-MAPPING-SET
778.description: note:Specifies a set of (one or more) PortInterfaceMappings. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PortInterfaceMappingSets";mmt.qualifiedName="PortInterfaceMappingSet" stereotype:atpObject

779.name: PORT-PROTOTYPE-BLUEPRINT
779.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a blueprint of a PortPrototype by referring to a particular PortInterface. This blueprint can then be used as a guidance to create particular PortPrototypes which are defined according to this blueprint. By this it is possible to standardize application interfaces without the need to also standardize software-components with PortPrototypes typed by the standardized PortInterfaces. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PortPrototypeBlueprints";mmt.qualifiedName="PortPrototypeBlueprint" stereotype:atpObject

780.name: PORT-PROTOTYPE-BLUEPRINT-INIT-VALUE
780.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express init values in PortPrototypeBlueprints. These init values act as a kind of blueprint from which for example proper ComSpecs can be derived. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PortPrototypeBlueprintInitValue" stereotype:atpObject

781.name: PORT-PROTOTYPE-BLUEPRINT-MAPPING
781.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to map a PortPrototypeBlueprint to a PortProtoype of which one acts as the blueprint for the other. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="PortPrototypeBlueprintMapping" stereotype:atpObject

782.name: PORT-PROTOTYPE-REF-CONDITIONAL
782.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PortPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

783.name: POSITIVE-INTEGER-VALUE-VARIATION-POINT
783.description:
note:This class represents an attribute value variation point for positive Integer attributes.

Note that this class might be used in the extended meta-model only. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PositiveIntegerValueVariationPoint" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

784.name: POST-BUILD-VARIANT-CONDITION
784.description:
note:This class specifies the value which must be assigned to a particular variant criterion in order to bind the variation point. If multiple criterion/value pairs are specified, they shall all match to bind the variation point.

In other words binding can be represented by

  (criterion1 == value1) && (condition2 == value2) ... tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PostBuildVariantCondition" stereotype:atpObject

785.name: POST-BUILD-VARIANT-CRITERION
785.description: note:This class specifies one particular PostBuildVariantSelector. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PostBuildVariantCriterions";mmt.qualifiedName="PostBuildVariantCriterion" stereotype:atpObject

786.name: POST-BUILD-VARIANT-CRITERION-VALUE
786.description: note:This class specifies a the value which must be assigned to a particular variant criterion in order to bind the variation point. If multiple criterion/value pairs are specified, they all must must match to bind the variation point. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PostBuildVariantCriterionValue" stereotype:atpObject

787.name: POST-BUILD-VARIANT-CRITERION-VALUE-SET
787.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to denote one set of postBuildVariantCriterionValues. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PostBuildVariantCriterionValueSets";mmt.qualifiedName="PostBuildVariantCriterionValueSet" stereotype:atpObject

788.name: PREDEFINED-CHAPTER
788.description: note:This represents a predefined chapter. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PredefinedChapter" stereotype:atpObject

789.name: PREDEFINED-VARIANT
789.description: note:This specifies one predefined variant. It is characterized by the union of all system constant values and post-build variant criterion values aggregated within all referenced system constant value sets and post build variant criterion value sets plus the value sets of the included variants. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PredefinedVariants";mmt.qualifiedName="PredefinedVariant" stereotype:atpObject

790.name: PRM-CHAR
790.description: note:This metaclass represents the ability to express the characteristics of one particular parameter. It can be exressed as numerical or as text parameter (provided as subclasses of PrmCharContents) tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PrmChar" stereotype:atpObject

791.name: PRM-CHAR-ABS-TOL
791.description: note:The parameter is specified as ablolute value with a tolerance. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PrmCharAbsTol" stereotype:atpObject

795.description: note:This metaclass represents the ability to specify a parameter table. It can be used e.g. to specify parameter tables in a data sheet. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Prms" stereotype:atpObject

796.name: PROVIDED-SERVICE-INSTANCE
796.description: note:Service instances that are provided by the ECU that is connected via the ApplicationEndpoint to a CommunicationConnector. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ProvidedServiceInstance" stereotype:atpObject

797.name: QUEUED-RECEIVER-COM-SPEC
797.description: note:Communication attributes specific to queued receiving. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="QueuedReceiverComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

798.name: QUEUED-SENDER-COM-SPEC
798.description: note:Communication attributes specific to distribution of  events (PPortPrototype, SenderReceiverInterface and dataElement carries an "event"). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="QueuedSenderComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

803.name: R-PORT-PROTOTYPE
803.description: note:Component port requiring a certain port interface. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RPortPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

806.name: RAPID-PROTOTYPING-SCENARIO
806.description: note:This meta class provides the ability to describe a Rapid Prototyping Scenario. Such a Rapid Prototyping Scenario consist out of two main aspects, the description of the byPassPoints and the relation to an rptHook. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="RapidPrototypingScenarios";mmt.qualifiedName="RapidPrototypingScenario" stereotype:atpObject

807.name: RECEIVER-ANNOTATION
807.description: note:Annotation of a receiver port, specifying properties of data elements that don't affect communication or generation of the RTE. The given attributes are requirements on the required data. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ReceiverAnnotation" stereotype:atpObject

808.name: RECORD-VALUE-SPECIFICATION
808.description: note:Specifies the values for a record. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RecordValueSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

note:This primitive denotes a name based reference. For detailed syntax see the xsd.pattern.

* first slash (relative or absolute reference) [optional]
* Identifier  [required]
* a sequence of slashes and Identifiers [optional]

This primitive is used by the meta-model tools to create the references. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Ref";xml.xsd.customType="REF";xml.xsd.pattern="/?[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,127}(/[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,127})*";xml.xsd.type="string" stereotype:atpObject,primitive

810.name: REFERENCE-BASE
810.description: note:This meta-class establishes a basis for relative references. Reference bases are identified by the shortLabel which must be unique in the current package. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ReferenceBase" stereotype:atpObject

811.name: REFERENCE-VALUE-SPECIFICATION
811.description: note:Specifies a reference to a data prototype to be used as an initial value for a pointer in the software. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ReferenceValueSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

812.name: REFERRABLE-REF-CONDITIONAL
812.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Referrable" stereotype:atpObject

814.name: REMOTING-TECHNOLOGY
814.description:
note:This element is deprecated and will be removed in future. 

Old description: Defines the used remoting Technology. tag:atp.Status="obsolete";mmt.qualifiedName="RemotingTechnology" stereotype:atpObject

815.name: REQUEST-RESPONSE-DELAY
815.description: note:Time to wait before answering the query. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RequestResponseDelay" stereotype:atpObject

816.name: RESOURCE-CONSUMPTION
816.description: note:Description of consumed resources by one implementation of a software. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ResourceConsumption" stereotype:atpObject

817.name: ROLE-BASED-BSW-MODULE-ENTRY-ASSIGNMENT
817.description:
note:This class specifies an assignment of a role to a particular BswModuleEntry (usually a configurable callback). 

With this assignment, the role of the callback is mapped to a specific ServiceNeeds element, so that a tool is able to create appropriate configuration values for the module that implements the AUTOSAR Service. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RoleBasedBswModuleEntryAssignment" stereotype:atpObject

818.name: ROLE-BASED-DATA-ASSIGNMENT
818.description:
note:This class specifies an assignment of a role to a particular data object in the SwcInternalBehavior of a software component (or in the BswModuleBehavior of a module or cluster) in the context of an AUTOSAR Service.

With this assignment, the role of the data can be mapped to a specific ServiceNeeds element, so that a tool is able to create the correct access. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RoleBasedDataAssignment" stereotype:atpObject

819.name: ROLE-BASED-DATA-TYPE-ASSIGNMENT
819.description:
note:This class specifies an assignment of a role to a particular data type of a software component (or in the BswModuleBehavior of a module or cluster) in the context of an AUTOSAR Service.

With this assignment, the role of the data type can be mapped to a specific ServiceNeeds element, so that a tool is able to create the correct access. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RoleBasedDataTypeAssignment" stereotype:atpObject

820.name: ROLE-BASED-MC-DATA-ASSIGNMENT
820.description:
note:This meta-class allows to define links that specify logical relationships between single McDataInstances. The details on the existence and semantics of such links are not standardized.

Possible Use Case: 
Rapid Prototyping solutions in which additional communication buffers and switches are implemented  in the RTE that allow to switch between the usage of the original and the bypass buffers. The different buffers and the switch can be represented by McDataInstances (in order to be accessed by MC tools) which have relationships to each other. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RoleBasedMcDataAssignment" stereotype:atpObject

821.name: ROLE-BASED-PORT-ASSIGNMENT
821.description: note:This class specifies an assignment of a role to a particular service port (RPortPrototype or PPortPrototype) of an AtomicSwComponentType. With this assignment, the role of the service port can be mapped to a specific ServiceNeeds element, so that a tool is able to create the correct connector. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RoleBasedPortAssignment" stereotype:atpObject

822.name: ROOT-SW-COMPOSITION-PROTOTYPE
822.description:
note:The RootSwCompositionPrototype represents the top-level-composition of software components within a given System. According to the use case of the System, this may for example be the a more or less complete VFB description, the software of a System Extract or the software of a flat ECU Extract with only atomic SWCs. 

Therefore the RootSwComposition will only occasionally contain all atomic software components that are used in a complete VFB System. The OEM is primarily interested in the required functionality and the interfaces defining the integration of the Software Component into the System. The internal structure of such a component contains often substantial intellectual property of a supplier. Therefore a top-level software composition will often contain empty compositions which represent subsystems. 

The contained SwComponentPrototypes are fully specified by their SwComponentTypes (including PortPrototypes, PortInterfaces, VariableDataPrototypes, SwcInternalBehavior etc.), and their ports are interconnected using SwConnectorPrototypes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RootSwCompositionPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

823.name: ROUGH-ESTIMATE-HEAP-USAGE
823.description: note:Rough estimation of the heap usage. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RoughEstimateHeapUsage" stereotype:atpObject

824.name: ROUGH-ESTIMATE-OF-EXECUTION-TIME
824.description: note:Provides a description of a rough estimate on the ExecutionTime. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RoughEstimateOfExecutionTime" stereotype:atpObject

825.name: ROUGH-ESTIMATE-STACK-USAGE
825.description: note:Rough estimation of the stack usage. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RoughEstimateStackUsage" stereotype:atpObject

826.name: ROW
826.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express one row in a table. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Row" stereotype:atpObject

827.name: RPT-CONTAINER
827.description:
note:This meta class defines a byPassPoint and the relation to a rptHook.

Additionally it may contain further rptContainers if the byPassPoint is not atomic. For example a byPassPoint refereing to a RunnableEntity may contain rptContainers referring to the data access points of the RunnableEntity. 

The RptContainer structure on M1 shall follow the M1 structure of the Software Component Descriptions. The category attribute denotes which level of the Software Component Description is annotated. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RptContainer" stereotype:atpObject

828.name: RPT-HOOK
828.description: note:This meta class provide the ability to describe a rapid prototyping hook. This can either be described by an other AUTOSAR system with the category RPT_SYSTEM or as a non AUTOSAR software. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RptHook" stereotype:atpObject

830.name: RTP-TP
830.description: note:RTP over UDP or over TCP as transport protocol. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RtpTp" stereotype:atpObject

831.name: RULE-ARGUMENTS
831.description: note:This represents the arguments for a rule-based value specification. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RuleArguments" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

832.name: RULE-BASED-AXIS-CONT
832.description:
note:This represents the values for the axis of a compound primitive (curve, map).

For standard and fix axes,  SwAxisCont contains the values of the axis directly. 

The axis values of SwAxisCont with the category CURVE_AXIS, COM_AXIS, RES_AXIS are for display only. For editing and processing, only the values in the related GroupAxis are binding. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RuleBasedAxisCont" stereotype:atpObject

833.name: RULE-BASED-VALUE-CONT
833.description: note:This represents the values of a compound primitive (CURVE, MAP, CUBOID, CUBE_4, CUBE_5, VAL_BLK) or an array. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RuleBasedValueCont" stereotype:atpObject

834.name: RULE-BASED-VALUE-SPECIFICATION
834.description: note:This meta-class is used to support a rule-based initialization approach for data types with an array-nature (ApplicationArrayDataType and ImplementationDataType of category ARRAY) or a compound ApplicationPrimitiveDataType (which also boils down to an array-nature). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RuleBasedValueSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

835.name: RUNNABLE-ENTITY
835.description: note:A RunnableEntity represents the smallest code-fragment that is provided by an AtomicSwComponentType and are executed under control of the RTE. RunnableEntities are for instance set up to respond to data reception or operation invocation on a server. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RunnableEntity" stereotype:atpObject

836.name: RUNNABLE-ENTITY-ARGUMENT
836.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to provide specific information regarding the arguments to a RunnableEntity. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RunnableEntityArgument" stereotype:atpObject

837.name: RUNNABLE-ENTITY-GROUP
837.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to define a collection of RunnableEntities. The collection can be nested. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RunnableEntityGroup" stereotype:atpObject

838.name: RUNNABLE-ENTITY-IN-COMPOSITION-INSTANCE-REF
838.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to define an InstanceRef to a RunnableEntity in the context of a CompositionSwComponentType. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RunnableEntityInCompositionInstanceRef" stereotype:atpObject,instanceRef

839.name: RX-IDENTIFIER-RANGE
839.description: note:Optional definition of a CanId range to reduce the effort of specifying every possible FrameTriggering within the defined Id range during reception. All frames received within a range are mapped to the same Pdu that is passed to a upper layer module (e.g. Nm, CDD, PduR). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RxIdentifierRange" stereotype:atpObject

840.name: SOMEIP-TRANSFORMATION-DESCRIPTION
840.description: note:The SOMEIPTransformationDescription is used to specify SOME/IP transformer specific attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SOMEIPTransformationDescription" stereotype:atpObject

841.name: SOMEIP-TRANSFORMATION-I-SIGNAL-PROPS
841.description: note:The class SOMEIPTransformationISignalProps specifies ISignal specific configuration properties for SOME/IP transformer attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SOMEIPTransformationISignalProps" stereotype:atpObject

842.name: SOMEIP-TRANSFORMATION-I-SIGNAL-PROPS-CONDITIONAL
842.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SOMEIPTransformationISignalPropsConditional" stereotype:atpObject

843.name: SAVE-CONFIGURATION-ENTRY
843.description: note:This service is used to notify a slave node to store its configuration. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SaveConfigurationEntry" stereotype:atpObject

844.name: SCALE-CONSTR

845.name: SD
845.description: note:This class represents a primitive element in a special data group. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Sd" stereotype:atpObject

846.name: SD-CLIENT-CONFIG

847.name: SD-SERVER-CONFIG
847.description: note:Server configuration for Service-Discovery. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SdServerConfig" stereotype:atpObject

848.name: SDF
848.description: note:This class represents a numerical value in a special data group which may be subject to variability. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Sdf" stereotype:atpObject

849.name: SDG
849.description:
note:Sdg (SpecialDataGroup) is a generic model which can be used to keep arbitrary information which is not explicitly modeled in the meta-model. 

Sdg can have various contents as defined by sdgContentsType. Special Data should only be used moderately since all elements should be defined in the meta-model. 

Thereby SDG should be considered as a temporary solution when no explicit model is available. If an sdgCaption is available, it is possible to establish a reference to the sdg structure. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Sdg" stereotype:atpObject

850.name: SDG-CAPTION
850.description: note:This meta-class represents the caption of a special data group. This allows to have some parts of special data as identifiable. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SdgCaption" stereotype:atpObject

851.name: SDG-CONTENTS
851.description: note:This meta-class represents the possible contents of a special data group. It can be an arbitrary mix of references, of primitive special data and nested special data groups. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SdgContents" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

852.name: SECTION-NAME-PREFIX
852.description: note:A prefix to be used for generated code artifacts defining a memory section name in the source code of the using module. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SectionNamePrefix" stereotype:atpObject

853.name: SECURE-COMMUNICATION-PROPS
853.description: note:Properties used to configure SecuredIPdus. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SecureCommunicationProps" stereotype:atpObject

854.name: SECURED-I-PDU
854.description: note:IPdu that contains payload of an Authentic IPdu supplemented by additional Authentication Information (Freshness Counter and an Authenticator). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SecuredIPdu" stereotype:atpObject

855.name: SEGMENT-POSITION
855.description:
note:The StaticPart and the DynamicPart can be
separated in multiple segments within the multiplexed PDU. 

The ISignalIPdus are copied bit by bit into the MultiplexedIPdu. If the space of the first segment is 5 bits large than the first 5 bits of the ISignalIPdu are copied into this first segment and so on. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SegmentPosition" stereotype:atpObject

856.name: SENDER-ANNOTATION
856.description: note:Annotation of a sender port, specifying properties of data elements that don't affect communication or generation of the RTE. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SenderAnnotation" stereotype:atpObject

857.name: SENDER-REC-ARRAY-ELEMENT-MAPPING
857.description:
note:The SenderRecArrayElement may be a primitive one or a composite one. If the element is primitive, it will be mapped to the SystemSignal (multiplicity 1). If the VariableDataPrototype that is referenced by SenderReceiverToSignalGroupMapping is typed by an ApplicationDataType the reference to the ApplicationArrayElement shall be used. If the VariableDataPrototype is typed by the ImplementationDataType the reference to the ImplementationArrayElement shall be used. 

If the element is composite, there will be no mapping to the SystemSignal (multiplicity 0). In this case the ArrayElementMapping element will aggregate the TypeMapping element. In that way also the composite datatypes can be mapped to SystemSignals. 

Regardless whether composite or primitive array element is mapped the indexed element always needs to be specified. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SenderRecArrayElementMapping" stereotype:atpObject

858.name: SENDER-REC-ARRAY-TYPE-MAPPING
858.description: note:If the ApplicationCompositeDataType is an Array, the "ArrayTypeMapping" will be used. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SenderRecArrayTypeMapping" stereotype:atpObject

859.name: SENDER-REC-RECORD-ELEMENT-MAPPING
859.description:
note:Mapping of a primitive record element to a SystemSignal. If the VariableDataPrototype that is referenced by SenderReceiverToSignalGroupMapping is typed by an ApplicationDataType the reference applicationRecordElement shall be used. If the VariableDataPrototype is typed by the ImplementationDataType the reference implementationRecordElement shall be used. Either the implementationRecordElement or applicationRecordElement reference shall be used. 

If the element is composite, there will be no mapping to the SystemSignal (multiplicity 0). In this case the RecordElementMapping element will aggregate the complexTypeMapping element. In that way also the composite datatypes can be mapped to SystemSignals. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SenderRecRecordElementMapping" stereotype:atpObject

860.name: SENDER-REC-RECORD-TYPE-MAPPING
860.description: note:If the ApplicationCompositeDataType is a Record, the "RecordTypeMapping" will be used. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SenderRecRecordTypeMapping" stereotype:atpObject

861.name: SENDER-RECEIVER-COMPOSITE-ELEMENT-TO-SIGNAL-MAPPING
861.description: note:Mapping of an Variable Data Prototype which is aggregated within a composite datatype to a SystemSignal (only one element of the composite data type is mapped). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SenderReceiverCompositeElementToSignalMapping" stereotype:atpObject

862.name: SENDER-RECEIVER-INTERFACE
862.description: note:A sender/receiver interface declares a number of data elements to be sent and received. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PortInterfaces";mmt.qualifiedName="SenderReceiverInterface" stereotype:atpObject

863.name: SENDER-RECEIVER-TO-SIGNAL-GROUP-MAPPING
863.description: note:Mapping of a sender receiver communication data element with a composite datatype to a signal group. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SenderReceiverToSignalGroupMapping" stereotype:atpObject

864.name: SENDER-RECEIVER-TO-SIGNAL-MAPPING
864.description: note:Mapping of a sender receiver communication data element with a primitive datatype to a signal. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SenderReceiverToSignalMapping" stereotype:atpObject

865.name: SENSOR-ACTUATOR-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE
865.description: note:The SensorActuatorSwComponentType introduces the possibility to link from the software representation of a sensor/actuator to its hardware description provided by the ECU Resource Template. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwComponentTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="SensorActuatorSwComponentType" stereotype:atpObject

866.name: SEPARATE-SIGNAL-PATH
866.description:
note:The SeparateSignalPath describes that two SwcToSwcSignals and/or SwcToSwcOperationArguments must not take the same way (Signal Path) in the topology (e.g. Redundancy). 
This means that the signals are not allowed to share 
even a single physical channel in their path. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SeparateSignalPath" stereotype:atpObject

867.name: SEQUENCE-COUNTER-MAPPING
867.description:
note:The purpose of sequence counters is to map a response to the correct request of a known client.

The SequenceCounter is mapped to the requestGroup and to the responseGroup. tag:atp.Status="removed";mmt.qualifiedName="SequenceCounterMapping" stereotype:atpObject

868.name: SERIALIZATION-TECHNOLOGY
868.description:
note:<font color="#0f0f0f">This element is deprecated and will be removed in future. This information is replaced by the TransformationTechnology element.</font>
<font color="#0f0f0f">
</font><font color="#0f0f0f">Old description: Identifies the used serialization technology. The corresponding serialization plugin has to be provided on each affected ECU by the integrator. </font> tag:atp.Status="obsolete";atp.recommendedPackage="SerializationTechnologies";mmt.qualifiedName="SerializationTechnology" stereotype:atpObject

869.name: SERVER-COM-SPEC
869.description: note:Communication attributes for a server port (PPortPrototype and ClientServerInterface). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ServerComSpec" stereotype:atpObject

870.name: SERVICE-PROXY-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE
870.description:
note:This class provides the ability to express a software-component which provides access to an internal service for remote ECUs. It acts as a proxy for the service providing access to the service.

An important use case is the request of vehicle mode switches: Such requests can be communicated via sender-receiver interfaces across ECU boundaries, but the mode manager being responsible to perform the mode switches is an AUTOSAR Service which is located in the Basic Software and is not visible in the VFB view. To handle this situation, a ServiceProxySwComponentType will act as proxy for the mode manager. It will have R-Ports to be connected with the mode requestors on VFB level and Service-Ports to be connected with the local mode manager at ECU integration time.

Apart from the semantics, a ServiceProxySwComponentType has these specific properties:
* A prototype of it can be mapped to more than one ECUs in the system description.
* Exactly one additional instance of it will be created in the ECU-Extract per ECU to which the prototype has been mapped.
* For remote communication, it can have only R-Ports with sender-receiver interfaces and 1:n semantics.
* There shall be no connectors between two prototypes of any ServiceProxySwComponentType. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwComponentTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="ServiceProxySwComponentType" stereotype:atpObject

871.name: SERVICE-SW-COMPONENT-TYPE
871.description: note:ServiceSwComponentType is used for configuring services for a given ECU. Instances of this class are only to be created in ECU Configuration phase for the specific purpose of the service configuration. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwComponentTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="ServiceSwComponentType" stereotype:atpObject

872.name: SHORT-NAME-FRAGMENT
872.description: note:This class describes how the Referrable.shortName is composed of several shortNameFragments. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ShortNameFragment" stereotype:atpObject

873.name: SIGNAL-I-PDU-COUNTER
873.description: note:A PduCounter is included in a predefined set of Pdus and used to ensure that a sequence of Pdus is maintained. The counter is incremented when a Pdu is transmitted. The receivers check if the received Pdu is the next one in sequence. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SignalIPduCounter" stereotype:atpObject

874.name: SIGNAL-I-PDU-REPLICATION
874.description: note:PduReplication is a form of redundancy where the data content of one ISignalIPdu (source) is transmitted inside a set of replica ISignalIPdus. These ISignalIPdus (copies) have different Pdu IDs, identical PduCounters, identical data content and are transmitted with the same frequency. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SignalIPduReplication" stereotype:atpObject

875.name: SIMULATED-EXECUTION-TIME
875.description: note:Specifies the ExecutionTime which has been gathered using simulation means. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SimulatedExecutionTime" stereotype:atpObject

877.name: SINGLE-LANGUAGE-UNIT-NAMES
877.description: note:This represents the ability to express a display name. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SingleLanguageUnitNames" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

878.name: SO-AD-CONFIG
878.description: note:SoAd Configuration for one specific Physical Channel. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SoAdConfig" stereotype:atpObject

879.name: SO-AD-ROUTING-GROUP
879.description: note:Routing of Pdus in the SoAd can be activated or deactivated. The ShortName of this element shall contain the RoutingGroupId. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SoAdRoutingGroups";mmt.qualifiedName="SoAdRoutingGroup" stereotype:atpObject

880.name: SOCKET-ADDRESS
880.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability represent a socket address towards the rest of the meta-model. The actual semantics of the represented socket address, however, is contributed by aggregation of ApplicationEndpoint. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SocketAddress" stereotype:atpObject

881.name: SOCKET-CONNECTION
881.description: note:The SoAd serves as a (De)Multiplexer between different PDU sources and the TCP/IP stack. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SocketConnection" stereotype:atpObject

882.name: SOCKET-CONNECTION-BUNDLE
882.description: note:This elements groups SocketConnections, i.e. specifies socket connections belonging to the bundle and describes properties which are common for all socket connections in the bundle. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SocketConnectionBundle" stereotype:atpObject

883.name: SOCKET-CONNECTION-IPDU-IDENTIFIER
883.description: note:An Identifier is required in case of one port per ECU communication where multiple Pdus are transmitted over the same connection. If only one IPdu is transmitted over the connetion this attribute can be ignored. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SocketConnectionIpduIdentifier" stereotype:atpObject

884.name: SOFTWARE-CONTEXT
884.description: note:Specifies the context of the software for this resource consumption. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SoftwareContext" stereotype:atpObject

885.name: SPORADIC-EVENT-TRIGGERING
885.description: note:The SporadicEventTriggering describes the behavior of an event which occurs occasionally or singly. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SporadicEventTriggering" stereotype:atpObject

886.name: STATIC-PART
886.description: note:Some parts/signals of the I-PDU may be the same regardless of the selector field. Such a part is called static part. The static part is optional. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="StaticPart" stereotype:atpObject

887.name: STD
887.description: note:This represents a reference to external standards. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Std" stereotype:atpObject

888.name: STRUCTURED-REQ
888.description:
note:This represents a structured requirement. This is intended for a case where specific requirements for features are collected.

Note that this can be rendered as a labeled list. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="StructuredReq" stereotype:atpObject

889.name: SUB-ELEMENT-MAPPING
889.description: note:This meta-class allows for the definition of mappings of elements of a composite data type. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SubElementMapping" stereotype:atpObject

890.name: SUPERVISED-ENTITY-NEEDS
890.description: note:Specifies the abstract needs on the configuration of the Watchdog Manager for one specific Supervised Entity. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SupervisedEntityNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

891.name: SW-ADDR-METHOD
891.description: note:Used to assign a common addressing method, e.g. common memory section, to data or code objects. These objects could actually live in different modules or components. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwAddrMethods";mmt.qualifiedName="SwAddrMethod" stereotype:atpObject

892.name: SW-AXIS-CONT
892.description:
note:This represents the values for the axis of a compound primitive (curve, map).

For standard and fix axes,  SwAxisCont contains the values of the axis directly. 

The axis values of SwAxisCont with the category CURVE_AXIS, COM_AXIS, RES_AXIS are for display only. For editing and processing, only the values in the related GroupAxis are binding. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwAxisCont" stereotype:atpObject

893.name: SW-AXIS-GENERIC
893.description:
note:This meta-class defines a generic axis. In a generic axis the axispoints points are calculated in the ECU. 

The ECU is equipped with a fixed calculation algorithm. Parameters for the algorithm can be stored in the data component of the ECU. Therefore these parameters are specified in the data declaration, not in the calibration data. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwAxisGeneric" stereotype:atpObject

894.name: SW-AXIS-GROUPED
894.description: note:An SwAxisGrouped is an axis which is shared between multiple calibration parameters. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwAxisGrouped" stereotype:atpObject

895.name: SW-AXIS-INDIVIDUAL

895.description: note:This meta-class describes an axis integrated into a parameter (field etc.). The integration makes this individual to each parameter. The so-called grouped axis represents the counterpart to this. It is conceived as an independent parameter (see class SwAxisGrouped). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwAxisIndividual" stereotype:atpObject

896.name: SW-AXIS-TYPE
896.description:
note:This meta-class represents a specific axis calculation strategy. No formal specification is given, due to the fact that it is possible to use arbitrary algorithms for calculating axis-points. 

Instead, the algorithm is described verbally but the parameters are specified formally with respect to their names and constraints. As a result, SwAxisType mainly reserves appropriate keywords. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwAxisTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="SwAxisType" stereotype:atpObject

897.name: SW-BASE-TYPE
897.description: note:This meta-class represents a base type used within ECU software. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="BaseTypes";mmt.qualifiedName="SwBaseType" stereotype:atpObject

898.name: SW-BIT-REPRESENTATION
898.description: note:Description of the structure of a bit variable: Comprises of the bitPosition in a memory object (e.g. swHostVariable, which stands parallel to swBitRepresentation) and the numberOfBits . In this way, interrelated memory areas can be described. Non-related memory areas are not supported. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwBitRepresentation" stereotype:atpObject

899.name: SW-CALPRM-AXIS
899.description: note:This element specifies an individual input parameter axis (abscissa). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwCalprmAxis" stereotype:atpObject

900.name: SW-CALPRM-AXIS-SET
900.description: note:This element specifies the input parameter axes (abscissas) of parameters (and variables, if these are used adaptively). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwCalprmAxisSet" stereotype:atpObject

901.name: SW-CALPRM-REF-PROXY
901.description: note:Wrapper class for different kinds of references to a calibration parameter. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwCalprmRefProxy" stereotype:atpObject

902.name: SW-COMPONENT-DOCUMENTATION
902.description: note:This class specifies the ability to write dedicated documentation to a component type according to ASAM FSX. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwComponentDocumentation" stereotype:atpObject

903.name: SW-COMPONENT-PROTOTYPE
903.description: note:Role of a software component within a composition. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwComponentPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

904.name: SW-DATA-DEF-PROPS
904.description:
note:This class is a collection of properties relevant for data objects under various aspects. One could consider this class as a "pattern of inheritance by aggregation". The properties can be applied to all objects of all classes in which SwDataDefProps is aggregated.

Note that not all of the attributes or associated elements are useful all of the time. Hence, the process definition (e.g. expressed with an OCL or a Document Control Instance MSR-DCI) has the task of implementing limitations.

SwDataDefProps covers various aspects:

* Structure of the data element for calibration use cases: is it a single value, a curve, or a map, but also the recordLayouts which specify how such elements are mapped/converted to the DataTypes in the programming language (or in AUTOSAR). This is mainly expressed by properties like swRecordLayout and swCalprmAxisSet 

* Implementation aspects, mainly expressed by swImplPolicy, swVariableAccessImplPolicy, swAddrMethod, swPointerTagetProps, baseType, implementationDataType and additionalNativeTypeQualifier

* Access policy for the MCD system, mainly expressed by swCalibrationAccess 

* Semantics of the data element, mainly expressed by compuMethod and/or unit, dataConstr, invalidValue

* Code generation policy provided by swRecordLayout tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwDataDefProps";vh.latestBindingTime="codeGenerationTime" stereotype:atpObject
