905.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwDataDefPropsConditional" stereotype:atpObject

906.name: SW-DATA-DEPENDENCY
906.description:
note:This element describes the interdependencies of data objects, e.g. variables and parameters. 

Use cases:
* Calculate the value of a calibration parameter (by the MCD system) from the value(s) of other calibration parameters.
* Virtual data - that means the data object is not directly in the ecu and this property describes how the "virtual variable" can be computed from the real ones (by the MCD system). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwDataDependency" stereotype:atpObject

907.name: SW-DATA-DEPENDENCY-ARGS
907.description: note:This element specifies the elements used in a SwDataDependency. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwDataDependencyArgs" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

908.name: SW-GENERIC-AXIS-PARAM
908.description:
note:This meta-class describes a specific parameter of a generic axis. The name of the parameter is defined through a reference to a parameter type defined on a corresponding axis type.

The value of the parameter is given here in case that it is not changeable during calibration. Example is shift / offset in a fixed axis. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwGenericAxisParam" stereotype:atpObject

909.name: SW-GENERIC-AXIS-PARAM-TYPE
909.description:
note:This meta-class describes a generic axis parameter type, namely:

* Plausibility checks can be specified via dataConstr.

* Textual description (desc), as a formal description is not of any use, due to the large variety of possibilities.

* If this parameter contains structures, these can be simulated through the recursive use of SwGenericAxisParamTypes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwGenericAxisParamType" stereotype:atpObject

910.name: SW-POINTER-TARGET-PROPS
910.description:
note:This element defines, that the data object (which is specified by the aggregating element) contains a reference to another data object or to a function in the CPU code. This corresponds to a pointer in the C-language.

The attributes of this element describe the category and the detailed properties of the target which is either a data description or a function signature. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwPointerTargetProps" stereotype:atpObject

911.name: SW-RECORD-LAYOUT
911.description: note:Defines how the data objects (variables, calibration parameters etc.) are to be stored in the ECU memory. As an example, this definition specifies the sequence of axis points in the ECU memory. Iterations through axis values are stored within the sub-elements swRecordLayoutGroup. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwRecordLayouts";mmt.qualifiedName="SwRecordLayout" stereotype:atpObject

912.name: SW-RECORD-LAYOUT-GROUP
912.description: note:Specifies how a record layout is set up. Using SwRecordLayoutGroup it recursively models iterations through axis values. The subelement swRecordLayoutGroupContentType may reference other SwRecordLayouts, SwRecordLayoutVs and SwRecordLayoutGroups for the modeled record layout. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwRecordLayoutGroup" stereotype:atpObject

913.name: SW-RECORD-LAYOUT-GROUP-CONTENT
913.description: note:This is the contents of a RecordLayout which is inserted for every iteration. Note that since this is atpMixed, multiple properties can be inserted for each iteration. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwRecordLayoutGroupContent" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

914.name: SW-RECORD-LAYOUT-V
914.description: note:This element specifies which values are stored for the current SwRecordLayoutGroup. If no baseType is present, the SwBaseType referenced initially in the parent SwRecordLayoutGroup is valid. The specification of swRecordLayoutVAxis gives the axis of the values which shall be stored in accordance with the current record layout SwRecordLayoutGroup. In swRecordLayoutVProp one can specify the information which shall be stored. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwRecordLayoutV" stereotype:atpObject

915.name: SW-SERVICE-ARG
915.description:
note:Specifies the properties of a data object exchanged during the call of an SwService, e.g. an argument or a return value.

The SwServiceArg can also be used in the argument list of a C-macro. For this purpose the category shall be set to "MACRO". A reference to implementationDataType can optional be added if the actual argument has an implementationDataType. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwServiceArg" stereotype:atpObject

916.name: SW-SYSTEMCONST
916.description:
note:This element defines a system constant which serves an input to 
select a particular variation point. In particular a system constant serves as an operand of the binding function (swSyscond) in a Variation point.

Note that the binding process can only happen  if a value was assigned to to the referenced system constants. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwSystemconsts";mmt.qualifiedName="SwSystemconst" stereotype:atpObject

917.name: SW-SYSTEMCONST-VALUE
917.description: note:This meta-class assigns a particular value to a system constant. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwSystemconstValue" stereotype:atpObject

918.name: SW-SYSTEMCONSTANT-VALUE-SET
918.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify a set of system constant values. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwSystemconstantValueSets";mmt.qualifiedName="SwSystemconstantValueSet" stereotype:atpObject

919.name: SW-TEXT-PROPS
919.description: note:This meta-class expresses particular properties applicable to strings in variables or calibration parameters. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwTextProps" stereotype:atpObject

920.name: SW-VALUE-CONT
920.description: note:This metaclass represents the content of one particular SwInstance. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwValueCont" stereotype:atpObject

921.name: SW-VALUES
921.description:
note:This meta-class represents a list of values. These values can either be the input values of a curve (abscissa values) or the associated values (ordinate values). 

In case of multidimensional structures, the values are ordered such that the lowest index runs the fastest. In particular for maps and cuboids etc. the resulting long value list can be subsectioned using ValueGroup. But the processing needs to be done as if vg is not there.

Note that numerical values and textual values should not be mixed. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwValues" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

922.name: SW-VARIABLE-REF-PROXY
922.description: note:Proxy class for several kinds of references to a variable. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwVariableRefProxy" stereotype:atpObject

923.name: SWC-BSW-MAPPING
923.description: note:Maps an SwcInternalBehavior to an BswInternalBehavior. This is required to coordinate the API generation and the scheduling for AUTOSAR Service Components, ECU Abstraction Components and Complex Driver Components by the RTE and the BSW scheduling mechanisms. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwcBswMappings";mmt.qualifiedName="SwcBswMapping" stereotype:atpObject

924.name: SWC-BSW-RUNNABLE-MAPPING
924.description: note:Maps a BswModuleEntity to a RunnableEntity if it is implemented as part of a BSW module (in the case of an AUTOSAR Service, a Complex Driver or an ECU Abstraction). The mapping can be used by a tool to find relevant information on the behavior, e.g. whether the bswEntity shall be running in interrupt context. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcBswRunnableMapping" stereotype:atpObject

925.name: SWC-BSW-SYNCHRONIZED-MODE-GROUP-PROTOTYPE
925.description: note:Synchronizes a mode group provided by a component via a port with a mode group provided by a BSW module or cluster. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcBswSynchronizedModeGroupPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

926.name: SWC-BSW-SYNCHRONIZED-TRIGGER
926.description: note:Synchronizes a Trigger provided by a component via a port with a Trigger provided by a BSW module or cluster. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcBswSynchronizedTrigger" stereotype:atpObject

927.name: SWC-IMPLEMENTATION
927.description: note:This meta-class represents a specialization of the general Implementation meta-class with respect to the usage in application software. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SwcImplementations";mmt.qualifiedName="SwcImplementation" stereotype:atpObject

928.name: SWC-INTERNAL-BEHAVIOR
928.description: note:The SwcInternalBehavior of an AtomicSwComponentType describes the relevant aspects of the software-component with respect to the RTE, i.e. the RunnableEntities and the RTEEvents they respond to. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcInternalBehavior" stereotype:atpObject

929.name: SWC-MODE-MANAGER-ERROR-EVENT
929.description: note:This represents the ability to react on errors occurring during mode handling. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcModeManagerErrorEvent" stereotype:atpObject

930.name: SWC-MODE-SWITCH-EVENT
930.description: note:This event is raised upon a received mode change. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcModeSwitchEvent" stereotype:atpObject

931.name: SWC-SERVICE-DEPENDENCY
931.description: note:Specialization of ServiceDependency in the context of an SwcInternalBehavior. It allows to associate ports, port groups and (in special cases) data defined for an atomic software component  to a given ServiceNeeds element. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcServiceDependency" stereotype:atpObject

933.name: SWC-TIMING
933.description:
note:The SwcTiming is used to describe the timing of an atomic software component.

TimingDescriptions aggregated by SwcTiming are restricted to event chains referring to events which are derived from the classes TDEventVfb and TDEventSwcInternalBehavior. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="TimingExtensions";mmt.qualifiedName="SwcTiming" stereotype:atpObject

934.name: SWC-TO-ECU-MAPPING
934.description: note:Map software components to a specific ECU Instance and optionally to a processing unit and to an EcuPartition. For each combination of ECUInstance and the optional ProcessingUnit and the optional EcuPartition and the optional SensorActuator only one SwcToEcuMapping shall be used. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcToEcuMapping" stereotype:atpObject

935.name: SWC-TO-ECU-MAPPING-CONSTRAINT
935.description: note:The System Constraint Description has to describe dedicated and exclusive mapping of SW-Cs to one or more ECUs. Dedicated mapping means that the SW-C can only be mapped to the ECUs it is dedicated to. Exclusive Mapping means that the SW-C cannot be mapped to the ECUs it is excluded from. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcToEcuMappingConstraint" stereotype:atpObject

936.name: SWC-TO-IMPL-MAPPING
936.description: note:Map instances of an AtomicSwComponentType to a specific Implementation. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcToImplMapping" stereotype:atpObject

937.name: SWC-TO-SWC-OPERATION-ARGUMENTS
937.description: note:The SwcToSwcOperationArguments describes the information (client server operation arguments, plus the operation identification, if required) that are exchanged between two SW Components from exactly one client to one server, or from one server back to one client. The direction attribute defines which direction is described. If direction == IN, all arguments sent from the client to the server are described by the SwcToSwcOperationArguments, in direction == OUT, it's the arguments sent back from server to client. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcToSwcOperationArguments" stereotype:atpObject

938.name: SWC-TO-SWC-SIGNAL
938.description: note:The SwcToSwcSignal describes the information (data element) that is exchanged between two SW Components. On the SWC Level it is possible that a SW Component sends one data element from one P-Port to two different SW Components (1:n Communication). The SwcToSwcSignal describes exactly the information which is exchanged between one P-Port of a SW Component and one R-Port of another SW Component. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SwcToSwcSignal" stereotype:atpObject

939.name: SYMBOL-PROPS
939.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to attach with the symbol attribute a symbolic name that is conform to C language requirements to another meta-class, e.g. AtomicSwComponentType, that is a potential subject to a name clash on the level of RTE source code. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SymbolProps" stereotype:atpObject

940.name: SYMBOL-STRING
940.description: note:This meta-class has the ability to contain a string plus an additional namePattern. Please note that this meta-class has only been introduced to fix an issue with the backwards compatibility between R4.0.3 and R4.1.1 in the context of McDataInstance tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SymbolString";xml.xsd.customType="SYMBOL-STRING";xml.xsd.type="string" stereotype:atpObject,primitive

941.name: SYMBOLIC-NAME-PROPS
941.description: note:This meta-class can be taken to contribute to the creation of symbolic name values. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SymbolicNameProps" stereotype:atpObject

942.name: SYNC-TIME-BASE-MGR-USER-NEEDS
942.description: note:Specifies the needs on the configuration of the Synchronized Time-base Manager for one time-base. This class currently contains no attributes. An instance of this class is used to find out which ports of a software-component belong to this time-base in order to group the request and response ports of the same time-base. The actual time-base value is stored in the PortDefinedArgumentValue of the respective port specification. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SyncTimeBaseMgrUserNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

943.name: SYNCHRONIZATION-TIMING-CONSTRAINT
943.description:
note:This constraint is used to restrict the timing behavior of different, but correlated events or event chains, with regard to synchronization.

Thereby, in case of imposing a synchronization timing constraint on events or event chains the following two scenarios are supported:

1) [synchronizationConstraintType=responseSynchronization] Events: An arbitrary number of correlated events which play the role of responses shall occur synchronously with respect to a predefined tolerance. Event Chains: An arbitrary number of correlated event chains with a common stimulus, but different responses, where the responses shall occur synchronously with respect to a predefined tolerance.

2) [synchronizationConstraintType=stimulusSynchronization] Events: An arbitrary number of correlated events which play the role of stimuli shall occur synchronously with respect to a predefined tolerance. Event Chains: An arbitrary number of correlated event chains with a common response, but different stimuli, where the stimuli shall occur synchronously with respect to a predefined tolerance.

In case of imposing a synchronization timing constraint on events the following two scenarios are supported:

1) [eventOccurrenceKind=singleOccurrence] Any of the events shall occur only once in the given time interval.

2) [eventOccurrenceKind=multipleOccurrences] Any of the events may occur more than once in the given time interval. In other words multiple occurrences of an event within the given time interval are permitted. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SynchronizationTimingConstraint" stereotype:atpObject

944.name: SYNCHRONOUS-SERVER-CALL-POINT
944.description: note:This means that the RunnableEntity is supposed to perform a  blocking wait for a response from the server. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SynchronousServerCallPoint" stereotype:atpObject

945.name: SYSTEM
945.description:
note:The top level element of the System Description.
The System description defines five major elements: Topology, Software, Communication, Mapping and Mapping Constraints.

The System element directly aggregates the elements describing the Software, Mapping and Mapping Constraints; it contains a reference to an ASAM FIBEX description specifying Communication and Topology. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Systems";mmt.qualifiedName="System" stereotype:atpObject

946.name: SYSTEM-MAPPING
946.description: note:The system mapping aggregates all mapping aspects (mapping of SW components to ECUs, mapping of data elements to signals, and mapping constraints). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SystemMapping" stereotype:atpObject

947.name: SYSTEM-SIGNAL
947.description: note:The system signal represents the communication system's view of data exchanged between SW components which reside on different ECUs. The system signals allow to represent this communication in a flattened structure, with exactly one system signal defined for each data element prototype sent and received by connected SW component instances. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SystemSignals";mmt.qualifiedName="SystemSignal" stereotype:atpObject

948.name: SYSTEM-SIGNAL-GROUP
948.description:
note:A signal group refers to a set of signals that must always be kept together. A signal group is used to guarantee the atomic transfer of AUTOSAR composite data types.  

The SystemSignalGroup defines a signal grouping on VFB level. On cluster level the Signal grouping is described by the ISignalGroup element. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="SystemSignalGroups";mmt.qualifiedName="SystemSignalGroup" stereotype:atpObject

949.name: SYSTEM-TIMING
949.description:
note:A model element used to refine timing descriptions and constraints (from a VfbTiming) at System level, utilizing information about topology, software deployment, and signal mapping described in the System Template.

TimingDescriptions aggregated by SystemTiming are restricted to events which are derived from the class TDEventVfb, TDEventSwcInternalBehavior and TDEventCom. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="TimingExtensions";mmt.qualifiedName="SystemTiming" stereotype:atpObject

950.name: TD-EVENT-BSW-INTERNAL-BEHAVIOR
950.description: note:This is used to describe timing events related to the BswInternalBehavior of a BSW module. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventBswInternalBehavior" stereotype:atpObject

951.name: TD-EVENT-BSW-MODE-DECLARATION
951.description: note:This is used to describe timing events related to the mode communication on BSW level. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventBswModeDeclaration" stereotype:atpObject

952.name: TD-EVENT-BSW-MODULE
952.description: note:This is used to describe timing events related to the interaction between BSW modules. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventBswModule" stereotype:atpObject

953.name: TD-EVENT-COMPLEX
953.description:
note:This is used to describe complex timing events.

The context of a complex timing event either is described informally, e.g. using the documentation block, or is described formally by the associated TDEventOccurrenceExpression. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventComplex" stereotype:atpObject

954.name: TD-EVENT-FR-CLUSTER-CYCLE-START
954.description: note:This is used to describe the timing event related to a point in time where a communication cycle starts on a FlexRay cluster. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventFrClusterCycleStart" stereotype:atpObject

955.name: TD-EVENT-FRAME
955.description: note:This is used to describe timing events related to the exchange of frames between the communication controller and the bus specific (FlexRay / CAN / LIN) Interface BSW module. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventFrame" stereotype:atpObject

956.name: TD-EVENT-I-PDU
956.description: note:This is used to describe timing events related to the exchange of I-PDUs between the bus specific (FlexRay / CAN / LIN) Interface BSW module and COM. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventIPdu" stereotype:atpObject

957.name: TD-EVENT-I-SIGNAL
957.description: note:This is used to describe timing events related to the exchange of I-Signals between COM and RTE. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventISignal" stereotype:atpObject

958.name: TD-EVENT-MODE-DECLARATION
958.description: note:This is used to describe timing events related to mode switch communication at VFB level. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventModeDeclaration" stereotype:atpObject

959.name: TD-EVENT-OCCURRENCE-EXPRESSION
959.description:
note:This is used to specify a filter on the occurrences of TimingDescriptionEvents by means of a TDEventOccurrenceExpressionFormula.
Filter criteria can be variable and argument values, i.e. the timing event only occurs for specific values, as well as the temporal characteristics of the occurrences of arbitrary timing events. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventOccurrenceExpression" stereotype:atpObject

960.name: TD-EVENT-OCCURRENCE-EXPRESSION-FORMULA
960.description:
note:This is an extension of the FormulaExpression for the AUTOSAR Timing Extensions.

A TDEventOccurrenceExpressionFormula provides the means to express the temporal characteristics of timing event occurrences in correlation with specific variable and argument values.

The formal definition of the extended functions (ExtUnaryFunctions) is described in detail in the AUTOSAR Timing Extensions. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventOccurrenceExpressionFormula" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

961.name: TD-EVENT-OPERATION
961.description: note:This is used to describe timing events related to client-server communication at VFB level. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventOperation" stereotype:atpObject

962.name: TD-EVENT-SWC-INTERNAL-BEHAVIOR
962.description: note:This is used to describe timing events related to the SwcInternalBehavior of an AtomicSwComponentType. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventSwcInternalBehavior" stereotype:atpObject

963.name: TD-EVENT-SWC-INTERNAL-BEHAVIOR-REFERENCE
963.description: note:This is used to reference timing description events related to the Software Component (SW-C) view which are specified in other timing views. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventSwcInternalBehaviorReference" stereotype:atpObject

964.name: TD-EVENT-TT-CAN-CYCLE-START
964.description: note:This is used to describe the timing event related to a point in time where a communication cycle starts on a TTCAN cluster. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventTTCanCycleStart" stereotype:atpObject

965.name: TD-EVENT-TRIGGER
965.description: note:This is used to describe timing events related to triggers at VFB level. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventTrigger" stereotype:atpObject

966.name: TD-EVENT-VARIABLE-DATA-PROTOTYPE
966.description: note:This is used to describe timing events related to sender-receiver communication at VFB level. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventVariableDataPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

967.name: TD-EVENT-VFB-REFERENCE
967.description: note:This is used to reference timing description events related to the Virtual Function Bus (VFB) view which are specified in other timing views. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TDEventVfbReference" stereotype:atpObject

968.name: TABLE
968.description:
note:This class implements an exchange table according to OASIS Technical Resolution TR 9503:1995.

http://www.oasis-open.org/specs/a503.htm tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Table" stereotype:atpObject

969.name: TAG-WITH-OPTIONAL-VALUE
969.description: note:A tagged value is a combination of a tag (key) and a value that gives supplementary information that is attached to a model element. Please note that keys without a value are allowed. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TagWithOptionalValue" stereotype:atpObject

970.name: TARGET-I-PDU-REF
970.description: note:Target destination of the referencing mapping. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TargetIPduRef" stereotype:atpObject

971.name: TBODY
971.description: note:This meta-class represents a part within a table group. Such a part can be the table head, the table body or the table foot. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Tbody" stereotype:atpObject

972.name: TCP-TP
972.description: note:Content Model for TCP configuration. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TcpTp" stereotype:atpObject

973.name: TEXT-TABLE-MAPPING
973.description: note:Defines the mapping of two DataPrototypes typed by AutosarDataTypes that refer to CompuMethods of category TEXTTABLE, SCALE_LINEAR_AND_TEXTTABLE or BITFIELD_TEXTTABLE. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TextTableMapping" stereotype:atpObject

974.name: TEXT-TABLE-VALUE-PAIR
974.description: note:Defines a pair of text values which are translated into each other. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TextTableValuePair" stereotype:atpObject

975.name: TEXT-VALUE-SPECIFICATION
975.description: note:The purpose of TextValueSpecification is to define the labels that correspond to enumeration values. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TextValueSpecification" stereotype:atpObject

976.name: TGROUP
976.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to denote a table section. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Tgroup" stereotype:atpObject

977.name: TIME-RANGE-TYPE
977.description: note:The timeRange can be specified with the value attribute. Optionally a tolerance can be defined. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TimeRangeType" stereotype:atpObject

978.name: TIME-SYNC-CLIENT-CONFIGURATION
978.description: note:Defines the configuration of the time synchronisation client. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TimeSyncClientConfiguration" stereotype:atpObject

979.name: TIME-SYNC-SERVER-CONFIGURATION
979.description: note:Defines the configuration of the time synchronisation server. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TimeSyncServerConfiguration" stereotype:atpObject

980.name: TIME-SYNCHRONIZATION
980.description: note:Defines the servers / clients in a time synchronised network. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TimeSynchronization" stereotype:atpObject

981.name: TIMING-DESCRIPTION-EVENT-CHAIN
981.description: note:An event chain describes the causal order for a set of functionally dependent timing events. Each event chain has a well defined stimulus and response, which describe its start and end point. Furthermore, it can be hierarchically decomposed into an arbitrary number of sub-chains, so called ''event chain segments''. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TimingDescriptionEventChain" stereotype:atpObject

982.name: TIMING-EVENT
982.description: note:TimingEvent references the RunnableEntity that need to be started in response to the TimingEvent tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TimingEvent" stereotype:atpObject

983.name: TOPIC-1
983.description:
note:This meta-class represents a topic of a documentation. Topics are similar to chapters but they cannot be nested. 

They also do not appear in the table of content. Topics can be used to produce intermediate headlines thus structuring a chapter internally. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Topic1" stereotype:atpObject

984.name: TOPIC-CONTENT
984.description: note:This meta-class represents the content of a topic. It is mainly a documentation block, but can also be a table. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TopicContent" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

985.name: TOPIC-CONTENT-OR-MSR-QUERY
985.description: note:This meta-class represents a topic or a topic content which is generated using queries. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TopicContentOrMsrQuery" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

986.name: TOPIC-OR-MSR-QUERY
986.description: note:This class provides the alternative of a Topic with an MsrQuery which delivers a topic. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TopicOrMsrQuery" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

987.name: TP-ADDRESS
987.description: note:An ECUs TP address on the referenced channel. This represents the diagnostic Address. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TpAddress" stereotype:atpObject

988.name: TP-CONNECTION-IDENT
988.description: note:This meta-class is created to add the ability to become the target of a reference to the non-Referrable TpConnection. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TpConnectionIdent" stereotype:atpObject

989.name: TP-PORT
989.description: note:Dynamic or direct assignment of a PortNumber. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TpPort" stereotype:atpObject

990.name: TRACEABLE-TEXT
990.description:
note:This meta-class represents the ability to denote a traceable text item such as requirements etc.

The following approach appliles:

* '''shortName''' represents the tag for tracing
* '''longName''' represents the head line
* '''category''' represents the kind of the tagged text tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TraceableText" stereotype:atpObject

991.name: TRANSFORMATION-TECHNOLOGY
991.description: note:A TransformationTechnology is a transformer inside a transformer chain. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TransformationTechnology";xml.namePlural="TRANSFORMATION-TECHNOLOGIES" stereotype:atpObject

992.name: TRANSFORMER-HARD-ERROR-EVENT
992.description: note:The event is raised when data are received which should trigger a Client/Server operation or an external trigger but during transformation of the data a hard transformer error occurred. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TransformerHardErrorEvent" stereotype:atpObject

993.name: TRANSMISSION-ACKNOWLEDGEMENT-REQUEST
993.description: note:Requests transmission acknowledgement that data has been sent successfully. Success/failure is reported via a SendPoint of a RunnableEntity. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TransmissionAcknowledgementRequest" stereotype:atpObject

994.name: TRANSMISSION-MODE-CONDITION
994.description:
note:Possibility to attach a condition to each signal within an I-PDU.

If at least one condition evaluates to true, TRANSMISSION MODE True shall be used for this I-Pdu. In all other cases, the TRANSMISSION MODE FALSE shall be used. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TransmissionModeCondition" stereotype:atpObject

995.name: TRANSMISSION-MODE-DECLARATION
995.description:
note:AUTOSAR COM provides the possibility to define two different TRANSMISSION MODES (True and False) for each I-PDU.

As TransmissionMode selector the signal content can be evaluated via transmissionModeCondition (implemented directly in the COM module) or mode conditions can be defined with the modeDrivenTrueCondition or modeDrivenFalseCondition (evaluated by BswM and invoking Com_SwitchIpduTxMode COM API). If modeDrivenTrueCondition and modeDrivenFalseCondition are defined they shall never evaluate to true both at the same time. 

The mixing of Transmission Mode Switch via API and signal value is not allowed. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TransmissionModeDeclaration" stereotype:atpObject

996.name: TRANSMISSION-MODE-TIMING
996.description:
note:If the COM Transmission Mode is false the timing is aggregated by the TransmissionModeTiming element in the role of transmissionModeFalseTiming. If the COM Transmission Mode is true the timing is aggregated by the TransmissionModeTiming element in the role of transmissionModeTrueTiming.  

COM supports the following Transmission Modes: 
Periodic (Cyclic Timing)
Direct /n-times (EventControlledTiming)
Mixed (Cyclic and EventControlledTiming are assigned)
None (no timing is assigned) tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TransmissionModeTiming" stereotype:atpObject

997.name: TRIGGER
997.description: note:A trigger which is provided (i.e. released) or required (i.e. used to activate something) in the given context. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Trigger" stereotype:atpObject

998.name: TRIGGER-I-PDU-SEND-CONDITION
998.description:
note:The condition defined by this class evaluates to true if one of the referenced modeDeclarations (OR associated) is active. All referenced modeDeclarations shall be from the same ModeDeclarationGroup.

The condition is used to define when the Pdu is triggered with the Com_TriggerIPDUSend API call. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TriggerIPduSendCondition" stereotype:atpObject

1000.name: TRIGGER-INTERFACE
1000.description: note:A trigger interface declares a number of triggers that can be sent by an trigger source. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="PortInterfaces";mmt.qualifiedName="TriggerInterface" stereotype:atpObject

1001.name: TRIGGER-INTERFACE-MAPPING
1001.description: note:Defines the mapping of unequal named Triggers in context of two different TriggerInterfaces. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TriggerInterfaceMapping" stereotype:atpObject

1002.name: TRIGGER-MAPPING
1002.description: note:Defines the mapping of two particular unequally named Triggers in the given context. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TriggerMapping" stereotype:atpObject

1003.name: TRIGGER-PORT-ANNOTATION
1003.description: note:Annotation to a port used for calibration regarding a certain Trigger. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TriggerPortAnnotation" stereotype:atpObject

1004.name: TRIGGER-REF-CONDITIONAL
1004.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Trigger" stereotype:atpObject

1005.name: TRIGGER-TO-SIGNAL-MAPPING
1005.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to map a trigger to a SystemSignal of size 0. The Trigger does not transport any other information than its existence, therefore the limitation in terms of signal length. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TriggerToSignalMapping" stereotype:atpObject

1006.name: TT
1006.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express specific technical terms.  The kind of term is denoted in the attribute "type". tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Tt" stereotype:atpObject

1007.name: TTCAN-ABSOLUTELY-SCHEDULED-TIMING
1007.description:
note:Each frame in TTCAN is identified by its slot id and communication cycle. A description is provided by the usage of AbsolutelyScheduledTiming. 

A frame can be sent multiple times within one communication cycle. For describing this case multiple AbsolutelyScheduledTimings have to be used. The main use case would be that a frame is sent twice within one communication cycle. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TtcanAbsolutelyScheduledTiming" stereotype:atpObject

1008.name: TTCAN-CLUSTER
1008.description: note:TTCAN bus specific cluster attributes. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="CommunicationClusters";mmt.qualifiedName="TtcanCluster" stereotype:atpObject

1009.name: TTCAN-CLUSTER-CONDITIONAL
1009.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TtcanClusterConditional" stereotype:atpObject

1010.description: note:TTCAN bus specific communication connector attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TtcanCommunicationConnector" stereotype:atpObject

1011.name: TTCAN-COMMUNICATION-CONTROLLER
1011.description: note:TTCAN bus specific communication port attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TtcanCommunicationController" stereotype:atpObject

1012.name: TTCAN-COMMUNICATION-CONTROLLER-CONDITIONAL
1012.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="TtcanCommunicationControllerConditional" stereotype:atpObject

1015.description: note:Udp attributes that are valid for each of the referenced (coupled) UdpNm clusters. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UdpNmClusterCoupling" stereotype:atpObject

1016.name: UDP-NM-ECU
1016.description: note:Udp NM specific ECU attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UdpNmEcu" stereotype:atpObject

1017.name: UDP-NM-NODE
1017.description: note:Udp specific NM Node attributes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UdpNmNode" stereotype:atpObject

1018.name: UDP-TP
1018.description: note:Content Model for UDP configuration. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UdpTp" stereotype:atpObject

1019.name: UNASSIGN-FRAME-ID
1019.description: note:Schedule entry for an Unassign Frame Id master request where the protected identifier is assigned the value 0x40. This will disable reception/transmission of a previously dynamically assigned frame identifier. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UnassignFrameId" stereotype:atpObject

1020.name: UNIT
1020.description:
note:This is a physical measurement unit. All units that might be defined should stem from SI units. In order to convert one unit into another factor and offset are defined. For the calculation from SI-unit to the defined unit the factor (factorSiToUnit ) and the offset (offsetSiToUnit ) are applied:

unit = siUnit * factorSiToUnit + offsetSiToUnit 

For the calculation from a unit to SI-unit the reciprocal of the factor (factorSiToUnit ) and the negation of the offset (offsetSiToUnit ) are applied:

siUnit = (unit - offsetSiToUnit) / factorSiToUnit tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Units";mmt.qualifiedName="Unit" stereotype:atpObject

1021.name: UNIT-GROUP
1021.description:
note:This meta-class represents the ability to specify a logical grouping of units.The category denotes the unit system that the referenced units are associated to. 

In this way, e.g. country-specific unit systems (CATEGORY="COUNTRY") can be defined as well as specific unit systems for certain application domains. 

In the same way a group of equivalent units, can be defined which are used in different countries, by setting CATEGORY="EQUIV_UNITS".  KmPerHour and MilesPerHour could such be combined to one group named "vehicle_speed". The unit MeterPerSec would not belong to this group because it is normally not used for vehicle speed. But all of the mentioned units could be combined to one group named "speed".

Note that the UnitGroup does not ensure the physical compliance of the units. This is maintained by the physical dimension. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="UnitGroups";mmt.qualifiedName="UnitGroup" stereotype:atpObject

1022.name: UNLIMITED-INTEGER-VALUE-VARIATION-POINT
1022.description:
note:This class represents an attribute value variation point for unlimited Integer attributes.

Note that this class might be used in the extended meta-model only. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UnlimitedIntegerValueVariationPoint" stereotype:atpMixedString,atpObject

1023.name: URL
1023.description: note:This meta-class specifies an Uniform Resource Locator (URL). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Url" stereotype:atpObject

1024.name: USER-DEFINED-CLUSTER
1024.description: note:This element allows the modelling of arbitrary Communication Clusters (e.g. bus systems that are not supported by AUTOSAR). tag:atp.recommendedPackage="CommunicationClusters";mmt.qualifiedName="UserDefinedCluster" stereotype:atpObject

1025.name: USER-DEFINED-CLUSTER-CONDITIONAL
1025.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UserDefinedClusterConditional" stereotype:atpObject

1026.name: USER-DEFINED-COMMUNICATION-CONNECTOR

1028.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UserDefinedCommunicationControllerConditional" stereotype:atpObject

1029.name: USER-DEFINED-ETHERNET-FRAME
1029.description: note:UserDefinedEthernetFrame allows the description of a frame-based communication to Complex Drivers that are located above the EthDrv. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UserDefinedEthernetFrame" stereotype:atpObject

1030.name: USER-DEFINED-I-PDU
1030.description: note:UserDefinedIPdu allows to describe PDU-based communication over Complex Drivers. If a new BSW module is added above the PduR (e.g. a Diagnostic Service ) then this IPdu element shall be used to describe the communication. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Pdus";mmt.qualifiedName="UserDefinedIPdu" stereotype:atpObject

1031.name: USER-DEFINED-PDU
1031.description: note:UserDefinedPdu allows to describe PDU-based communication over Complex Drivers. If a new BSW module is added above the BusIf (e.g. a new Nm module) then this Pdu element shall be used to describe the communication. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="Pdus";mmt.qualifiedName="UserDefinedPdu" stereotype:atpObject

1032.name: USER-DEFINED-PHYSICAL-CHANNEL
1032.description: note:This element allows the modelling of arbitrary Physical Channels. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UserDefinedPhysicalChannel" stereotype:atpObject

1033.name: USER-DEFINED-TRANSFORMATION-COM-SPEC-PROPS
1033.description: note:The UserDefinedTransformationComSpecProps is used to specify port specific configuration properties for custom transformers. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UserDefinedTransformationComSpecProps" stereotype:atpObject

1034.name: USER-DEFINED-TRANSFORMATION-DESCRIPTION
1034.description: note:The UserDefinedTransformationDescription is used to specify details and documentation for custom transformers. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UserDefinedTransformationDescription" stereotype:atpObject

1035.name: USER-DEFINED-TRANSFORMATION-I-SIGNAL-PROPS
1035.description: note:The UserDefinedTransformationISignalProps is used to specify ISignal specific configuration properties for custom transformers. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UserDefinedTransformationISignalProps" stereotype:atpObject

1036.name: USER-DEFINED-TRANSFORMATION-I-SIGNAL-PROPS-CONDITIONAL
1036.description: note:This element was generated/modified due to an atpVariation stereotype. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UserDefinedTransformationISignalPropsConditional" stereotype:atpObject

1037.name: VALUE-GROUP
1037.description: note:This element enables valules  to be grouped. It can be used to perform row and column-orientated groupings, so that these can be rendered properly e.g. as a table. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ValueGroup" stereotype:atpObject

1038.name: VALUE-LIST
1038.description: note:This is a generic list of numerical values. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ValueList" stereotype:atpMixed,atpObject

1039.name: VARIABLE-ACCESS
1039.description:
note:The presence of a VariableAccess implies that a RunnableEntity needs access to a VariableDataPrototype. 

The kind of access is specified by the role in which the class is used. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="VariableAccess" stereotype:atpObject

1041.name: VARIABLE-AND-PARAMETER-INTERFACE-MAPPING
1041.description: note:Defines the mapping of VariableDataPrototypes or ParameterDataPrototypes in context of two different SenderReceiverInterfaces, NvDataInterfaces or ParameterInterfaces. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="VariableAndParameterInterfaceMapping" stereotype:atpObject

1042.name: VARIABLE-DATA-PROTOTYPE
1042.description:
note:A VariableDataPrototype is used to contain values in an ECU application. This means that most likely a VariableDataPrototype allocates "static" memory on the  ECU. In some cases optimization strategies might lead to a situation where the  memory allocation can be avoided.

In particular, the value of a VariableDataPrototype is likely to change as the ECU on which it is used executes. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="VariableDataPrototype" stereotype:atpObject

1043.name: VARIABLE-DATA-PROTOTYPE-IN-COMPOSITION-INSTANCE-REF
1043.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to define an InstanceRef to a VariableDataPrototype in the context of a CompositionSwComponentType. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="VariableDataPrototypeInCompositionInstanceRef" stereotype:atpObject,instanceRef

1047.name: VARIATION-POINT
1047.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to express a "structural variation point". The container of the variation point is part of the selected variant if swSyscond evaluates to true and each postBuildVariantCriterion is fulfilled. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="VariationPoint" stereotype:atpObject

1048.name: VARIATION-POINT-PROXY
1048.description: note:The VariationPointProxy represents variation points of the C/C++ implementation. In case of bindingTime = compileTime the RTE provides defines which can be used for Pre Processor directives to implement compileTime variability. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="VariationPointProxy" stereotype:atpObject

1049.name: VERBATIM-STRING
1049.description: note:This primitive represents a string in which white-space needs to be preserved. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="VerbatimString";xml.xsd.customType="VERBATIM-STRING";xml.xsd.type="string";xml.xsd.whiteSpace="preserve" stereotype:atpObject,primitive

1050.name: VFB-TIMING

TimingDescriptions aggregated by VfbTiming are restricted to event chains referring to events which are derived from the class TDEventVfb. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="TimingExtensions";mmt.qualifiedName="VfbTiming" stereotype:atpObject

1051.name: VIEW-MAP
1051.description:

This mapping allows to trace transformations of artifacts within the AUTOSAR environment. The references to the mapped elements can be plain references and/or InstanceRefs. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="ViewMap" stereotype:atpObject

1052.name: VIEW-MAP-SET
1052.description: note:Collection of ViewMaps that are used to establish relationships between different AUTOSAR artifacts. tag:atp.recommendedPackage="ViewMapSets";mmt.qualifiedName="ViewMapSet" stereotype:atpObject

1054.name: VLAN-MEMBERSHIP
1054.description: note:Static logical channel or VLAN binding to a switch-port. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="VlanMembership" stereotype:atpObject

1055.name: WAIT-POINT

1056.name: WARNING-INDICATOR-REQUESTED-BIT-NEEDS
1056.description: note:This meta-class represents the ability to explicitly request the existence of the WarningIndicatorRequestedBit. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="WarningIndicatorRequestedBitNeeds" stereotype:atpObject

1058.name: WORST-CASE-STACK-USAGE
1058.description: note:Provides a formal worst case stack usage. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="WorstCaseStackUsage" stereotype:atpObject

1059.name: XCP-PDU
1059.description:

note:A datatype representing a timestamp. The smallest granularity is 1 second.

This datatype represents a timestamp in the format yyyy-mm-dd followed by an optional time. The lead-in character for the time is "T" and the format is hh:mm:ss. 2009-07-23

1140.name: DISPLAY-FORMAT-STRING
1140.description:
note:This is a display format specifier for the display of values  e.g. in documents or in measurement and calibration systems. 

The display format specifier is a subset of the ANSI C printf specifiers with the following
form:

  % [flags] [width] [.prec] type character 

For more details refer to "ASAM-HarmonizedDataObjects-V1.1.pdf" chapter 13.3.2 DISPLAY OF DATA. 

Due to the numerical nature of value settings, only the following type characters are allowed:

* d:  Signed decimal integer 
* i:  Signed decimal integer 
* o:  Unsigned octal integer 
* u:  Unsigned decimal integer 
* x:  Unsigned hexadecimal integer, using "abcdef" 
* X:  Unsigned hexadecimal integer, using "ABCDEF" 
* e:  Signed value having the form [-]d.dddd e [sign]ddd where d is a single decimal digit, dddd is one or more decimal digits, ddd is exactly three decimal digits, and sign is + or - 
* E:  Identical to the e format except that E rather than e introduces the exponent 
* f:  Signed value having the form [-]dddd.dddd, where dddd is one or more decimal digits; the number of digits before the decimal point depends on the magnitude of the number, and the number of digits after the decimal point depends on the requested precision 
* g:  Signed value printed in f or e format, whichever is more compact for the given value and precision; trailing zeros are truncated, and the decimal point appears only if one or more digits follow it 
* G:  Identical to the g format, except that E, rather than e, introduces the exponent (where appropriate) tag:mmt.qualifiedName="DisplayFormatString";xml.xsd.customType="DISPLAY-FORMAT-STRING";xml.xsd.pattern="%[ \-+#]?[0-9]*(\.[0-9])?[diouxXfeEgGcs]";xml.xsd.type="string" stereotype:primitive

1200.name: MCD-IDENTIFIER
1200.description:
note:This primitive denotes a name used for measurement and calibration systems and shall follow the restrictions for an ASAM ASAP2 ident. For detailed syntax see the xsd.pattern. The size limitations are not captured. 

McdIdentifiers are random names which may contain characters A through Z, a through z, underscore (_), numerals 0 through 9, points (‘.’) and brackets ( ‘[‘,’]’ ).
However, the following limitations apply: the first character must be a letter or an underscore, brackets must occur in pairs at the end of a partial string and must
contain a number or an alpha-numerical string (description of the index of an array element). tag:mmt.qualifiedName="McdIdentifier";xml.xsd.customType="MCD-IDENTIFIER";xml.xsd.pattern="[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(\[([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*|[0-9]+)\])*(\.[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(\[([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*|[0-9]+)\])*)*";xml.xsd.type="string" stereotype:primitive

1201.name: MEMORY-ALLOCATION-KEYWORD-POLICY-TYPE

1211.name: NETWORK-TARGET-ADDRESS-TYPE

1213.name: NOTE-TYPE-ENUM

1214.name: NUMERICAL-VALUE

note:This primitive specifies a numerical value. It can be denoted in different formats such as Decimal, Octal, Hexadecimal, Float. See the xsd pattern for details.

The value can be expressed in octal, hexadecimal, binary representation. Negative numbers can only be expressed in decimal or float notation. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="Numerical";xml.xsd.customType="NUMERICAL-VALUE";xml.xsd.pattern="(0x[0-9a-f]+)|(0[0-7]+)|(0b[0-1]+)|(([+\-]?[1-9][0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?|[+\-]?[0-9](\.[0-9]+)?)(E([+\-]?)[0-9]+)?)|\.0|INF|-INF|NaN";xml.xsd.type="string" stereotype:primitive

1225.name: PRIMITIVE-IDENTIFIER

Please note that this meta-class has only been introduced to fix an issue with the generation of attributes on primitives in context with [TR_APRXML_00024]. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="PrimitiveIdentifier";xml.xsd.customType="PRIMITIVE-IDENTIFIER";xml.xsd.maxLength="128";xml.xsd.pattern="[a-zA-Z]([a-zA-Z0-9]|_[a-zA-Z0-9])*_?";xml.xsd.type="string" stereotype:primitive

Legal patterns are for example:

4.0.0
4.0.0.1234565
4.0.0_vendor specific;13
4.0.0;12 tag:mmt.qualifiedName="RevisionLabelString";xml.xsd.customType="REVISION-LABEL-STRING";xml.xsd.pattern="[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([\._;].*)?";xml.xsd.type="string" stereotype:primitive

1245.name: SECTION-INITIALIZATION-POLICY-TYPE
1245.description:
note:SectionInitializationPolicyType describes the intended initialization of MemorySections. 
The following values are standardized in AUTOSAR Methodology:

* '''NO-INIT''': No initialization and no clearing is performed. Such data elements shall not be read before one has written a value into it.
* '''INIT''': To be used for data that are initialized by every reset to the specified value (initValue). 
* '''POWER-ON-INIT''': To be used for data that are initialized by "Power On" to the specified value (initValue). Note: there might be several resets between power on resets. 
* '''CLEARED''': To be used for data that are initialized by every reset to zero. 
* '''POWER-ON-CLEARED''': To be used for data that are initialized by "Power On" to zero. Note: there might be several resets between power on resets.

Please note that the values are defined similar to the representation of enumeration types in the XML schema to ensure backward compatibility. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="SectionInitializationPolicyType";xml.xsd.customType="SECTION-INITIALIZATION-POLICY-TYPE";xml.xsd.type="NMTOKEN" stereotype:primitive

1290.name: UNLIMITED-INTEGER
1290.description:
note:An instance of UnlimitedInteger is an element in the set of integer numbers ( ..., -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ...). 

The range is limited by constraint 2534.

The value can be expressed in decimal, octal, hexadecimal and binary representation. Negative numbers can only be expressed in decimal notation. tag:mmt.qualifiedName="UnlimitedInteger";xml.xsd.customType="UNLIMITED-INTEGER";xml.xsd.pattern="[+\-]?[1-9][0-9]*|0x[0-9a-f]+|0[0-7]*|0b[0-1]+";xml.xsd.type="string" stereotype:primitive
